1.165.d: कया शुभा सवयसः सनीळाः समान्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः | कया मती कुत एतास एते.अर्चन्ति शुष्मं वर्षणो वसूया ||
1.165.e: WITH what bright beauty are the Maruts jointly invested, peers in age, who dwell together?  From what place have they come? With what intention? Sing they their strength through love of wealth, these Heroes?

1.165.d: कस्य बरह्माणि जुजुषुर्युवानः को अध्वरे मरुत आ ववर्त | शयेनानिव धरजतो अन्तरिक्षे केन महा मनसा रीरमाम ||
1.165.e: Whose prayers have they, the Youthful Ones, accepted? Who to his sacrifice hath turned the Maruts?  We will delay them on their journey sweeping—with what high spirit!—through the air like eagles.

1.165.d: कुतस्त्वमिन्द्र माहिनः सन्नेको यासि सत्पते किं त इत्था | सं पर्छसे समराणः शुभानैर्वोचेस्तन नो हरिवो यत्ते अस्मे ||
1.165.e: Whence comest thou alone, thou who art mighty, Indra, Lord of the Brave? What is thy purpose?  Thou greetest us when meeting us the Bright Ones. Lord of Bay Steeds, say what thou hast against us.

1.165.d: बरह्माणि मे मतयः शं सुतासः शुष्म इयर्ति परभ्र्तो मे अद्रिः | आ शासते परति हर्यन्त्युक्थेमा हरी वहतस्ता नो अछ ||
1.165.e: Mine are devotions, hymns; sweet are libations. Strength stirs, and hurled forth is my bolt of thunder.  They call for me, their lauds are longing for me. These my Bay Steeds bear me to these oblations.

1.165.d: अतो वयमन्तमेभिर्युजानाः सवक्षत्रेभिस्तन्वः शुम्भमानाः | महोभिरेतानुप युज्महे नविन्द्र सवधामनु हि नो बभूथ ||
1.165.e: Therefore together with our strong companions, having adorned our bodies, now we harness,  Our spotted deer with might, for thou, O Indra, hast learnt and understood our Godlike nature.

1.165.d: कव सया वो मरुतः सवधासीद यन मामेकं समधत्ताहिहत्ये | अहं हयूग्रस्तविषस्तुविष्मान विश्वस्य शत्रोरनमं वधस्नैः ||
1.165.e: Where was that nature then of yours, O Maruts, that ye charged me alone to slay the Dragon?  For I in truth am fierce and strong and mighty. I bent away from every foeman's weapons.

1.165.d: भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्व्र्षभ पौंस्येभिः | भूरीणि हि कर्णवामा शविष्ठेन्द्र करत्वा मरुतो यद्वशाम ||
1.165.e: Yea, much hast thou achieved with us for comrades, with manly valour like thine own, thou Hero.  Much may we too achieve, O mightiest Indra, with our great power, we Maruts, when we will it.

1.165.d: वधीं वर्त्रं मरुत इन्द्रियेण सवेन भामेन तविषो बभूवान | अहमेता मनवे विश्वश्चन्द्राः सुगा अपश्चकर वज्रबाहुः ||
1.165.e: Vṛtra I slew by mine own strength, O Maruts, having waxed mighty in mine indignation.  I with the thunder in my hand created for man these lucid softly flowing waters.

1.165.d: अनुत्तमा ते मघवन नकिर्नु न तवावानस्ति देवता विदानः | न जायमानो नशते न जातो यानि करिष्या कर्णुहिप्रव्र्द्ध ||
1.165.e: Nothing, O Maghavan, stands firm before thee; among the Gods not one is found thine equal.  None born or springing into life comes nigh thee. Do what thou hast to do, exceeding mighty?

1.165.d: एकस्य चिन मे विभ्वस्त्वोजो या नु दध्र्ष्वान कर्णवै मनीषा | अहं हयूग्रो मरुतो विदानो यानि चयवमिन्द्र इदीश एषाम ||
1.165.e: Mine only be transcendent power, whatever I, daring in my spirit, may accomplish.  For I am known as terrible, O Maruts I, Indra, am the Lord of what I ruined.

1.165.d: अमन्दन मा मरुत सतोमो अत्र यन मे नरः शरुत्यं बरह्म चक्र | इन्द्राय वर्ष्णे सुमखाय मह्यं सख्ये सखायस्तन्वेतनूभिः ||
1.165.e: Now, O ye Maruts, hath your praise rejoiced me, the glorious hymn which ye have made me, Heroes!  For me, for Indra, champion strong in battle, for me, yourselves, as lovers for a lover.

1.165.d: एवेदेते परति मा रोचमाना अनेद्यः शरव एषो दधानाः | संचक्ष्या मरुतश्चन्द्रवर्णा अछान्त मे छदयाथा चनूनम ||
1.165.e: Here, truly, they send forth their sheen to meet me, wearing their blameless glory and their vigour.  When I have seen you, Maruts, in gay splendour, ye have delighted me, so now delight me.

1.165.d: को नवत्र मरुतो मामहे वः पर यातन सखीन्रछा सखायः | मन्मानि चित्रा अपिवातयन्त एषां भूत नवेदा म रतानाम ||
1.165.e: Who here hath magnified you, O ye Maruts? speed forward, O ye lovers, to your lovers.  Ye Radiant Ones, assisting their devotions, of these my holy rites he ye regardful.

1.165.d: आ यद दुवस्याद दुवसे न कारुरस्माञ्चक्रे मान्यस्य मेधा | ओ षु वर्त्त मरुतो विप्रमछेमा बरह्माणि जरिता वोर्चत ||
1.165.e: To this hath Mānya's wisdom brought us, so as to aid, as aids the poet him who worships.  Bring hither quick! On to the sage, ye Maruts! These prayers for you the singer hath recited.

1.165.d: एष व सतोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मान्दार्यस्य मान्यस्य करोः | एषा यासीष्ट तन्वे वयां विद्यामेषं वर्जनं जीरदानुम ||
1.165.e: May this your praise, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya,  Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance!

1.166.d: तन नु वोचाम रभसाय जन्मने पूर्वं महित्वं वर्षभस्यकेतवे | ऐधेव यामन मरुतस्तुविष्वणो युधेव शक्रास्तविषाणि कर्तन ||
1.166.e: Now let us publish, for the vigorous company the herald of the Strong One, their primeval might.  With fire upon your way, O Maruts loud of voice, with battle, Mighty Ones, achieve your deeds of strength.

1.166.d: नित्यं न सूनुं मधु बिभ्रत उप करीळन्ति करीळा विदथेषु घर्ष्वयः | नक्षन्ति रुद्रा अवसा नमस्विनं न मर्धन्ति सवतवसो हविष्क्र्तम ||
1.166.e: Bringing the pleasant meath as ’twere their own dear son, they sport in sportive wise gay at their gatherings.  The Rudras come with succour to the worshipper; self-strong they fail not him who offers sacrifice.

1.166.d: यस्मा ऊमासो अम्र्ता अरासत रायस पोषं च हविषा ददाशुषे | उक्षन्त्यस्मै मरुतो हिता इव पुरू रजांसि पयसा मयोभुवः ||
1.166.e: To whomsoever, bringer of oblations, they immortal guardians, have given plenteous wealth,  For him, like loving friends, the Maruts bringing bliss bedew the regions round with milk abundantly.

1.166.d: आ ये रजांसि तविषीभिरव्यत पर व एवासः सवयतासोध्रजन | भयन्ते विश्वा भुवनानि हर्म्या चित्रो वो यामःप्रयतास्व रष्टिषु ||
1.166.e: Ye who with mighty powers have stirred the regions up, your coursers have sped forth directed by themselves.  All creatures of the earth, all dwellings are afraid, for brilliant is your coming with your spears advanced.

1.166.d: यत तवेषयामा नदयन्त पर्वतान दिवो वा पर्ष्ठं नर्याचुच्यवुः | विश्वो वो अज्मन भयते वनस्पती रथीयन्तीवप्र जिहीत ओषधिः ||
1.166.e: When they in dazzling rush have made the mountains roar, and shaken heaven's high back in their heroic strength,  Each sovran of the forest fears as ye drive near, aid the shrubs fly before you swift as whirling wheels.

1.166.d: यूयं न उग्रा मरुतः सुचेतुनारिष्टग्रामाः सुमतिं पिपर्तन | यत्रा वो दिद्युद रदति करिविर्दती रिणाति पश्वः सुधितेव बर्हणा ||
1.166.e: Terrible Maruts, ye with ne’er-diminished host, with great benevolence fulfil our heart's desire.  Where’er your lightning bites armed with its gory teeth it crunches up the cattle like a well-aimed dart.

1.166.d: पर सकम्भदेष्णा अनवभ्रराधसो.अलात्र्णासो विदथेषु सुष्टुताः | अर्चन्त्यर्कं मदिरस्य पीतये विदुर्वीरस्य परथमानि पौंस्या ||
1.166.e: Givers of during gifts whose bounties never fail, free from ill-will, at sacrifices glorified,  They sing their song aloud that they may drink sweet juice: well do they know the Hero's first heroic deeds.

1.166.d: शतभुजिभिस्तमभिह्रुतेरघात पूर्भी रक्षता मरुतो यमावत | जनं यमुग्रास्तवसो विरप्शिनः पाथना शंसात तनयस्य पुष्टिषु ||
1.166.e: With castles hundredfold, O Maruts, guard ye well the man whom ye have loved from ruin and from sin,—  The man whom ye the fierce, the Mighty ones who roar, preserve from calumny by cherishing his seed.

1.166.d: विश्वानि भद्रा मरुतो रथेषु वो मिथस्प्र्ध्येव तविषाण्याहिता | अंसेष्वा वः परपथेषु खादयो.अक्षो वश्चक्रा समया वि वाव्र्ते ||
1.166.e: O Maruts, in your cars are all things that are good: great powers are set as ’twere in rivalry therein.  Rings are upon your shoulders when ye journey forth: your axle turns together both the chariot wheels.

1.166.d: भूरीणि भद्रा नर्येषु बाहुषु वक्षस्सु रुक्मा रभसासो अञ्जयः | अंसेष्वेताः पविषु कषुरा अधि वयो न पक्षान वयनु शरियो धिरे ||
1.166.e: Held in your manly arms are many goodly things, gold chains are on your chests, and glistering ornaments,  Deer-skins are on their shoulders, on their fellies knives: they spread their glory out as birds spread out their wings.

1.166.d: महान्तो मह्ना विभ्वो विभूतयो दूरेद्र्शो ये दिव्या इव सत्र्भिः | मन्द्राः सुजिह्वाः सवरितार आसभिः सम्मिश्ला इन्द्रे मरुतः परिष्टुभः ||
1.166.e: Mighty in mightiness, pervading, passing strong, visible from afar as ’twere with stars of heaven,  Lovely with pleasant tongues, sweet singers with their mouths, the Maruts, joined with Indra, shout forth all around.

1.166.d: तद वः सुजाता मरुतो महित्वनं दीर्घं वो दात्रमदितेरिव वरतम | इन्द्रश्चन तयजसा वि हरुणाति तज्जनाय यस्मै सुक्र्ते अराध्वम ||
1.166.e: This is your majesty, ye Maruts nobly born, far as the sway of Aditi your bounty spreads.  Even Indra by desertion never disannuls the boon bestowed by you upon the pious man.

1.166.d: तद वो जामित्वं मरुतः परे युगे पुरू यच्छंसमम्र्तासावत | अया धिया मनवे शरुष्टिमाव्या साकं नरो दंसनैरा चिकित्रिरे ||
1.166.e: This is your kinship, Maruts, that, Immortals, ye were oft in olden time regardful of our call,  Having vouchsafed to man a hearing through this prayer, by wondrous deeds the Heroes have displayed their might.

1.166.d: येन दीर्घं मरुतः शूशवाम युष्माकेन परीणसा तुरासः | आ यत ततनन वर्जने जनास एभिर्यज्ञेभिस्तदभीष्टिमश्याम ||
1.166.e: That, O ye Maruts, we may long time flourish through your abundant riches, O swift movers,  And that our men may spread in the encampment, let me complete the rite with these oblations.
May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya,  Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.167.d: सहस्रं त इन्द्रोतयो नः सहस्रमिषो हरिवो गूर्ततमाः | सहस्रं रायो मादयध्यै सहस्रिण उप नो यन्तु वाजाः ||
1.167.e: A THOUSAND are thy helps for us, O Indra: a thousand, Lord of Bays, thy choice refreshments.  Wealth of a thousand sorts hast thou to cheer us: may precious goods come nigh to us in thousands.

1.167.d: आ नो.अवोभिर्मरुतो यान्त्वछा जयेष्ठेभिर्वा बर्हद्दिवैःसुमायाः | अध यदेषां नियुतः परमाः समुद्रस्य चिद्धनयन्त पारे ||
1.167.e: May the most sapient Maruts, with protection, with best boons brought from lofty heaven, approach us,  Now when their team of the most noble horses speeds even on the sea's extremest limit.

1.167.d: मिम्यक्ष येषु सुधिता घर्ताची हिरण्यनिर्णिगुपरा न रष्टिः | गुहा चरन्ती मनुषो न योषा सभावती विदथ्येव सं वाक ||
1.167.e: Close to them clings one moving in seclusion, like a man's wife, like a spear carried rearward,  Well grasped, bright, decked with gold there is Vāk also, like to a courtly, eloquent dame, among them.

1.167.d: परा शुभ्रा अयासो यव्या साधारण्येव मरुतो मिमिक्षुः | न रोदसी अप नुदन्त घोरा जुषन्त वर्धं सख्याय देवाः ||
1.167.e: Far off the brilliant, never-weary Maruts cling to the young Maid as a joint possession.  The fierce Gods drave not Rodasī before them, but wished for her to grow their friend and fellow.

1.167.d: जोषद यदीमसुर्या सचध्यै विषितस्तुका रोदसी नर्मणाः | आ सूर्येव विधतो रथं गात तवेषप्रतीका नभसो नेत्या ||
1.167.e: When chose immortal Rodasī to follow—she with loose tresses and heroic spirit—  She climbed her servant's chariot, she like Sūrya with cloud-like motion and refulgent aspect.

1.167.d: आस्थापयन्त युवतिं युवानः शुभे निमिष्लां विदथेषुपज्राम | अर्को यद वो मरुतो हविष्मान गायद गाथं सुतसोमो दुवस्यन ||
1.167.e: Upon their car the young men set the Maiden wedded to glory, mighty in assemblies,  When your song, Maruts, rose, and, with oblation, the Soma-pourer sang his hymn in worship.

1.167.d: परतं विवक्मि वक्म्यो य एषां मरुतां महिमा सत्यो अस्ति | सचा यदीं वर्षमणा अहंयु सथिरा चिज्जनीर्वहते सुभागाः ||
1.167.e: I will declare the greatness of these Maruts, their real greatness, worthy to be lauded,  How, with them, she though firm, strong-minded, haughty, travels to women happy in their fortune.

1.167.d: पान्ति मित्रावरुणाववद्याच्चयत ईमर्यमो अप्रशस्तान | उत चयवन्ते अच्युता धरुवाणि वाव्र्ध ईं मरुतो दातिवारः ||
1.167.e: Mitra and Varuṇa they guard from censure: Aryaman too, discovers worthless sinners Firm things are overthrown that ne’er were shaken: he prospers, Maruts, who gives choice oblations.

1.167.d: नही नु वो मरुतो अन्त्यस्मे आरात्ताच्चिच्छवसो अन्तमापुः | ते धर्ष्णुना शवसा शूशुवांसो.अर्णो न दवेषो धर्षता परि षठुः ||
1.167.e: None of us, Maruts, near or at a distance, hath ever reached the limit of your vigour.  They in courageous might still waxing boldly have compassed round their foemen like an ocean.

1.167.d: वयमद्येन्द्रस्य परेष्ठा वयं शवो वोचेमहि समर्ये | वयं पुरा महि च नो अनु दयून तन न रभुक्षा नरामनु षयात ||
1.167.e: May we this day be dearest friends of Indra, and let us call on him in fight to-morrow.  So were we erst. New might attend us daily! So be with us! Ṛbhukṣan of the Heroes!
May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya,  Bring offspring for ourselves with. food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.168.d: यज्ञा-यज्ञा वः समना तुतुर्वणिर्धियं-धियं वो देवया उ दधिध्वे | आ वो.अर्वाचः सुविताय रोदस्योर्महे वव्र्त्यामवसे सुव्र्क्तिभिः ||
1.168.e: SWIFT gain is his who hath you near at every rite: ye welcome every song of him who serves the Gods.  So may I turn you hither with fair hymns of praise to give great succour for the weal of both the worlds.

1.168.d: वव्रासो न ये सवजाः सवतवस इषं सवरभिजायन्त धूतयः | सहस्रियासो अपां नोर्मय आसा गावो वन्द्यासो नोक्षणः ||
1.168.e: Surrounding, as it were, self-born, self-powerful, they spring to life the shakers-down of food and light;  Like as the countess undulations of the floods, worthy of praise when near, like bullocks and like kine.

1.168.d: सोमासो न ये सुतास्त्र्प्तांशवो हर्त्सु पीतासो दुवसो नासते | ऐषामंसेषु रम्भिणीव रारभे हस्तेषु खादिश्चक्र्तिश्च सं दधे ||
1.168.e: They who, like Somas with their well-grown stalks pressed out, imbibed within the heart, dwell there in friendly wise.  Upon their shoulders rests as ’twere a warrior's spear and in their hand they hold a dagger and a ring.

1.168.d: अव सवयुक्ता दिव आ वर्था ययुरमर्त्याः कशया चोदत तमना | अरेणवस्तुविजाता अचुच्यवुर्द्र्ळ्हानि चिन मरुतो भराजद्र्ष्टयः ||
1.168.e: Self-yoked they have descended lightly from the sky. With your own lash, Immortals, urge yourselves to speed.  Unstained by dust the Maruts, mighty in their strength, have cast down e’en firm things, armed with their shining spears.

1.168.d: को वो.अन्तर्मरुत रष्टिविद्युतो रेजति तमना हन्वेव जिह्वया | धन्वच्युत इषां न यामनि पुरुप्रैषा अहन्यो नैतशः ||
1.168.e: Who among you, O Maruts armed with lightning-spears, moveth you by himself, as with the tongue his jaws?  Ye rush from heaven's floor as though ye sought for food, on many errands like the Sun's diurnal Steed.

1.168.d: कव सविदस्य रजसो महस परं कवावरं मरुतो यस्मिन्नायय | यच्च्यावयथ विथुरेव संहितं वयद्रिणा पतथ तवेषमर्णवम ||
1.168.e: Say where, then, is this mighty region's farthest bound, where, Maruts, is the lowest depth that ye have reached,  When ye cast down like chaff the firmly stablished pile, and from the mountain send the glittering water-flood?

1.168.d: सातिर्न वो.अमवती सवर्वती तवेषा विपाका मरुतः पिपिष्वती | भद्रा वो रातिः पर्णतो न दक्षिणा पर्थुज्रयी असुर्येव जञ्जती ||
1.168.e: Your winning is with strength, dazzling, with heavenly light, with fruit mature, O Maruts, fall of plenteousness.  Auspicious is your gift like a free giver's meed, victorious, spreading far, as of immortal Gods.

1.168.d: परति षटोभन्ति सिन्धवः पविभ्यो यदभ्रियां वाचमुदीरयन्ति | अव समयन्त विद्युतः पर्थिव्यां यदी घर्तं मरुतः परुष्णुवन्ति ||
1.168.e: The rivers roar before your chariot fellies when they are uttering the voice of rain-clouds.  The lightnings laugh upon the earth beneath them, what time the Maruts scatter forth their fatness.

1.168.d: असूत पर्श्निर्महते रणाय तवेषमयासां मरुतामनीकम | ते सप्सरासो.अजनयन्ताभ्वमादित सवधामिषिरां पर्यपश्यन ||
1.168.e: Pṛśni brought forth, to fight the mighty battle, the glittering army of the restless Maruts.  Nurtured together they begat the monster, and then looked round them for the food that strengthens.
May this your laud, may this your song O Maruts, sung by the poet Māna's son, Māndārya,  Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.169.d: महश्चित तवमिन्द्र यत एतान महश्चिदसि तयजसो वरूता | स नो वेधो मरुतां चिकित्वान सुम्ना वनुष्व तव हि परेष्ठा ||
1.169.e: As, Indra, from great treason thou protectest, yea, from great treachery these who approach us,  So, marking well, Controller of the Maruts grant us their blessings, for they are thy dearest.

1.169.d: अयुज्रन त इन्द्र विश्वक्र्ष्टीर्विदानासो निष्षिधो मर्त्यत्रा | मरुतां पर्त्सुतिर्हासमाना सवर्मीळ्हस्य परधनस्य सातौ ||
1.169.e: The various doings of all mortal people by thee are ordered, in thy wisdom, Indra.  The host of Maruts goeth forth exulting to win the light-bestowing spoil of battle.

1.169.d: अम्यक सा त इन्द्र रष्टिरस्मे सनेम्यभ्वं मरुतो जुनन्ति | अग्निश्चिद धि षमातसे शुशुक्वानापो न दवीपं दधतिप्रयांसि ||
1.169.e: That spear of thine sat firm for us, O Indra: the Maruts set their whole dread power in motion.  E’en Agni shines resplendent in the brush-wood: the viands hold him as floods hold an island.

1.169.d: तवं तू न इन्द्र तं रयिं दा ओजिष्ठया दक्षिणयेव रातिम | सतुतश्च यास्ते चकनन्त वायो सतनं न मध्वःपीपयन्त वाजैः ||
1.169.e: Vouchsafe us now that opulence, O Indra, as guerdon won by mightiest donation.  May hymns that please thee cause the breast of Vāyu to swell as with the mead's refreshing sweetness.

1.169.d: तवे राय इन्द्र तोशतमाः परणेतारः कस्य चिद रतायोः | ते षु णो मरुतो मर्ळयन्तु ये समा पुरा गातूयन्तीव देवाः ||
1.169.e: With thee, O Indra, are most bounteous riches that further every one who lives uprightly.  Now may these Maruts show us loving-kindness, Gods who of old were ever prompt to help us.

1.169.d: परति पर याहीन्द्र मीळ्हुषो नॄन महः पार्थिवे सदने यतस्व | अध यदेषां पर्थुबुध्नास एतास्तीर्थे नार्यः पौंस्यानि तस्थुः ||
1.169.e: Bring forth the Men who rain down boons, O Indra: exert thee in the great terrestrial region;  For their broad-chested speckled deer are standing like a King's armies on the field of battle.

1.169.d: परति घोराणामेतानामयासां मरुतां शर्ण्व आयतामुपब्दिः | ये मर्त्यं पर्तनायन्तमूमैर्र्णावानं न पतयन्त सर्गैः ||
1.169.e: Heard is the roar of the advancing Maruts, terrific, glittering, and swiftly moving,  Who with their rush o’erthrow as ’twere a sinner the mortal who would fight with those who love him

1.169.d: तवं मानेभ्य इन्द्र विश्वजन्या रदा मरुद्भिः शुरुधो गोग्राः | सतवानेभि सतवसे देव देवैर्विद्यामेषं वर्जनं जीरदानुम ||
1.169.e: Give to the Mānas, Indra with Maruts, gifts universal, gifts of cattle foremost.  Thou, God, art praised with Gods who must be lauded. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.170.d: न नूनमस्ति नो शवः कस्तद वेद यदद्भुतम | अन्यस्यचित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं वि नश्यति ||
1.170.e: NAUGHT is to-day, to-morrow naught. Who comprehends the mystery?  We must address ourselves unto another's thought, and lost is then the hope we formed.

1.170.d: किं न इन्द्र जिघांससि भरातरो मरुतस्तव | तेभिः कल्पस्व साधुया मा नः समरणे वधीः ||
1.170.e: The Maruts are thy brothers. Why, O Indra, wouldst thou take our lives?  Agree with them in friendly wise, and do not slay us in the fight.

1.170.d: किं नो भरातरगस्त्य सखा सन्नति मन्यसे | विद्मा हि तेयथा मनो.अस्मभ्यमिन न दित्ससि ||
1.170.e: Agastya, brother, why dost thou neglect us, thou who art our friend?  We know the nature of thy mind. Verity thou wilt give us naught.

1.170.d: अरं कर्ण्वन्तु वेदिं समग्निमिन्धतां पुरः | तत्राम्र्तस्य चेतनं यज्ञं ते तनवावहै ||
1.170.e: Let them prepare the altar, let them kindle fire in front: we two  Here will spread sacrifice for thee, that the Immortal may observe.

1.170.d: तवमीशिषे वसुपते वसूनां तवं मित्राणां मित्रपते धेष्ठः | इन्द्र तवं मरुद्भिः सं वदस्वाध पराशान रतुथा हवींषि ||
1.170.e: Thou, Lord of Wealth, art Master of all treasures, thou, Lord of friends, art thy friends' best supporter.  O Indra, speak thou kindly with the Maruts, and taste oblations in their proper season.

1.171.d: परति व एना नमसाहमेमि सूक्तेन भिक्षे सुमतिं तुराणाम | रराणता मरुतो वेद्याभिर्नि हेळो धत्त वि मुचध्वमश्वान ||
1.171.e: To you I come with this mine adoration, and with a hymn I crave the Strong Ones' favour  A hymn that truly makes you joyful, Maruts. Suppress your anger and unyoke your horses.

1.171.d: एष व सतोमो मरुतो नमस्वान हर्दा तष्टो मनसा धायि देवाः | उपेमा यात मनसा जुषाणा यूयं हि षठा नमस इद वर्धासः ||
1.171.e: Maruts, to you this laud with prayer and worship, formed in the mind and heart, ye Gods, is offered.  Come ye to us, rejoicing in your spirit, for ye are they who make our prayer effective.

1.171.d: सतुतासो नो मरुतो मर्ळयन्तूत सतुतो मघवा शमभविष्ठः | ऊर्ध्वा नः सन्तु कोम्या वनान्यहानि विश्वा मरुतो जिगीषा ||
1.171.e: The Maruts, praised by us, shall show us favour; Maghavan, lauded, shall be most propitious.  Maruts,, may all our days that are to follow be very pleasant, lovely and triumphant.

1.171.d: अस्मादहं तविषादीषमाण इन्द्राद भिया मरुतो रेजमानः | युष्मभ्यं हव्या निशितान्यासन तान्यारे चक्र्मा मर्ळत नः ||
1.171.e: I fled in  terror  from this mighty Indra, my body trembling in alarm, O Maruts.  Oblations meant for you had been made ready; these have we set aside: for this forgive us.

1.171.d: येन मानासश्चितयन्त उस्रा वयुष्टिषु शवसा शश्वतीनाम | स नो मरुद्भिर्व्र्षभ शरवो धा उग्र उग्रेभि सथविरः सहोदाः ||
1.171.e: By whom the Mānas recognize the day-springs, by whose strength at the dawn of endless mornings,  Give us, thou Mighty, glory with Maruts. fierce with the fierce, the Strong who givest triumph.

1.171.d: तवं पाहीन्द्र सहीयसो नॄन भवा मरुद्भिरवयातहेळाः | सुप्रकेतेभिः सासहिर्दधानो विद्यामेषं व. ज. ||
1.171.e: Do thou, O Indra, guard the conquering Heroes, and rid thee of thy wrath against the Maruts,  With them, the wise, victorious and bestowing. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.172.d: चित्रो वो.अस्तु यामश्चित्र ऊती सुदानवः | मरुतो अहिभानवः ||
1.172.e: WONDERFUL let your coming be, wondrous with help, ye Bounteous Ones,  Maruts, who gleam as serpents gleam.

1.172.d: आरे सा वः सुदानवो मरुत रञ्जती शरुः | आरे अश्मा यमस्यथ ||
1.172.e: Far be from us, O Maruts, ye free givers, your impetuous shaft;  Far from us be the stone ye hurl.

1.172.d: तर्णस्कन्दस्य नु विशः परि वर्ङकत सुदानवः | ऊर्ध्वान नः कर्त जीवसे ||
1.172.e: O Bounteous Givers, touch ye not, O Maruts, Tṛṇskanda's folk;  Lift ye us up that we may live.

1.173.d: गायत साम नभन्यं यथा वेरर्चाम तद वाव्र्धानं सवर्वत | गावो धेनवो बर्हिष्यदब्धा आ यत सद्मानं दिव्यं विवासान ||
1.173.e: THE praise-song let him sing forth bursting bird-like: sing we that hymn which like heaven's light expandeth,  That the milk-giving cows may, unimpeded call to the sacred grass the Gods’ assembly.

1.173.d: अर्चद वर्षा वर्षभिः सवेदुहव्यैर्म्र्गो नाश्नो अति यज्जुगुर्यात | पर मन्दयुर्मनां गूर्त होता भरते मर्यो मिथुना यजत्रः ||
1.173.e: Let the Bull sing with Bulls whose toil is worship, with a loud roar like some wild beast that hungers.  Praised God! the glad priest brings his heart's devotion; the holy youth presents twofold oblation.

1.173.d: नक्षद धोता परि सद्म मिता यन भरद गर्भमा शरदः पर्थिव्याः | करन्ददश्वो नयमानो रुवद गौरन्तर्दूतो न रोदसी चरद वाक ||
1.173.e: May the Priest come circling the measured stations, and with him bring the earth's autumnal fruitage.  Let the Horse neigh led near, let the Steer bellow: let the Voice go between both worlds as herald,

1.173.d: ता कर्माषतरास्मै पर चयौत्नानि देवयन्तो भरन्ते | जुजोषदिन्द्रो दस्मवर्चा नासत्येव सुग्म्यो रथेष्ठाः ||
1.173.e: To him we offer welcomest oblations, the pious bring their strength-inspiring praises.  May Indra, wondrous in his might, accept them, car-borne and swift to move like the Nāsatyas.

1.173.d: तमु षटुहीन्द्रं यो ह सत्वा यः शूरो मघवा यो रथेष्ठाः | परतीचश्चिद योधीयान वर्षण्वान ववव्रुषश्चित तमसो विहन्ता ||
1.173.e: Praise thou that Indra who is truly mighty, the car-borne Warrior, Maghavan the Hero;  Stronger in war than those who fight against him, borne by strong steeds, who kills enclosing darkness;

1.173.d: पर यदित्था महिना नर्भ्यो अस्त्यरं रोदसी कक्ष्ये नास्मै | सं विव्य इन्द्रो वर्जनं न भूमा भर्ति सवधावानोपशमिव दयाम ||
1.173.e: Him who surpasses heroes in his greatness: the earth and heavens suffice not for his girdles.  Indra endues the earth to be his garment, and, God-like, wears the heaven as ’twere a frontlet,

1.173.d: समत्सु तवा शूर सतामुराणं परपथिन्तमं परितंसयध्यै | सजोषस इन्द्रं मदे कषोणीः सूरिं चिद ये अनुमदन्ति वाजैः ||
1.173.e: Thee, Hero, guardian of the brave in battles, who roamest in the van,—to draw thee hither,  Indra, the hosts agree beside the Soma, and joy, for his great actions, in the Chieftain.

1.173.d: एवा हि ते शं सवना समुद्र आपो यत त आसु मदन्ति देवीः | विश्वा ते अनु जोष्या भूद गौः सूरींश्चिद यदि धिषा वेषि जनान ||
1.173.e: Libations in the sea to thee are pleasant, when thy divine Floods come to cheer these people.  To thee the Cow is sum of all things grateful when with the wish thou seekest men and princes.

1.173.d: असाम यथा सुषखाय एन सवभिष्टयो नरां न शंसैः | असद यथा न इन्द्रो वन्दनेष्ठास्तुरो न कर्म नयमान उक्था ||
1.173.e: So may we in this One be well befriended, well aided as it were through praise of chieftains,  That Indra still may linger at our worship, as one led swift to work, to hear our praises.

1.173.d: विष्पर्धसो नरां न शंसैरस्माकासदिन्द्रो वज्रहस्तः | मित्रायुवो न पूर्पतिं सुशिष्टौ मध्यायुव उप शिक्षन्ति यज्ञैः ||
1.173.e: Like men in rivalry extolling princes, our Friend be Indra, wielder of the thunder.  Like true friends of some city's lord within them held in good rule with sacrifice they help him.

1.173.d: यज्ञो हि षमेन्द्रं कश्चिद रन्धञ जुहुराणश्चिन मनसापरियन | तीर्थे नाछा तात्र्षाणमोको दीर्घो न सिध्रमा कर्णोत्यध्वा ||
1.173.e: For every sacrifice makes Indra stronger, yea, when he goes around angry in spirit;  As pleasure at the ford invites the thirsty, as the long way brings him who gains his object.

1.173.d: मो षू ण इन्द्रात्र पर्त्सु देवैरस्ति हि षमा ते शुष्मिन्नवयाः | महश्चिद यस्य मीळ्हुषो यव्या हविष्मतो मरुतोवन्दते गीः ||
1.173.e: Let us not here contend with Gods, O Indra, for here, O Mighty One, is thine own portion,  The Great, whose Friends the bounteous Maruts honour, as with a stream, his song who pours oblations.

1.173.d: एष सतोम इन्द्र तुभ्यमस्मे एतेन गातुं हरिवो विदो नः | आ नो वव्र्त्याः सुविताय देव विद्यामेषं व. ज. ||
1.173.e: Addressed to thee is this our praise, O Indra: Lord of Bay Steeds, find us hereby advancement.  So mayst thou lead us on, O God, to comfort. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.174.d: तवं राजेन्द्र ये च देवा रक्षा नॄन पाह्यसुर तवमस्मान | तवं सत्पतिर्मघवा नस्तरुत्रस्त्वं सत्यो वसवानः सहोदाः ||
1.174.e: THOU art the King of all the Gods, O Indra: protect the men, O Asura, preserve us.  Thou Lord of Heroes, Maghavan, our saver, art faithful, very rich, the victory-giver.

1.174.d: दनो विश इन्द्र मर्ध्रवाचः सप्त यत पुरः शर्म शारदीर्दर्त | रणोरपो अनवद्यार्णा यूने वर्त्रं पुरुकुत्साय रन्धीः ||
1.174.e: Indra, thou humbledst tribes that spake with insult by breaking down seven autumn forts, their refuge.  Thou stirredst, Blameless! billowy floods, and gavest his foe a prey to youthful Purukutsa.

1.174.d: अजा वर्त इन्द्र शूरपत्नीर्द्यां च येभिः पुरुहूत नूनम | रक्षो अग्निमशुषं तूर्वयाणं सिंहो न दमे अपांसि वस्तोः ||
1.174.e: With whom thou drivest troops whose lords are heroes, and bringest daylight now, much worshipped Indra,  With them guard lion-like wasting active Agni to dwell in our tilled fields and in our homestead.

1.174.d: शेषन नु त इन्द्र सस्मिन योनौ परशस्तये पवीरवस्य मह्ना | सर्जदर्णांस्यव यद युधा गास्तिष्ठद धरी धर्षता मर्ष्ट वाजान ||
1.174.e: They through the greatness of thy spear, O Indra, shall, to thy praise, rest in this earthly station.  To loose the floods, to seek, for kine, the battle, his Bays he mounted boldly seized the booty.

1.174.d: वह कुत्समिन्द्र यस्मिञ्चाकन सयूमन्यू रज्रा वातस्याश्वा | पर सूरश्चक्रं वर्हतादभीके.अभि सप्र्धो यासिषद्वज्रबाहुः ||
1.174.e: Indra, bear Kutsa, him in whom thou joyest: the dark-red horses of the Wind are docile.  Let the Sun roll his chariot wheel anear us, and let the Thunderer go to meet the foemen.

1.174.d: जघन्वानिन्द्र मित्रेरूञ्चोदप्रव्र्द्धो हरिवो अदाशून | परये पश्यन्नर्यमणं सचायोस्त्वया शूर्ता वहमाना अपत्यम ||
1.174.e: Thou Indra, Lord of Bays, made strong by impulse, hast slain the vexers of thy friends, who give not.  They who beheld the Friend beside the living were cast aside by thee as they rode onward.

1.174.d: रपत कविरिन्द्रार्कसातौ कषां दासायोपबर्हणीं कः | करत तिस्रो मघवा दानुचित्रा नि दुर्योणे कुयवाचं मर्धिश्रेत ||
1.174.e: Indra, the bard sang forth in inspiration: thou madest earth a covering for the Dāsa.  Maghavan made the three that gleam with moisture, and to his home brought Kuyavāc to slay him.

1.174.d: सना ता त इन्द्र नव्या आगुः सहो नभो.अविरणाय पूर्वीः | भिनत पुरो न भिदो अदेवीर्ननमो वधरदेवस्य पीयोः ||
1.174.e: These thine old deeds new bards have sung, O Indra. Thou conqueredst, boundest many tribes for ever.  Like castles thou hast crushed the godless races, and bowed the godless scorner's deadly weapon.

1.174.d: तवं धुनिरिन्द्र धुनिमतीर्र्णोरपः सीरा न सरवन्तीः | पर यत समुद्रमति शूर पर्षि पारया तुर्वशं यदुं सवस्ति ||
1.174.e: A Stormer thou hast made the stormy waters flow down, O Indra, like the running rivers.  When o’er the flood thou broughtest them, O Hero, thou keptest Turvaśa and Yadu safely.

1.174.d: तवमस्माकमिन्द्र विश्वध सय अव्र्कतमो नरां नर्पाता | स नो विश्वासां सप्र्धां सहोदा वि... ||
1.174.e: Indra, mayst thou be ours in all occasions, protector of the men, most gentle-hearted,  Giving us victory over all our rivals. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.175.d: मत्स्यपायि ते महः पात्रस्येव हरिवो मत्सरो मदः | वर्षा ते वर्ष्ण इन्दुर्वाजी सहस्रसातमः ||
1.175.e: GLAD thee: thy glory hath been quaffed, Lord of Bay Steeds, as ’twere the bowl's enlivening mead.  For thee the Strong there is strong drink, mighty, omnipotent to win.

1.175.d: आ नस्ते गन्तु मत्सरो वर्षा मदो वरेण्यः | सहावानिन्द्रसानसिः पर्तनाषाळ अमर्त्यः ||
1.175.e: Let our strong drink, most excellent, exhilarating, come to thee,  Victorious, Indra! bringing gain, immortal conquering in fight,

1.175.d: तवं हि शूरः सनिता चोदयो मनुषो रथम | सहावान दस्युमव्रतमोषः पात्रं न शोचिषा ||
1.175.e: Thou, Hero, winner of the spoil, urgest to speed the car of man.  Burn, like a vessel with the flame, the lawless Dasyu, Conqueror!

1.175.d: मुषाय सुर्यं कवे चक्रमीशान ओजसा | वह शुष्णायवधं कुत्सं वातस्याश्वैः ||
1.175.e: Empowered by thine own might, O Sage, thou stolest Sūrya's chariot wheel.  Thou barest Kutsa with the steeds of Wind to Śuṣṇa as his death.

1.175.d: शुष्मिन्तमो हि ते मदो दयुम्निन्तम उत करतुः | वर्त्रघ्ना वरिवोविदा मंसीष्ठा अश्वसातमः ||
1.175.e: Most mighty is thy rapturous joy, most splendid is thine active power,  Wherewith, foe-slaying, sending bliss, thou art supreme in gaining steeds.

1.175.d: यथा पुर्वेभ्यो जरित्र्भ्य इन्द्र मय इवापो न तर्ष्यते बभूथ | तामनु तवा निविदं जोहवीमि वि... ||
1.175.e: As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, as water to the thirsty,  So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.176.d: मत्सि नो वस्यैष्टय इन्द्रमिन्दो वर्षा विश | रघायमाणैन्वसि शत्रुमन्ति न विन्दसि ||
1.176.e: CHEER thee with draughts to win us bliss: Soma, pierce Indra in thy strength.  Thou stormest trembling in thy rage, and findest not a foeman nigh.

1.176.d: तस्मिन्ना वेशया गिरो य एकश्चर्षणीनाम | अनु सवधायमुप्यते यवं न चर्क्र्षद वर्षा ||
1.176.e: Make our songs penetrate to him who is the Only One of men;  For whom the sacred food is spread, as the steer ploughs the barley in.

1.176.d: यस्य विश्वानि हस्तयोः पञ्च कषितीनां वसु | सपाशयस्व यो अस्मध्रुग दिव्येवाशनिर्जहि ||
1.176.e: Within whose hands deposited all the Five Peoples’ treasures rest.  Mark thou the man who injures us and kill him like the heavenly bolt.

1.176.d: असुन्वन्तं समं जहि दूणाशं यो न ते मयः | अस्मभ्यमस्य वेदनं दद्धि सूरिश्चिदोहते ||
1.176.e: Slay everyone who pours no gift, who, hard to reach, delights thee not.  Bestow on us what wealth he hath: this even the worshipper awaits.

1.176.d: आवो यस्य दविबर्हसो.अर्केषु सानुषगसत | आजाविन्द्रस्येन्दो परावो वाजेषु वाजिनम ||
1.176.e: Thou helpest him the doubly strong whose hymns were sung unceasingly.  When Indra fought, O Soma, thou helpest the mighty in the fray.
As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, like water to the thirsty,  So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.177.d: आ चर्षणिप्रा वर्षभो जनानां राजा कर्ष्टीनां पुरुहूत इन्द्रः | सतुतः शरवस्यन्नवसोप मद्रिग युक्त्वा हरीव्र्षणा याह्यर्वां ||
1.177.e: THE Bull of men, who cherishes all people, King of the Races, Indra, called of many,  Fame-loving, praised, hither to me with succour turn having yoked both vigorous Bay Horses!

1.177.d: ये ते वर्षणो वर्षभास इन्द्र बरह्मयुजो वर्षरथासो अत्याः | ताना तिष्ठ तेभिरा याह्यर्वां हवामहे तवा सुत इन्द्र सोमे ||
1.177.e: Thy mighty Stallions, yoked by prayer, O Indra, thy. Coursers to thy mighty chariot harnessed,—  Ascend thou these, and borne by them come hither: with Soma juice outpoured, Indra, we call thee.

1.177.d: आ तिष्ठ रथं वर्षणं वर्षा ते सुतः सोमः परिषिक्ता मधूनि | युक्त्वा वर्षभ्यां वर्षभ कषितीनां हरिभ्यां याहि परवतोप मद्रिक ||
1.177.e: Ascend thy mighty car: the mighty Soma is poured for thee and sweets are sprinkled round us.  Come down to us-ward, Bull of human races, come, having harnessed them, with strong Bay Horses.

1.177.d: अयं यज्ञो देवया अयं मियेध इमा बरह्मण्ययमिन्द्र सोमः | सतीर्णं बर्हिरा तु शक्र पर याहि पिबा निषद्यवि मुचा हरी इह ||
1.177.e: Here is God-reaching sacrifice, here the victim; here, Indra, are the prayers, here is the Soma.  Strewn is the sacred grass: come hither, Śakra; seat thee and drink: unyoke thy two Bay Coursers.

1.177.d: ओ सुष्टुत इन्द्र याह्यर्वां उप बरह्माणि मान्यस्य कारोः | विद्याम वस्तोरवसा गर्णन्तो वि... ||
1.177.e: Come to us, Indra, come thou highly lauded to the devotions of the singer Māna.  Singing, may we find early through thy succour, may we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.178.d: यद ध सया त इन्द्र शरुष्टिरस्ति यया बभूथ जरित्र्भ्य ऊती | मा नः कामं महयन्तमा धग विश्वा ते अश्याम्पर्याप आयोः ||
1.178.e: IF, Indra, thou hast given that gracious hearing where with thou helpest those who sang thy praises.  Blast not the wish that would exalt us may I gain all from thee, and pay all man's devotions.

1.178.d: न घा राजेन्द्र आ दभन नो या नु सवसारा कर्णवन्त योनौ | आपश्चिदस्मै सुतुका अवेषन गमन न इन्द्रः सख्या वयश्च ||
1.178.e: Let not the Sovran Indra disappoint us in what shall bring both Sisters to our dwelling.  To him have run the quickly flowing waters. May Indra come to us with life and friendship.

1.178.d: जेता नर्भिरिन्द्रः पर्त्सु शूरः शरोता हवं नाधमानस्य कारोः | परभर्ता रथं दाशुष उपक उद्यन्त गिरो यदि च तमना भूत ||
1.178.e: Victorious with the men, Hero in battles, Indra, who hears the singer's supplication,  Will bring his car nigh to the man who offers, if he himself upholds the songs that praise him.

1.178.d: एवा नर्भिरिन्द्रः सुश्रवस्या परखादः पर्क्षो अभि मित्रिणो भूत | समर्य इष सतवते विवाचि सत्राकरो यजमानस्यशंसः ||
1.178.e: Yea, Indra, with the men, through love of glory consumes the sacred food which friends have offered.  The ever-strengthening song of him who worships is sung in fight amid the clash of voices.

1.178.d: तवया वयं मघवन्निन्द्र शत्रुनभि षयम महतो मन्यमनान | तवं तराता तवमु नो वर्धे भुर्वि... ||
1.178.e: Aided by thee, O Maghavan, O Indra, may we subdue our foes who count them mighty.  Be our protector, strengthen and increase us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.179.d: परुवीरहं शरदः शश्रमणा दोषा वस्तोरुषसो जरयन्तीः | मिनाति शरियं जरिमा तनूनमप्यु नु पत्नीर्व्र्षणो जगम्युः ||
1.179.e: Many years have I been serving you diligently, both day and night, and through mornings, bringing on old age; decay now impairs the beauty of my limbsn  What, therefore, is now (to be done); let husbands approach their wives.

1.179.d: ये चिद धि पूर्व रतसाप आसन साकं देवेभिरवदन्न्र्तानि | ते चिदवसुर्नह्यन्तमापुः समू नु पत्नीर्व्र्षभिर्जगम्युः ||
1.179.e: The ancient sages, disseminators of truth, who, verily, conversed of tuths with the gods, begot (progeny), nor thereby violated (their vow of continence), therefore should wives be approached by their husbands.

1.179.d: न मर्षा शरान्तं यदवन्ति देवा विश्वा इत सप्र्धो अभ्यश्नवाव | जयावेदत्र शतनीथमजिं यत सम्यञ्चा मिथुनावभ्यजाव ||
1.179.e: (Agastya): Penance has not been practised in vain; since the gods protect us, we may indulge all our desires; in this world we may triumph in many conflicts, if we exert ourselves mutually together

1.179.d: नदस्य मा रुधतः काम आगन्नित आजातो अमुतः कुतश्चित | लोपामुद्र वर्षणं नी रिणति धीरमधीर धयति शवसन्तम ||
1.179.e: Desire, either from this cause or from that, has come upon me whilst engaged in prayer and suppressing (passion); let Lopāmudrā approach her husband; the unsteady feminine le beguiles the firm and resolute man.

1.179.d: इमं न सोममन्तितो हर्त्सु पीतमुप बरुवे | यत सीमागश्चक्र्मा तत सु मर्ळतु पुलुकामो हि मर्त्यः ||
1.179.e: (Pupil): I beseech the Soma, which has been drunk in my heart, that it may fully expiate the sin we have committed; man is subject to many desires.

1.179.d: अगस्त्यः खनमनः खनित्रैः परजमपत्यं बलमिछमानः | उभौ वर्णाव रषिरुग्रः पुपोष सत्या देवेष्वशिषो जगाम ||
1.179.e: Agastya, a venerable sage, working with (fit) implements, desiring progeny, offspring, and strength, practised both classes (of obligations), and received true benedictions from the gods.

1.180.d: युवो रजांसि सुयमासो अश्वा रथो यद वां पर्यर्णांसिदियत | हिरण्यया वां पवयह परुषायन मध्वः पिबन्ता उषसः सचेथे ||
1.180.e: LIGHTLY your coursers travel through the regions when round the sea of air your car is flying.  Your golden fellies scatter drops of moisture: drinking the sweetness ye  attend  the Mornings.

1.180.d: युवमत्यस्याव नक्षथो यद विपत्मनो नर्यस्य परयज्योः | सवसा यद वां विश्वगूर्ती भराति वाजायेट्टे मधुपाविषे च ||
1.180.e: Ye as ye travel overtake the Courser who flies apart, the Friend of man, most holy.  The prayer is that the Sister may convey you, all praised, meath-drinkers! to support and strengthen.

1.180.d: युवं पय उस्रियायामधत्तं पक्वमामायामव पूर्व्यंगोः | अन्तर्यद वनिनो वां रतप्सू हवारो न शुचिर्यजते हविष्मान ||
1.180.e: Ye have deposited, matured within her, in the raw cow the first milk of the milch-cow,  Which the bright offerer, shining like a serpent mid trees, presents to you whose form is perfect.

1.180.d: युवं ह घर्मं मधुमन्तमत्रये.अपो न कषोदो.अव्र्णीतमेषे | तद वां नरावश्विना पश्वैष्टी रथ्येव चक्रा परति यन्ति मध्वः ||
1.180.e: Ye made the fierce heat to be full of sweetness for Atri at his wish, like streaming water.  Fire-offering thence is yours, O Aśvins, Heroes: your car-wheels speed to us like springs of honey.

1.180.d: आ वां दानाय वव्र्तीय दस्रा गोरोहेण तौग्र्यो न जिव्रिः | अपः कषोणी सचते माहिना वां जूर्णो वामक्षुरंहसो यजत्रा ||
1.180.e: Like Tugra's ancient son may I, ye Mighty, bring you to give your gifts with milk-oblations.  Your greatness compasseth Earth, Heaven, and Waters: decayed for you is sorrow's net, ye Holy.

1.180.d: नि यद युवेथे नियुतः सुदानू उप सवधाभिः सर्जथः पुरन्धिम | परेषद वेषद वातो न सूरिरा महे ददे सुव्रतोन वाजम ||
1.180.e: When, Bounteous Ones, ye drive your yoked team downward, ye send, by your own natures, understanding.  Swift as the wind let the prince please and feast you: he, like a pious man, gains strength for increase.

1.180.d: वयं चिद धि वां जरितारः सत्या विपन्यामहे वि पणिर्हितावान | अधा चिद धि षमाश्विनावनिन्द्या पाथो हि षमाव्र्षणावन्तिदेवम ||
1.180.e: For verily we truthful singers praise you the niggard trafficker is here excluded.  Now, even now do ye O blameless Aśvins, ye Mighty, guard the man whose God is near him.

1.180.d: युवं चिद धि षमाश्विनावनु दयून विरुद्रस्य परस्रवणस्यसातौ | अगस्त्यो नरां नर्षु परशस्तः काराधुनीव चितयत सहस्रैः ||
1.180.e: You of a truth day after day, O Aśvins, that he might win the very plenteous torrent,  Agastya, famous among mortal heroes, roused with a thousand lauds like sounds of music.

1.180.d: पर यद वहेथे महिना रथस्य पर सयन्द्रा याथो मनुषो न होता | धत्तं सूरिभ्य उत व सवश्व्यं नासत्य रयिषाचः सयाम ||
1.180.e: When with the glory of your car ye travel, when we go speeding like the priest of mortals,  And give good horses to sacrificers, may we, Nāsatyas! gain our share of riches.

1.180.d: तं वां रथं वयमद्या हुवेम सतोमैरश्विना सुवितायनव्यम | अरिष्टनेमिं परि दयामियानं वि... ||
1.180.e: With songs of praise we call to-day, O Aśvins, that your new chariot, for our own well-being,  That circles heaven with never-injured fellies. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.181.d: कदु परेष्टाविषां रयीणामध्वर्यन्ता यदुन्निनीथोपाम | अयं वां यज्ञो अक्र्त परशस्तिं वसुधिती अवितारा जनानाम ||
1.181.e: WHAT, dearest Pair, is this in strength and riches that ye as Priests are bring from the waters?  This sacrifice is your glorification, ye who protect mankind and give them treasures.

1.181.d: आ वामश्वासः शुचयः पयस्पा वातरंहसो दिव्यासो अत्याः | मनोजुवो वर्षणो वीतप्र्ष्ठा एह सवराजो अश्विनावहन्तु ||
1.181.e: May your pure steeds, rain-drinkers, bring you hither, swift as the tempest, your celestial coursers,  Rapid as thought, with fair backs, full of vigour, resplendent in their native light, O Aśvins.

1.181.d: आ वां रथो.अवनिर्न परवत्वान सर्प्रवन्धुरः सुविताय गम्याः | वर्ष्ण सथातारा मनसो जवीयानहम्पूर्वो यजतोधिष्ण्या यः ||
1.181.e: Your car is like a torrent rushing downward: may it come nigh, broad-seated, for our welfare,—  Car holy, strong, that ever would be foremost, thought-swift, which ye, for whom we long, have mounted.

1.181.d: इहेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा नामभिः सवैः | जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ||
1.181.e: Here sprung to life, they both have sung together, with bodies free from stain, with signs that mark them;  One of you Prince of Sacrifice, the Victor, the other counts as Heaven's auspicious offspring.

1.181.d: पर वां निचेरुः ककुहो वशाननु पिशङगरूपः सदनानि गम्याः | हरी अन्यस्य पीपयन्त वाजैर्मथ्रा रजांस्यश्विना वि घोषैः ||
1.181.e: May your car-seat, down-gliding, golden-coloured, according to your wish approach our dwellings.  Men shall feed full the bay steeds of the other, and, Aśvins they with roars shall stir the regions.

1.181.d: पर वां शरद्वान वर्षभो न निष्षाट पूर्वीरिषश्चरति मध्व इष्णन | एवैरन्यस्य पीपयन्त वाजैर्वेषन्तीरूर्ध्वा नद्यो न आगुः ||
1.181.e: Forth comes your strong Bull like a cloud of autumn, sending abundant food of liquid sweetness.  Let them feed with the other's ways and vigour: the upper streams have come and do us service.

1.181.d: असर्जि वां सथविरा वेधसा गीर्बाळ्हे अश्विना तरेधा कषरन्ती | उपस्तुताववतं नाधमानं यामन्नयामञ्छ्र्णुतं हवं मे ||
1.181.e: Your constant song hath been sent forth, Disposers! that flows threefold in mighty strength, O Aśvins.  Thus lauded, give the suppliant protection moving or resting hear mine invocation.

1.181.d: उत सया वां रुशतो वप्ससो गीस्त्रिबर्हिषि सदसि पिन्वतेनॄन | वर्षा वां मेघो वर्षणा पीपाय गोर्न सेके मनुषोदशस्यन ||
1.181.e: This song of bright contents for you is swelling in the men's hall where three-fold grass is ready.  Your strong rain-cloud, ye Mighty Ones, hath swollen, honouring men as ’twere with milk's outpouring.

1.181.d: युवां पूषेवाश्विना पुरन्धिरग्निमुषां न जरते हविष्मान | हुवे यद वां वरिवस्या गर्णानो वि... ||
1.181.e: The prudent worshipper, like Pūṣan, Aśvins! praises you as he praises Dawn and Agni,  When, singing with devotion, he invokes you. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.182.d: अभूदिदं वयुनमो षु भूषता रथो वर्षण्वान मदता मनीषिणः | धियंजिन्वा धिष्ण्या विश्पलावसू दिवो नपात सुक्र्ते शुचिव्रता ||
1.182.e: THIS was the task. Appear promptly, ye prudent Ones. Here is the chariot drawn by strong steeds: be ye glad.  Heart-stirring, longed for, succourers of Viśpalā, here are Heaven's Sons whose sway blesses the pious man.

1.182.d: इन्द्रतमा हि धिष्ण्या मरुत्तमा दस्रा दंसिष्ठा रथ्या रथीतमा | पूर्णं रथं वहेथे मध्व आचितं तेन दाश्वांसमुप याथो अश्विना ||
1.182.e: Longed for, most Indra-like, mighty, most Marut-like, most wonderful in deed, car-borne, best charioteers,  Bring your full chariot hither heaped with liquid sweet: thereon, ye Aśvins, come to him who offers gifts.

1.182.d: किमत्र दस्रा कर्णुथः किमासाथे जनो यः कश्चिदहविर्महीयते | अति करमिष्टं जुरतं पणेरसुं जयोतिर्विप्राय कर्णुतं वचस्यवे ||
1.182.e: What make ye there, ye Mighty? Wherefore linger ye with folk who, offering not, are held in high esteem?  Pass over them; make ye the niggard's life decay: give light unto the singer eloquent in praise.

1.182.d: जम्भयतमभितो रायतः शुनो हतं मर्धो विदथुस्तान्यश्विना | वाचं-वाचं जरितू रत्निनीं कर्तमुभा शंसं नासत्यावतं मम ||
1.182.e: Crunch up on. every side the dogs who bark at us: slay ye our foes, O Aśvins this ye understand.  Make wealthy every word of him who praises you: accept with favour, both Nāsatyas, this my laud.

1.182.d: युवमेतं चक्रथुः सिन्धुषु पलवमात्मन्वन्तं पक्षिणन्तौग्र्याय कम | येन देवत्रा मनसा निरूहथुः सुपप्तनीपेतथुः कषोदसो महः ||
1.182.e: Ye made for Tugra's son amid the water-floods that animated ship with wings to fly withal,  Whereon with God-devoted mind ye brought him forth, and fled with easy flight from out the mighty surge.

1.182.d: अवविद्धं तौग्र्यमप्स्वन्तरनारम्भणे तमसि परविद्धम | चतस्रो नावो जठलस्य जुष्टा उदश्विभ्यामिषिताः पारयन्ति ||
1.182.e: Four ships most welcome in the midst of ocean, urged by the Aśvins, save the son of Tugra,  Him who was cast down headlong in the waters, plunged in the thick inevitable darkness.

1.182.d: कः सविद वर्क्षो निष्ठितो मध्ये अर्णसो यं तौग्र्यो नाधितः पर्यषस्वजत | पर्णा मर्गस्य पतरोरिवारभ उदश्विना ऊहथुः शरोमताय कम ||
1.182.e: What tree was that which stood fixed in surrounding sea to which the son of Tugra supplicating clung?  Like twigs, of which some winged creature may take hold, ye, Aśvins, bore him off safely to your renown.

1.182.d: तद वां नरा नासत्यावनु षयाद यद वां मानास उचथमवोचन | अस्मादद्य सदसः सोम्यादा] वि... ||
1.182.e: Welcome to you be this the hymn of praises uttered by Mānas, O Nāsatyas, Heroes,  From this our gathering where we offer Soma. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.183.d: तं युञ्जाथां मनसो यो जवीयान तरिवन्धुरो वर्षण यस्त्रिचक्रः | येनोपयाथः सुक्र्तो दुरोणं तरिधातुन पतथोविर्न पर्णैः ||
1.183.e: MAKE ready that which passes thought in swiftness, that hath three wheels and triple seat, ye Mighty,  Whereon ye seek the dwelling of the pious, whereon, threefold, ye fly like birds with pinions.

1.183.d: सुव्र्द रथो वर्तते यन्नभि कषां यत तिष्ठथः करतुमन्तानु पर्क्षे | वपुर्वपुष्या सचतामियं गीर्दिवो दुहित्रोषसा सचेथे ||
1.183.e: Light rolls your easy chariot faring earthward, what time, for food, ye, full of wisdom, mount it.  May this song, wondrous fair, attend your glory: ye, as ye travel, wait on Dawn Heaven's Daughter.

1.183.d: आ तिष्ठतं सुव्र्तं यो रथो वामनु वरतानि वर्तते हविष्मान | येन नरा नासत्येषयध्यै वर्तिर्याथस्तनयायत्मने च ||
1.183.e: Ascend your lightly rolling car, approaching the worshipper who turns him to his duties,—  Whereon ye come unto the house to quicken man and his offspring, O Nāsatyas, Heroes.

1.183.d: मा वां वर्को मा वर्कीरा दधर्षीन मा परि वर्क्तमुतमाति धक्तम | अयं वां भागो निहित इयं गीर्दस्राविमे वां निधयो मधूनाम ||
1.183.e: Let not the wolf, let not the she-wolf harm you. Forsake me not, nor pass me by or others.  Here stands your share, here is your hymn, ye Mighty: yours are these vessels, full of pleasant juices.

1.183.d: युवां गोतमः पुरुमीळ्हो अत्रिर्दस्रा हवते.अवसे हविष्मान | दिशं न दिष्टां रजूयेव यन्ता मे हवं नासत्योप यातम ||
1.183.e: Gotama, Purumīlha, Atri bringing oblations all invoke you for protection.  Like one who goes straight to the point directed, ye Nāsatyas, to mine invocation.

1.183.d: अतारिष्म तमसस पारमस्य परति वां सतोमो अश्विनावधायि | एह यातं पथिभिर्देवयानैर्वि... ||
1.183.e: We have passed o’er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Aśvins.  Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.184.d: ता वामद्य तावपरं हुवेमोछन्त्यामुषसि वह्निरुक्थैः | नासत्या कुह चित सन्तावर्यो दिवो नपाता सुदास्तराय ||
1.184.e: LET us invoke you both this day and after the priest is here with lauds when morn is breaking:  Nāsatyas, wheresoe’er ye be, Heaven's Children, for him who is more liberal than the godless.

1.184.d: अस्मे ऊ षु वर्षणा मादयेथामुत पणीन्र्हतमूर्म्या मदन्ता | शरुतं मे अछोक्तिभिर्मतीनामेष्टा नरा निचेतारच कर्णैः ||
1.184.e: With us, ye Mighty, let yourselves be joyful, glad in our stream of Soma slay the niggards.  Graciously hear my hymns and invitations, marking, O Heroes, with your cars my longing.

1.184.d: शरिये पूषन्निषुक्र्तेव देवा नासत्या वहतुं सूर्यायाः | वच्यन्ते वां ककुहा अप्सु जाता युगा जूर्णेव वरुणस्य भूरेः ||
1.184.e: Nāsatyas, Pūṣans, ye as Gods for glory arranged and set in order Sūrya's bridal.  Your giant steeds move on, sprung from the waters, like ancient times of Varuṇa the Mighty.

1.184.d: अस्मे सा वां माध्वी रातिरस्तु सतोमं हिनोतं मान्यस्य कारोः | अनु यद वां शरवस्या सुदानू सुवीर्याय चर्षणयोमदन्ति ||
1.184.e: Your grace be with us, ye who love sweet juices: further the hymn sung by the poet Māna,  When men are joyful in your glorious actions, to win heroic strength, ye Bounteous Givers.

1.184.d: एष वां सतोमो अश्विनावकारि मानेभिर्मघवाना सुव्र्क्ति | यातं वर्तिस्तनयाय तमने चागस्त्ये नासत्या मदन्ता ||
1.184.e: This praise was made, O liberal Lords, O Aśvins, for you with fair adornment by the Mānas.  Come to our house for us and for our children, rejoicing, O Nāsatyas, in Agastya.
We have passed o’er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Aśvins.  Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. may we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.185.d: कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरायोः कथा जाते कवयः को वि वेद | विश्वं तमना बिभ्र्तो यद ध नाम वि वर्तेते अहनी चक्रियेव ||
1.185.e: WHETHER of these is elder, whether later? How were they born? Who knoweth it, ye sages?  These of themselves support all things existing: as on a car the Day and Night roll onward.

1.185.d: भूरिं दवे अचरन्ती चरन्तं पद्वन्तं गर्भमपदी दधाते | नित्यं न सूनुं पित्रोरुपस्थे दयावा रक्षतं पर्थिवी नो अभ्वात ||
1.185.e: The Twain uphold, though motionless and footless, a widespread offspring having feet and moving.  Like your own son upon his parents’ bosom, protect us, Heaven and earth, from fearful danger.

1.185.d: अनेहो दात्रमदितेरनर्वं हुवे सवर्वदवधं नमस्वत | तद रोदसी जनयतं जरित्रे दयावा ... ||
1.185.e: I call for Aditi's unrivalled bounty, perfect, celestial, deathless, meet for worship.  Produce this, ye Twain Worlds, for him who lauds you. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.

1.185.d: अतप्यमाने अवसावन्ती अनु षयाम रोदसी देवपुत्रे | उभे देवानामुभयेभिरह्नां दयावा ... ||
1.185.e: May we be close to both the Worlds who suffer no pain, Parents of Gods, who aid with favour,  Both mid the Gods, with Day and Night alternate. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.

1.185.d: संगछमाने युवती समन्ते सवसारा जामी पित्रोरुपस्थे | अभिजिघ्रन्ती भुवनस्य नाभिं दयावा ... ||
1.185.e: Faring together, young, with meeting limits, Twin Sisters lying in their Parents’ bosom,  Kissing the centre of the world together. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.

1.185.d: उर्वी सद्मनी बर्हती रतेन हुवे देवानामवसा जनित्री | दधाते ये अम्र्तं सुप्रतीके दयावा ... ||
1.185.e: Duly I call the two wide seats, the mighty, the general Parents, with the God's protection.  Who, beautiful to look on, make the nectar. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.

1.185.d: उर्वी पर्थ्वी बहुले दूरेन्ते उप बरुवे नमसा यज्ञे अस्मिन | दधाते ये सुभगे सुप्रतूर्ती दयावा ... ||
1.185.e: Wide, vast, and manifold, whose bounds are distant,—these, reverent, I address at this our worship,  The blessed Pair, victorious, all-sustaining. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.

1.185.d: देवान वा यच्चक्र्मा कच्चिदागः सखायं वा सदमिज्जास्पतिं वा | इयं धीर्भूया अवयानमेषां दयावा .. . ||
1.185.e: What sin we have at any time committed against the Gods, our friend, our house's chieftain,  Thereof may this our hymn be expiation. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.

1.185.d: उभा शंसा नर्या मामविष्टामुभे मामूती अवसा सचेताम | भूरि चिदर्यः सुदास्तरायेषा मदन्त इषयेम देवाः ||
1.185.e: May both these Friends of man, who bless, preserve me, may they attend me with their help and favour.  Enrich the man more liberal than the godless. May we, ye Gods, be strong with food rejoicing.

1.185.d: रतं दिवे तदवोचं पर्थिव्या अभिश्रावाय परथमं सुमेधाः | पातामवद्याद दुरितादभीके पिता माता च रक्षतामवोभिः ||
1.185.e: Endowed with understanding, I have uttered this truth, for all to hear, to Earth and Heaven.  Be near us, keep us from reproach and trouble. Father and Mother, with your help preserve us.

1.185.d: इदं दयावाप्र्थिवी सत्यमस्तु पितर्मातर्यदिहोपब्रुवे वाम | भूतं देवानामवमे अवोभिर्विद्या... ||
1.185.e: Be this my prayer fulfilled, O Earth and Heaven, wherewith, Father and Mother, I address you.  Nearest of Gods be ye with your protection. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.186.d: आ न इळभिर्विदथे सुशस्ति विश्वानरः सविता देव एतु | अपि यथा युवानो मत्सथा नो विश्वं जगदभिपित्वे मनीषा ||
1.186.e: LOVED of all men, may Savitar, through praises offered as sacred food, come to our synod,  That you too, through-our hymn, ye ever-youthful, may gladden, at your visit, all our people.

1.186.d: आ नो विश्व आस्क्रा गमन्तु देवा मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणः सजोषाः | भुवन यथा नो विश्वे वर्धासः करन सुषाहा विथुरं न शवः ||
1.186.e: To us may all the Gods come trooped together, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa concordant,  That all may be promoters of our welfare, and with great might preserve our strength from slackness.

1.186.d: परेष्ठं वो अतिथिं गर्णीषे.अग्निं शस्तिभिस्तुर्वणिः सजोषाः | असद यथा नो वरुणः सुकीर्तिरिषश्च पर्षदरिगूर्तः सूरिः ||
1.186.e: Agni I sing, the guest you love most dearly: the Conqueror through our lauds is friendly-minded.  That he may be our Varuṇa rich in glory and send food like a prince praised by the godly.

1.186.d: उप व एषे नमसा जिगीषोषासानक्ता सुदुघेव धेनुः | समाने अहन विमिमानो अर्कं विषुरूपे पयसि सस्मिन्नूधन ||
1.186.e: To you I seek with reverence, Night and Morning, like a cow good to milk, with hope to conquer,  Preparing on a common day the praise. song with milk of various hues within this udder.

1.186.d: उत नो.अहिर्बुध्न्यो मयस कः शिशुं न पिप्युषीव वेति सिन्धुः | येन नपातमपां जुनाम मनोजुवो वर्षणो यं वहन्ति ||
1.186.e: May the great Dragon of the Deep rejoice us: as one who nourishes her young comes Sindhu,  With whom we will incite the Child of Waters whom vigorous course swift as thought bring hither.

1.186.d: उत न ईं तवष्टा गन्त्वछा समत सूरिभिरभिपित्वे सजोषाः | आ वर्त्रहेन्द्रश्चर्षणिप्रास्तुविष्टमो नरां नैह गम्याः ||
1.186.e: Moreover Tvaṣṭar also shall approach us, one-minded with the princes at his visit.  Hither shall come the Vṛtra-slayer Indra, Ruler of men, as strongest of the Heroes.

1.186.d: उत न ईं मतयो.अश्वयोगः शिशुं न गावस्तरुणं रिहन्ति | तमीं गिरो जनयो न पत्नीः सुरभिष्टमं नरांनसन्त ||
1.186.e: Him too our hymns delight, that yoke swift horses, like mother cows who lick their tender youngling.  To him our songs shall yield themselves like spouses, to him the most delightful of the Heroes.

1.186.d: उत न ईं मरुतो वर्द्धसेनाः समद रोदसी समनसः सदन्तु | पर्षदश्वासो.अवनयः न रथा रिशादसो मित्रयुजो न देवाः ||
1.186.e: So may the Maruts, armed with mighty weapons, rest here on heaven and earth with hearts in concord,  As Gods whose cars have dappled steeds like torrents, destroyers of the foe allies of Mitra.

1.186.d: पर नु यदेषां महिना चिकित्रे पर युञ्जते परयुजस्ते सुव्र्क्ति | अध यदेषां सुदिने न शरुर्विश्वमेरिणं परुषायन्त सेनः ||
1.186.e: They hasten on to happy termination their orders when they are made known by  glory.  As on a fair bright day the arrow flieth o’er all the barren soil their missiles sparkle.

1.186.d: परो अश्विनाववसे कर्णुध्वं पर पूषणं सवतवसो हि सन्ति | अद्वेषो विष्णुर्वात रभुक्षा अछा सुम्नाय वव्र्तीयदेवान ||
1.186.e: Incline the Aśvins to show grace, and Pūṣan, for power and might have they, their own possession.  Friendly are Viṣṇu, Vāta, and Ṛbhukṣan so may I bring the Gods to make us happy.

1.186.d: इयं सा वो अस्मे दीधितिर्यजत्रा अपिप्राणी च सदनी च भूयः | नि या देवेषु यतते वसूयुर्वि... ||
1.186.e: This is my reverent thought of you, ye Holy; may it inspire you, make you dwell among us,—  Thought, toiling for the Gods and seeking treasure. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.187.d: पितुं नु सतोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम | यस्य तरितो वयोजसा वर्त्रं विपर्वमर्दयत ||
1.187.e: Now will I glorify Food that upholds great strength,  By whose invigorating power Trita rent Vṛtra limb from limb.

1.187.d: सवादो पितो मधो पितो वयं तवा वव्र्महे | अस्माकमविता भव ||
1.187.e: O pleasant Food, O Food of meath, thee have we chosen for our own,  So be our kind protector thou.

1.187.d: उप नः पितवा चर शिवः शिवाभिरूतिभिः | मयोभुरद्विषेण्यः सखा सुशेवो अद्वयाः ||
1.187.e: Come hitherward to us, O Food, auspicious with auspicious help,  Health-bringing, not unkind, a dear and guileless friend.

1.187.d: तव तये पितो रस रजांस्यनु विष्ठिताः | दिवि वाता इव शरिताः ||
1.187.e: These juices which, O Food, are thine throughout the regions are diffused.  like winds they have their place in heaven.

1.187.d: तव तये पितो ददतस्तव सवादिष्ठ ते पितो | पर सवाद्मानो रसानां तुविग्रीवा इवेरते ||
1.187.e: These gifts of thine, O Food, O Food most sweet to taste,  These savours of thy juices work like creatures that have mighty necks.

1.187.d: तवे पितो महानां देवानां मनो हिताम | अकारि चारु केतुना तवाहिमवसावधीत ||
1.187.e: In thee, O Food, is set the spirit of great Gods.  Under thy flag brave deeds were done he slew the Dragon with thy help.

1.187.d: यददो पितो अजगन विवस्व पर्वतानाम | अत्रा चिन नो मधो पितो.अरं भक्षाय गम्याः ||
1.187.e: If thou be gone unto the splendour of the clouds,  Even from thence, O Food of meath, prepared for our enjoyment, come.
Whatever morsel we consume from waters or from plants of earth, O Soma, wax thou fat thereby.

1.187.d: यत ते सोम गवाशिरो यवाशिरो भजामहे | वातापे ... ||
1.187.e: What Soma, we enjoy from thee in milky food or barley-brew, Vātāpi, grow thou fat thereby.

1.187.d: करम्भ ओषधे भव पीवो वर्क्क उदारथिः | वातापे ... ||
1.187.e: O Vegetable, Cake of meal, he wholesome, firm, and strengthening: Vātāpi, grow thou fat thereby.

1.187.d: तं तवा वयं पितो वचोभिर्गावो न हव्या सुषूदिम | देवेभ्यस्त्वा सधमादमस्मभ्यं तवा सधमादम ||
1.187.e: O Food, from thee as such have we drawn forth with lauds, like cows, our sacrificial gifts,  From thee who banquetest with Gods, from thee who banquetest with us.

1.188.d: समिद्धो अद्य राजसि देवो देवैः सहस्रजित | दूतो हव्या कविर्वह ||
1.188.e: WINNER of thousands, kindled, thou shinest a God with Gods to-day.  Bear out oblations, envoy, Sage.

1.188.d: तनुनपाद रतं यते मध्वा यज्ञः समज्यते | दधत सहस्रिणीरिषः ||
1.188.e: Child of Thyself the sacrifice is for the righteous blent with meath,  Presenting viands thousandfold.

1.188.d: आजुह्वानो न ईड्यो देवाना वक्षि यज्ञियान | अग्ने सहस्रसा असि ||
1.188.e: Invoked and worthy of our praise bring Gods whose due is sacrifice:  Thou, Agni, givest countless gifts.
To seat a thousand Heroes they eastward have strewn the grass with might,  Whereon, Ādityas, ye shine forth.

1.188.d: विराट सम्राड विभ्वीः परभ्वीर्बह्वीश्च भूयसीश्चयाः | दुरो घर्तान्यक्षरन ||
1.188.e: The sovran all-imperial Doors, wide, good, many and manifold,  Have poured their streams of holy oil.

1.188.d: सुरुक्मे हि सुपेशसाधि शरिया विराजतः | उषासावेहसीदताम ||
1.188.e: With gay adornment, fair to see, in glorious beauty shine they forth:  Let Night and Morning rest them here.

1.188.d: परथमा हि सुवाचसा होतारा दैव्या कवी | यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमम ||
1.188.e: Let these two Sages first of all, heralds divine and eloquent,  Perform for us this sacrifice.

1.188.d: भारतीळे सरस्वति या वः सर्वा उपब्रुवे | ता नश्चोदयत शरिये ||
1.188.e: You I address, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī, and Iḷā, all:  Urge ye us on to glorious fame.

1.188.d: तवष्टा रूपाणि हि परभुः पशुन विश्वान समानजे | तेषां नः सफातिमा यज ||
1.188.e: Tvaṣṭar the Lord hath made all forms and all the cattle of the field  Cause them to multiply for us.

1.188.d: उप तमन्या वनस्पते पाथो देवेभ्यः सर्ज | अग्निर्हव्यानि सिष्वदत ||
1.188.e: Send to the Gods, Vanaspati, thyself, the sacrificial draught:  Let Agni make the oblations sweet.

1.188.d: पुरोगा अग्निर्देवानां गायत्रेण समज्यते | सवाहाक्र्तीषु रोचते ||
1.188.e: Agni, preceder of the Gods, is honoured with the sacred song:  He glows at offerings blest with Hail!

1.189.d: अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान | युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमौक्तिंविधेम ||
1.189.e: BY goodly paths lead us to riches, Agni, God who knowest every sacred duty.  Remove the sin that makes us stray and wander. most ample adoration will we bring thee.

1.189.d: अग्ने तवं पारया नव्यो अस्मान सवस्तिभिरति दुर्गाणि विश्वा | पुश्च पर्थ्वी बहुला न उर्वि भवा तोकाय तनयाय शं योः ||
1.189.e: Lead us anew to happiness, O Agni; lead us beyond all danger and affliction.  Be unto us a wide broad ample castle bless, prosper on their way our sons and offspring.

1.189.d: अग्ने तवमस्मद युयोध्यमीवा अनग्नित्रा अभ्यमन्त कर्ष्टीः | पुनरस्मभ्यं सुविताय देव कषां विश्वेभिरम्र्तेभिर्यजत्र ||
1.189.e: Far from us, Agni, put thou all diseases let them strike lauds that have no saving Agni.  God, make our home again to be a blessing, with all the Immortal Deities, O Holy.

1.189.d: पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैरुत परिये सदन आ शुशुक्वान | मा ते भयं जरितारं यविष्ठ नूनं विदन मापरं सहस्वः ||
1.189.e: Preserve us, Agni, with perpetual succour, refulgent in the dwelling which thou lovest.  O Conqueror, most youthful, let no danger touch him who praises thee to-day or after.

1.189.d: मा नो अग्ने.अव सर्जो अघायाविष्यवे रिपवे दुछुनायै | मादत्वते दशते मादते नो मा रीषते सहसावन परा दाः ||
1.189.e: Give not us up a prey to sin, O Agni, the greedy enemy that brings us trouble;  Not to the fanged that bites, not to the toothless: give not us up, thou Conqueror, to the spoiler.

1.189.d: वि घ तवावान रतजात यंसद गर्णानो अग्ने तन्वे वरूथम | विश्वाद रिरिक्षोरुत वा निनित्सोरभिह्रुतामसि हि देव विष्पट ||
1.189.e: Such as thou art, born after Law, O Agni when lauded give protection to our bodies,  From whosoever would reproach or injure: for thou, God, rescuest from all oppression.

1.189.d: तवं तानग्न उभयानिव विद्वान वेषि परपित्वे मनुषो यजत्र | अभिपित्वे मनवे शास्यो भूर्मर्म्र्जेन्य उशिग्भिर्नाक्रः ||
1.189.e: Thou, well discerning both these classes, comest to men at early morn, O holy Agni.  Be thou obedient unto man at evening, to be adorned, as keen, by eager suitors.

1.189.d: अवोचाम निवचनान्यस्मिन मानस्य सूनुः सहसाने अग्नौ | वयं सहस्रं रषिभिः सनेम वि... ||
1.189.e: To him have we addressed our pious speeches, I, Māna's son, to him victorious Agni.  May we gain countless riches with the sages. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.190.d: अनर्वाणं वर्षभं मन्द्रजिह्वं बर्हस्पतिं वर्धया नव्यमर्कैः | गाथान्यः सुरुचो यस्य देवा आश्र्ण्वन्ति नवमानस्य मर्ताः ||
1.190.e: GLORIFY thou Bṛhaspati, the scatheless, who must be praised with hymns, sweet-tongued and mighty,  To whom as leader of the song, resplendent, worthy of lauds, both Gods and mortals listen.

1.190.d: तं रत्विया उप वाचः सचन्ते सर्गो न यो देवयतामसर्जि | बर्हस्पतिः स हयञ्जो वरांसि विभ्वाभवत सं रते मातरिश्वा ||
1.190.e: On him wait songs according to the season even as a stream of pious men set moving.  Bṛhaspati—for he laid out the expanses—was, at the sacrifice, vast Mātariśvan.

1.190.d: उपस्तुतिं नमस उद्यतिं च शलोकं यंसत सवितेव पर बाहू | अस्य करत्वाहन्यो यो अस्ति मर्गो न भीमो अरक्षसस्तुविष्मान ||
1.190.e: The praise, the verse that offers adoration, may he bring forth, as the Sun sends his arms out,  He who gives daily light through this God's wisdom, strong as a dread wild beast, and inoffensive.

1.190.d: अस्य शलोको दिवीयते पर्थिव्यामत्यो न यंसद यक्षभ्र्द विचेताः | मर्गाणां न हेतयो यन्ति चेमा बर्हस्पतेरहिमायानभि दयून ||
1.190.e: His song of praise pervades the earth and heaven: let the wise worshipper draw it, like a courser.  These of Bṛhaspati, like hunters' arrows, go to the skies that change their hue like serpents.

1.190.d: ये तवा देवोस्रिकं मन्यमानाः पापा भद्रमुपजीवन्ति पज्राः | न दूढ्ये अनु ददासि वामं बर्हस्पते चयस इत पियारुम ||
1.190.e: Those, God, who count thee as a worthless bullock, and, wealthy sinners, live on thee the Bounteous,—  On fools like these no blessing thou bestowest: Bṛhaspati, thou punishest the spiteful.

1.190.d: सुप्रैतुः सूयवसो न पन्था दुर्नियन्तुः परिप्रीतो न मित्रः | अनर्वाणो अभि ये चक्षते नो.अपीव्र्ता अपोर्णुवन्तो अस्थुः ||
1.190.e: Like a fair path is he, where grass is pleasant, though hard to win, a Friend beloved most early.  Those who unharmed by enemies behold us, while they would make them bare, stood closely compassed.

1.190.d: सं यं सतुभो.अवनयो न यन्ति समुद्रं न सरवतो रोधचक्राः | स विद्वानुभयं चष्टे अन्तर्ब्र्हस्पतिस्तर आपश्च गर्ध्रः ||
1.190.e: He to whom songs of praise go forth like torrents, as rivers eddying under banks flow sea-ward—  Bṛhaspati the wise, the eager, closely looks upon both, the waters and the vessel.

1.190.d: एवा महस्तुविजातस्तुविष्मान बर्हस्पतिर्व्र्षभो धायि देवः | स न सतुतो वीरवद धातु गोमद वि... ||
1.190.e: So hath Bṛhaspati, great, strong and mighty, the God exceeding powerful, been brought hither.  May he thus lauded give us kine and horses. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

1.191.d: कङकतो न कङकतो.अथो सतीनकङकतः | दवाविति पलुषी इति नयद्र्ष्ट अलिप्सत ||
1.191.e: VENOMOUS, slightly venomous, or venomous aquatic worm,—  Both creatures, stinging, unobserved, with poison have infected me.

1.191.d: अद्र्ष्टान हन्त्यायत्यथो हन्ति परायती | अथो अवघ्नती हन्त्यथो पिनष्टि पिंषती ||
1.191.e: Coming, it kills the unobserved; it kills them as it goes away,  It kills them as it drives them off, and bruising bruises them to death.

1.191.d: शरासः कुशरासो दर्भासः सैर्या उत | मौञ्जा अद्र्ष्टा वैरिणाः सर्वे साकं नयलिप्सत ||
1.191.e: Sara grass, Darbha, Kuśara, and Sairya, Muñja, Vīraṇa,  Where all these creatures dwell unseen, with poison have infected me.

1.191.d: नि गावो गोष्ठे असदन नि मर्गासो अविक्षत | नि केतवो जनानां नयद्र्ष्टा अलिप्सत ||
1.191.e: The cows had settled in their stalls, the beasts of prey had sought their lairs,  Extinguished were the lights of men, when things unseen infected me.

1.191.d: एत उ तये परत्यद्र्श्रन परदोषं तस्करा इव | अद्र्ष्टा विश्वद्र्ष्टाः परतिबुद्धा अभूतन ||
1.191.e: Or these, these reptiles, are observed, like lurking thieves at evening time.  Seers of all, themselves unseen: be therefore very vigilant.

1.191.d: दयौर्वः पिता पर्थिवी माता सोमो भरातादितिः सवसा | अद्र्ष्टा विश्वद्र्ष्टास्तिष्ठतेलयता सु कम ||
1.191.e: Heaven is your Sire, your Mother Earth, Soma your Brother, Aditi  Your Sister: seeing all, unseen, keep still and dwell ye happily.

1.191.d: ये अंस्या ये अङगयाः सूचीका ये परकङकताः | अद्र्ष्टाः किं चनेह वः सर्वे साकं नि जस्यत ||
1.191.e: Biters of shoulder or of limb, with needle-stings, most venomous,  Unseen, whatever ye may be, vanish together and be gone.

1.191.d: उत पुरस्तात सूर्य एति विश्वद्र्ष्टो अद्र्ष्टहा | अद्र्ष्टान सर्वाञ जम्भयन सर्वाश्च यातुधान्यः ||
1.191.e: Slayer of things unseen, the Sun, beheld of all, mounts, eastward, up,  Consuming all that are not seen, and evil spirits of the night.

1.191.d: उदपप्तदसौ सूर्यः पुरु विश्वानि जूर्वन | आदित्यः पर्वतेभ्यो विश्वद्र्ष्टो अद्र्ष्टहा ||
1.191.e: There hath the Sun-God mounted up, who scorches much and everything.  Even the Āditya from the hills, all-seen, destroying things unseen.

1.191.d: सूर्ये विषमा सजामि दर्तिं सुरावतो गर्हे | सो चिन नु नमराति नो वयं मरामारे अस्य योजनं हरिष्ठा मधु तवामधुला चकार ||
1.191.e: I hang the poison in the Sun, a wine-skin in a vintner's house,  He will not die, nor shall we die: his path is far: he whom Bay Horses bear hath turned thee to sweet meath.

1.191.d: इयत्तिका शकुन्तिका सका जघास ते विषम | सो चिन नु ... ||
1.191.e: This little bird, so very small, hath swallowed all thy poison up.  She will not die, nor shall we die: his path is far: he whom Bay Horses bear hath turned thee to sweet meath.

1.191.d: तरिः सप्त विष्पुलिङगका विषस्य पुष्यमक्षन | ताश्चिन्नु न मरन्ति नो वयं म... ||
1.191.e: The three-times-seven bright sparks of fire have swallowed up the poison's strength.  They will not die, nor shall we die: his path is far: he whom Bay Horses bear hath turned thee to sweet meath.

1.191.d: नवानां नवतीनां विषस्य रोपुषीणाम | सर्वासामग्रभं नामारे अस्य यो... ||
1.191.e: Of ninety rivers and of nine with power to stay the venom's course,—  The names of all I have secured: his path is far: he whom Bay Horses bear hath turned thee to sweet meath.

1.191.d: तरिः सप्त मयूर्यः सप्त सवसारो अग्रुवः | तास्ते विषं वि जभ्रिर उदकं कुम्भिनीरिव ||
1.191.e: So have the peahens three-times-seven, so have the maiden Sisters Seven  Carried thy venom far away, as girls bear water in their jars.

1.191.d: इयत्तकः कुषुम्भकस्तकं भिनद्म्यश्मना | ततो विषं पर वाव्र्ते पराचीरनु संवतः ||
1.191.e: The poison-insect is so small; I crush the creature with a stone.  I turn the poison hence away, departed unto distant lands.

1.191.d: कुषुम्भकस्तदब्रवीद गिरेः परवर्तमानकः | वर्श्चिकस्यारसं विषमरसं वर्श्चिक ते विषम ||
1.191.e: Forth issuing from the mountain's side the poison-insect spake and said:  Scorpion, they venom is but weak.

2.1.d: तवमग्ने दयुभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिस्त्वमद्भ्यस्त्वमश्मनस परि | तवं वनेभ्यस्त्वमोषधीभ्यस्त्वं नर्णां नर्पते जायसे शुचिः ||
2.1.e: THOU, Agni, shining in thy glory through the days, art brought to life from out the waters, from the stone:  From out the forest trees and herbs that grow on ground, thou, Sovran Lord of men art generated pure.

2.1.d: तवाग्ने होत्रं तव पोत्रं रत्वियं तव नेष्ट्रं तवमग्निद रतायतः | तव परशास्त्रं तवमध्वरीयसि बरह्मा चासि गर्हपतिश्च नो दमे ||
2.1.e: Thine is the Herald's task and Cleanser's duly timed; Leader art thou, and Kindler for the pious man.  Thou art Director, thou the ministering Priest: thou art the Brahman, Lord and Master in our home.

2.1.d: तवमग्न इन्द्रो वर्षभः सतामसि तवं विष्णुरुरुगायो नमस्यः | तवं बरह्मा रयिविद बरह्मणस पते तवं विधर्तःसचसे पुरन्ध्या ||
2.1.e: Hero of Heroes, Agni! Thou art Indra, thou art Viṣṇu of the Mighty Stride, adorable:  Thou, Brahmaṇaspati, the Brahman finding wealth: thou, O Sustainer, with thy wisdom tendest us.

2.1.d: तवमग्ने राजा वरुणो धर्तव्रतस्त्वं मित्रो भवसि दस्म ईड्यः | तवमर्यमा सत्पतिर्यस्य सम्भुजं तवमंशो विदथे देव भाजयुः ||
2.1.e: Agni, thou art King Varuṇa whose laws stand fast; as Mitra, Wonder-Worker, thou must be implored.  Aryaman, heroes' Lord, art thou, enriching all, and liberal Aṁśa in the synod, O thou God.

2.1.d: तवमग्ने तवष्टा विधते सुवीर्यं तव गनावो मित्रमहः सजात्यम | तवमाशुहेमा ररिषे सवश्व्यं तवं नरां शर्धो असि पुरूवसुः ||
2.1.e: Thou givest strength, as Tvaṣṭar, to the worshipper: thou wielding Mitra's power hast kinship with the Dames.  Thou, urging thy fleet coursers, givest noble steeds: a host of heroes art thou with great store of wealth.

2.1.d: तवमग्ने रुद्रो असुरो महो दिवस्त्वं शर्धो मारुतं पर्क्ष ईशिषे | तवं वातैररुणैर्यासि शंगयस्त्वं पूषा विधतः पासि नु तमना ||
2.1.e: Rudra art thou, the Asura of mighty heaven: thou art the Maruts’ host, thou art the Lord of food,  Thou goest with red winds: bliss hast thou in thine home. As Pūṣan thou thyself protectest worshippers.

2.1.d: तवमग्ने दरविणोदा अरंक्र्ते तवं देवः सविता रत्नधासि | तवं भगो नर्पते वस्व ईशिषे तवं पायुर्दमे यस्तेऽविधत ||
2.1.e: Giver of wealth art thou to him who honours thee; thou art God Savitar, granter of precious things.  As Bhaga, Lord of men! thou rulest over wealth, and guardest in his house him who hath served thee well.

2.1.d: तवमग्ने दम आ विश्पतिं विशस्त्वां राजानं सुविदत्रं रञ्जते | तवं विश्वानि सवनीक पत्यसे तवं सहस्राणि शता दश परति ||
2.1.e: To thee, the people's Lord within the house, the folk press forward to their King most graciously inclined.  Lord of the lovely look, all things belong to thee: ten, hundred, yea, a thousand are outweighed by thee.

2.1.d: तवामग्ने पितरमिष्टिभिर्नरस्त्वां भरात्राय शम्या तनूरुचम | तवं पुत्रो भवसि यस्ते.अविधत तवं सखा सुशेवः पास्याध्र्षः ||
2.1.e: Agni, men seek thee as a Father with their prayers, win thee, bright-formed, to brotherhood with holy act.  Thou art a Son to him who duly worships thee, and as a trusty Friend thou guardest from attack.

2.1.d: तवमग्न रभुराके नमस्यस्त्वं वाजस्य कषुमतो राय ईशिषे | तवं वि भास्यनु दक्षि दावने तवं विशिक्षुरसियज्ञमातनिः ||
2.1.e: A Ṛbhu art thou, Agni, near to be adored thou art the Sovran Lord of foodful spoil and wealth.  Thou shinest brightly forth, thou burnest to bestow: pervading sacrifice, thou lendest us thine help.

2.1.d: तवमग्ने अदितिर्देव दाशुषे तवं होत्रा भारती वर्धसेगिरा | तवमिळा षतहिमासि दक्षसे तवं वर्त्रहा वसुपते सरस्वती ||
2.1.e: Thou, God, art Aditi to him who offers gifts: thou, Hotrā, Bhāratī, art strengthened by the song.  Thou art the hundred-wintered Iḷā to give strength, Lord of Wealth! Vṛtra-slayer and Sarasvatī.

2.1.d: तवमग्ने सुभ्र्त उत्तमं वयस्तव सपार्हे वर्ण आ सन्द्र्शि शरियः | तवं वाजः परतरणो बर्हन्नसि तवं रयिर्बहुलो विश्वतस पर्थुः ||
2.1.e: Thou, Agni, cherished well, art highest vital power; in thy delightful hue are glories visible.  Thou art the lofty might that furthers each design: thou art wealth manifold, diffused on every side.

2.1.d: तवामग्न आदित्यास आस्यं तवां जिह्वां शुचयश्चक्रिरेकवे | तवां रातिषाचो अध्वरेषु सश्चिरे तवे देवा हविरदन्त्याहुतम ||
2.1.e: Thee, Agni, have the Ādityas taken as their mouth; the Bright Ones have made thee, O Sage, to be their tongue.  They who love offerings cling to thee at solemn rites: by thee the Gods devour the duly offered food.

2.1.d: तवे अग्ने विश्वे अन्र्तासो अद्रुह आसा देवा हविरदन्त्याहुतम | तवया मर्तासः सवदन्त आसुतिं तवं गर्भो वीरुधां जज्ञिषे शुचिः ||
2.1.e: By thee, O Agni, all the Immortal guileless Gods cat with thy mouth the oblation that is offered them.  By thee do mortal men give sweetness to their drink. Bright art thou born, the embryo of the plants of earth.

2.1.d: तवं तान सं च परति चासि मज्मनाग्ने सुजात पर च देवरिच्यसे | पर्क्षो यदत्र महिना वि ते भुवदनु दयावाप्र्थिवी रोदसी उभे ||
2.1.e: With these thou art united, Agni; yea thou, God of noble birth, surpassest them in majesty,  Which, through the power of good, here spreads abroad from thee, diffused through both the worlds, throughout the earth and heaven.

2.1.d: ये सतोत्र्भ्यो गोग्रामश्वपेशसमग्ने रातिमुपस्र्जन्ति सूरयः | अस्माञ्च तांश्च पर हि नेषि वस्य आ बर्हद वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ||
2.1.e: The princely worshippers who send to those who sing thy praise, O Agni, guerdon graced with kine and steeds,—  Lead thou both these and us forward to higher bliss. With brave men in the assembly may we speak aloud.

2.2.d: यज्ञेन वर्धत जातवेदसमग्निं यजध्वं हविषा तना गिरा | समिधानं सुप्रयसं सवर्णरं दयुक्षं होतारंव्र्जनेषु धूर्षदम ||
2.2.e: WITH sacrifice exalt Agni who knows all life; worship him with oblation and the song of praise,  Well kindled, nobly fed; heaven's Lord, Celestial Priest, who labours at the pole where deeds of might are done.

2.2.d: अभि तवा नक्तीरुषसो ववाशिरे.अग्ने वत्सं न सवसरेषुधेनवः | दिव इवेदरतिर्मानुषा युगा कषपो भासि पुरुवार संयतः ||
2.2.e: At night and morning, Agni, have they called to thee, like milch-kine in their stalls lowing to meet their young.  As messenger of heaven thou lightest all night long the families of men. Thou Lord of precious boons.

2.2.d: तं देवा बुध्ने रजसः सुदंससं दिवस्प्र्थिव्योररतिंन्येरिरे | रथमिव वेद्यं शुक्रशोचिषमग्निं मित्रं नक्षितिषु परशंस्यम ||
2.2.e: Him have the Gods established at the region's base, doer of wondrous deeds, Herald of heaven and earth;  Like a most famous car, Agni the purely bright, like Mitra to be glorified among the folk.

2.2.d: तमुक्षमाणं रजसि सव आ दमे चन्द्रमिव सुरुचं हवार आ दधुः | पर्श्न्याः पतरं चितयन्तमक्षभिः पाथो न पायुं जनसी उभे अनु ||
2.2.e: Him have they set in his own dwelling, in the vault, like the Moon waxing, fulgent, in the realm of air.  Bird of the firmament, observant with his eyes, guard of the place as ’twere, looking to Gods and men.

2.2.d: स होता विश्वं परि भूत्वध्वरं तमु हव्यैर्मनुष रञ्जते गिरा | हिरिशिप्रो वर्धसानासु जर्भुरद दयौर्न सत्र्भिश्चितयद रोदसी अनु ||
2.2.e: May he as Priest encompass all the sacrifice. men throng to him with offerings and with hymns of praise.  Raging with jaws of gold among the growing plants, like heaven with all the stars, he quickens earth and sky.

2.2.d: स नो रेवत समिधानः सवस्तये सन्ददस्वान रयिमस्मासु दीदिहि | आ नः कर्णुष्व सुविताय रोदसी अग्ने हव्या मनुषोदेव वीतये ||
2.2.e: Such as thou art, brilliantly kindled for our weal, a liberal giver, send us riches in thy shine,  For our advantage, Agni, God, bring Heaven and Earth hither that they may taste oblation brought by man.

2.2.d: दा नो अग्ने बर्हतो दाः सहस्रिणो दुरो न वाजं शरुत्या अपा वर्धि | पराची दयावाप्र्थिवी बरह्मणा कर्धि सवर्ण शुक्रमुषसो वि दिद्युतः ||
2.2.e: Agni, give us great wealth, give riches thousandfold. unclose to us, like doors, strength that shall bring renown.  Make Heaven and Earth propitious through the power of prayer, and like the sky's bright sheen let mornings beam on us.

2.2.d: स इधान उषसो राम्या अनु सवर्ण दीदेदरुषेण भानुना | होत्राभिरग्निर्मनुषः सवध्वरो राजा विशामतिथिश्चारुरायवे ||
2.2.e: Enkindled night by night at every morning's dawn, may he shine forth with red flame like the realm of light,—  Agni adored in beauteous rites with lauds of men, fair guest of living man and King of all our folk.

2.2.d: एवा नो अग्ने अम्र्तेषु पूर्व्य धीष पीपाय बर्हद्दिवेषु मानुषा | दुहाना धेनुर्व्र्जनेषु कारवे तमना शतिनं पुरुरूपमिषणि ||
2.2.e: Song chanted by us men, O Agni, Ancient One, has swelled unto the deathless Gods in lofty heaven—  A milch-cow yielding to the singer in the rites wealth manifold, in hundreds, even as he wills.

2.2.d: वयमग्ने अर्वता वा सुवीर्यं बरह्मणा वा चितयेमा जनानति | अस्माकं दयुम्नमधि पञ्च कर्ष्टिषूच्चा सवर्णशुशुचीत दुष्टरम ||
2.2.e: Agni, may we show forth our valour with the steed or with the power of prayer beyond all other men;  And over the Five Races let our glory shine high like the realm of light and unsurpassable.

2.2.d: स नो बोधि सहस्य परशंस्यो यस्मिन सुजाता इषयन्त सूरयः | यमग्ने यज्ञमुपयन्ति वाजिनो नित्ये तोके दीदिवांसं सवे दमे ||
2.2.e: Such, Conqueror! be to us, be worthy of our praise, thou for whom princes nobly born exert themselves;  Whose sacrifice the strong seek, Agni, when it shines for never-failing offspring in thine own abode.

2.2.d: उभयासो जातवेदः सयाम ते सतोतारो अग्ने सूरयश्च शर्मणि | वस्वो रायः पुरुश्चन्द्रस्य भूयसः परजावतः सवपत्यस्य शग्धि नः ||
2.2.e: Knower of all that lives, O Agni may we both, singers of praise and chiefs, be in thy keeping still.  Help us to wealth exceeding good and glorious, abundant, rich in children and their progeny.

The princely worshippers who send to those who sing thy praise, O Agni, guerdon, graced with kine and steeds,—  Lead thou both these and us forward to higher bliss. With brave men in the assembly may we speak aloud.

2.3.d: समिद्धो अग्निर्निहितः पर्थिव्यां परत्यं विश्वानि भुवनान्यस्थात | होता पावकः परदिवः सुमेधा देवो देवान यजत्वग्निरर्हन ||
2.3.e: AGNI is set upon the earth well kindled; he standeth in the presence of all beings.  Wise, ancient, God, the Priest and Purifier, let Agni serve the Gods for he is worthy.

2.3.d: नराशंसः परति धामान्यञ्जन तिस्रो दिवः परति मह्ना सवर्चिः | घर्तप्रुषा मनसा हव्यमुन्दन मूर्धन यज्ञस्य समनक्तु देवान ||
