2.3.e: May Narāśaṁsa lighting up the chambers, bright in his majesty through threefold heaven,  Steeping the gift with oil diffusing purpose, bedew the Gods at chiefest time of worship.

2.3.d: ईळितो अग्ने मनसा नो अर्हन देवान यक्षि मानुषात पूर्वो अद्य | स आ वह मरुतां शर्धो अच्युतमिन्द्रं नरो बर्हिषदं यजध्वम ||
2.3.e: Adored in heart, as is thy right, O Agni, serve the Gods first to-day before the mortal.  Bring thou the Marut host. Ye men do worship to Indra seated on the grass, eternal.

2.3.d: देव बर्हिर्वर्धमानं सुवीरं सतीर्णं राये सुभरं वेद्यस्याम | घर्तेनाक्तं वसवः सीदतेदं विश्वे देवा आदित्या यज्ञियासः ||
2.3.e: O Grass divine, increasing, rich in heroes, strewn for wealth's sake, well laid upon this altar,—  On this bedewed with oil sit ye, O Vasus, sit all ye Gods, ye Holy, ye Ādityas.

2.3.d: वि शरयन्तामुर्विया हूयमाना दवारो देवीः सुप्रायणा नमोभिः | वयचस्वतीर्वि परथन्तामजुर्या वर्णं पुनानायशसं सुवीरम ||
2.3.e: Wide be the Doors, the Goddesses, thrown open, easy to pass, invoked, through adorations,  Let them unfold, expansive, everlasting, that sanctify the class famed, rich in heroes.

2.3.d: साध्वपांसि सनता न उक्षिते उषासानक्ता वय्येव रण्विते | तन्तुं ततं संवयन्ती समीची यज्ञस्य पेशः सुदुघे पयस्वती ||
2.3.e: Good work for us, the glorious Night and Morning, like female weavers, waxen from aforetime,  Yielders of rich milk, interweave in concert the long-extended thread, the web of worship.

2.3.d: दैव्या होतारा परथमा विदुष्टर रजु यक्षतः सं रचावपुष्टरा | देवान यजन्ताव रतुथा समञ्जतो नाभा पर्थिव्या अधि सानुषु तरिषु ||
2.3.e: Let the two heavenly Heralds, first, most wise, most fair, present oblation duly with the sacred verse,  Worshipping God at ordered seasons decking them at three high places at the centre of the earth.

2.3.d: सरस्वती साधयन्ती धियं न इळा देवी भारती विश्वतूर्तिः | तिस्रो देवीः सवधया बर्हिरेदमछिद्रं पान्तुशरणं निषद्य ||
2.3.e: Sarasvatī who perfects our devotion, Iḷā divine, Bhāratī all surpassing,—  Three Goddesses, with power inherent, seated, protect this holy Grass, our flawless refuge!

2.3.d: पिशङगरूपः सुभरो वयोधाः शरुष्टी वीरो जायते देवकामः | परजां तवष्टा वि षयतु नाभिमस्मे अथा देवानामप्येतु पाथः ||
2.3.e: Born is the pious hero swift of hearing, like gold in hue, well formed, and full of vigour.  May Tvaṣṭar lengthen our line and kindred, and may they reach the place which Gods inhabit.

2.3.d: वनस्पतिरवस्र्जन्नुप सथादग्निर्हविः सूदयाति पर धीभिः | तरिधा समक्तं नयतु परजानन देवेभ्यो दैव्यः शमितोप हव्यम ||
2.3.e: Vanaspati shall stand anear and start us, and Agni with his arts prepare oblation.  Let the skilled heavenly Immolator forward unto the Gods the offering thrice anointed.

2.3.d: घर्तं मिमिक्षे घर्तमस्य योनिर्घ्र्ते शरितो घर्तं वस्य धाम | अनुष्वधमा वह मादयस्व सवाहाक्र्तं वर्षभ वक्षि हव्यम ||
2.3.e: Oil has been mixt: oil is his habitation. In oil he rests: oil is his proper province.  Come as thy wont is: O thou Steer, rejoice thee; bear off the oblation duly consecrated.

2.4.d: हुवे वः सुद्योत्मानं सुव्र्क्तिं विशामग्निमतिथिं सुप्रयसम | मित्र इव यो दिधिषाय्यो भूद देव आदेवे जने जातवेदाः ||
2.4.e: FOR you I call the glorious refulgent Agni, the guest of men, rich in oblations  Whom all must strive to win even as a lover, God among godly people, Jātavedas.

2.4.d: इमं विधन्तो अपां सधस्थे दवितादधुर्भ्र्गवो विक्ष्वायोः | एष विश्वान्यभ्यस्तु भूमा देवानामग्निररतिर्जीराश्वः ||
2.4.e: Bhṛgus who served him in the home of waters set him of old in houses of the living.  Over all worlds let Agni be the Sovran, the messenger of Gods with rapid coursers.

2.4.d: अग्निं देवासो मानुषीषु विक्षु परियं धुः कषेष्यन्तो नमित्रम | स दीदयदुशतीरूर्म्या आ दक्षाय्यो यो दास्वते दम आ ||
2.4.e: Among the tribes of men the Gods placed Agni as a dear Friend when they would dwell among them.  Against the longing nights may he shine brightly, and show the offerer in the house his vigour.

2.4.d: अस्य रण्वा सवस्येव पुष्टिः सन्द्र्ष्टिरस्य हियानस्य दक्षोः | वि यो भरिभ्रदोषधीषु जिह्वामत्यो न रथ्यो दोधवीति वारान ||
2.4.e: Sweet is his growth as of one's own possessions; his look when rushing fain to burn is lovely.  He darts his tongue forth, like a harnessed courser who shakes his flowing tail, among the bushes.

2.4.d: आ यन मे अभ्वं वनदः पनन्तोशिग्भ्यो नामिमीत वर्णम | स चित्रेण चिकिते रंसु भासा जुजुर्वान यो मुहुरा युवा भूत ||
2.4.e: Since they who honour me have praised my greatness,—he gave, as ’twere, his hue to those who love him.  Known is he by his bright delightful splendour, and waxing old renews his youth for ever.

2.4.d: आ यो वना तात्र्षाणो न भाति वार्ण पथा रथ्येवस्वानीत | कर्ष्णाध्वा तपू रण्वश्चिकेत दयौरिव समयमानो नभोभिः ||
2.4.e: Like one athirst, he lighteth up the forests; like water down the chariot ways he roareth.  On his black path he shines in burning beauty, marked as it were the heaven that smiles through vapour.

2.4.d: स यो वयस्थादभि दक्षदुर्वीं पशुर्नैति सवयुरगोपाः | अग्निः शोचिष्मानतसान्युष्णन कर्ष्णव्यथिरस्वदयन न भूम ||
2.4.e: Around, consuming the broad earth, he wanders, free roaming like an ox without a herdsman,—  Agni refulgent, burning up the bushes, with blackened lines, as though the earth he seasoned.

2.4.d: नू ते पूर्वस्यावसो अधीतौ तर्तीये विदथे मन्म शंसि | अस्मे अग्ने संयद्वीरं बर्हन्तं कषुमन्तं वाजं सवपत्यंरयिं दाः ||
2.4.e: I, in remembrance of thine ancient favour have sung my hymn in this our third assembly.  O Agni, give us wealth with store of heroes and mighty strength in food and noble offspring.

2.4.d: तवया यथा गर्त्समदासो अग्ने गुहा वन्वन्त उपरानभि षयुः | सुवीरासो अभिमातिषाहः समत सूरिभ्यो गर्णते तद वयो धाः ||
2.4.e: May the Gṛtsamadas, serving in secret, through thee, O Agni, overcome their neighbours,  Rich in good heroes and subduing foemen. That vital power give thou to chiefs and singers.

2.5.d: होताजनिष्ट चेतनः पिता पित्र्भ्य ऊतये | परयक्षञ जेन्यं वसु शकेम वाजिनो यमम ||
2.5.e: HERALD and teacher was he born, a guardian for our patrons’ help,  Earner by rites of noble wealth. That Strong One may we grasp and guide;

2.5.d: आ यस्मिन सप्त रश्मयस्तता यज्ञस्य नेतरि | मनुष्वद दैव्यमष्टमं पोता विश्वं तदिन्वति ||
2.5.e: In whom, Leader of sacrifice, the seven reins, far extended, meet;  Who furthers, man-like, eighth in place, as Cleanser, all the work divine.

2.5.d: दधन्वे वा यदीमनु वोचद बरह्माणि वेरु तत | परि विश्वानि काव्या नेमिश्चक्रमिवाभवत ||
2.5.e: When swift he follows this behest, bird-like he chants the holy prayers.  He holds all knowledge in his grasp even as the felly rounds the wheel.

2.5.d: साकं हि शुचिना शुचिः परशास्ता करतुनाजनि | विद्वानस्य वरता धरुवा वया इवानु रोहते ||
2.5.e: Together with pure mental power, pure, as Director, was he born.  Skilled in his own unchanging laws he waxes like the growing boughs.

2.5.d: ता अस्य वर्णमायुवो नेष्टुः सचन्त धेनवः | कुवित तिस्र्भ्य आ वरं सवसारो या इदं ययुः ||
2.5.e: Clothing them in his hues, the kine of him the Leader wait on him.  Is he not better than the Three, the Sisters who have come to us?

2.5.d: यदी मातुरुप सवसा घर्तं भरन्त्यस्थित | तासामध्वर्युरागतौ यवो वर्ष्टीव मोदते ||
2.5.e: When, laden with the holy oil, the  Sister  by the Mother stands,  The Priest delights in their approach, as corn at coming of the rain.

2.5.d: सवः सवाय धायसे कर्णुतां रत्विग रत्विजम | सतोमं यज्ञं चादरं वनेमा ररिमा वयम ||
2.5.e: For his support let him perform as ministrant his priestly task;  Yea, song of praise and sacrifice: we have bestowed, let us obtain.

2.5.d: यथ विद्वानरं करद विश्वेभ्यो यजतेभ्यः अयमग्ने तवे अपि यं यज्ञं चक्र्मा वयम ||
2.5.e: That so this man well skilled, may pay worship to all the Holy Ones.  And, Agni, this our sacrifice which we have here prepared, to thee.

2.6.d: इमां मे अग्ने समिधमिमामुपसदं वनेः | इमा उ षु शरुधी गिरः ||
2.6.e: AGNI, accept this flaming brand, this waiting with my prayer on thee:  Hear graciously these songs of praise.

2.6.d: अया ते अग्ने विधेमोर्जो नपादश्वमिष्टे | एना सूक्तेन सुजात ||
2.6.e: With this hymn let us honour thee, seeker of horses, Son of Strength,  With this fair hymn, thou nobly born.

2.6.d: तं तवा गीर्भिर्गिर्वणसं दरविणस्युं दरविणोदः | सपर्येम सपर्यवः ||
2.6.e: As such, lover of song, with songs, wealth-lover, giver of our wealth!  With reverence let us worship thee.

2.6.d: स बोधि सूरिर्मघवा वसुपते वसुदावन | युयोध्यस्मद दवेषांसि ||
2.6.e: Be thou for us a liberal Prince, giver and Lord of precious things.  Drive those who hate us far away.

2.6.d: स नो वर्ष्तिं दिवस परि स नो वाजमनर्वाणम | स नः सहस्रिणीरिषः ||
2.6.e: Such as thou art, give rain from heaven, give strength which no man may resist:  Give food exceeding plentiful.

2.6.d: ईळानायावस्यवे यविष्ठ दूत नो गिरा | यजिष्ठ होतरा गहि ||
2.6.e: To him who lauds thee, craving help, most youthful envoy! through our song,  Most holy Herald! come thou nigh.

2.6.d: अन्तर्ह्यग्न ईयसे विद्वान जन्मोभया कवे | दूतो जन्येवमित्र्यः ||
2.6.e: Between both races, Agni, Sage, well skilled thou passest to and fro,  As envoy friendly to mankind.

2.6.d: स विद्वाना च पिप्रयो यक्षि चिकित्व आनुषक | आ चास्मिन सत्सि बर्हिषि ||
2.6.e: Befriend us thou as knowing all. Sage, duly worship thou the Gods,  And seat thee on this sacred grass.

2.7.d: शरेष्ठं यविष्ठ भारताग्ने दयुमन्तमा भर | वसो पुरुस्प्र्हं रयिम ||
2.7.e: VASU, thou most youthful God, Bhārata, Agni, bring us wealth,  Excellent, splendid, much-desired.

2.7.d: मा नो अरातिरीशत देवस्य मर्त्यस्य च | पर्षि तस्या उतद्विषः ||
2.7.e: Let no malignity prevail against us, either God's or man's.  Save us from this and enmity.

2.7.d: विश्वा उत तवया वयं धारा उदन्या इव | अति गाहेमहि दविषः ||
2.7.e: So through thy favour may we force through all our enemies a way,  As ’twere through streaming water-floods.

2.7.d: शुचिः पावक वन्द्यो.अग्ने बर्हद वि रोचसे | तवं घर्तेभिराहुतः ||
2.7.e: Thou, Purifier Agni, high shinest forth, bright, adorable,  When worshipped with the sacred oil.

2.7.d: तवं नो असि भारताग्ने वशाभिरुक्षभिः | अष्टापदीभिराहुतः ||
2.7.e: Ours art thou, Agni, Bhārata, honoured by us with barren cows,  With bullocks and with kine in calf

2.7.d: दर्वन्नः सर्पिरासुतिः परत्नो होता वरेण्यः | सहसस पुत्रो अद्भुतः ||
2.7.e: Wood-fed, bedewed with sacred oil, ancient, Invoker, excellent,  The Son of Strength, the Wonderful.

2.8.d: वाजयन्निव नू रथान योगानग्नेरुप सतुहि | यशस्तमस्य मीळ्हुषः ||
2.8.e: Now praise, as one who strives for strength, the harnessing of Agni's car,  The liberal, the most splendid One;
Who, guiding worshippers aright, withers, untouched by age, the foe:  When worshipped fair to look upon;

2.8.d: य उ शरिया दमेष्वा दोषोषसि परशस्यते | यस्य वरतं न मीयते ||
2.8.e: Who for his glory is extolled at eve and morning in our homes,  Whose statute is inviolate;

2.8.d: आ यः सवर्ण भानुना चित्रो विभात्यर्चिषा | अञ्जानोजरैरभि ||
2.8.e: Who shines refulgent like the Sun, with brilliance and with fiery flame,  Decked with imperishable sheen.

2.8.d: अत्रिमनु सवराज्यमग्निमुक्थानि वाव्र्धुः | विश्वा अधि शरियो दधे ||
2.8.e: Him Atri, Agni, have our songs Strengthened according to his sway:  All glories hath he made his own.

2.8.d: अग्नेरिन्द्रस्य सोमस्य देवानामूतिभिर्वयम | अरिष्यन्तःसचेमह्यभि षयाम पर्तन्यतः ||
2.8.e: May we with Agni's, Indra's help, with Soma's, yea, of all the Gods,  Uninjured dwell together still, and conquer those who fight with us.

2.9.d: नि होता होत्र्षदने विदानस्त्वेषो दीदिवानसदत सुदक्षः | अदब्धव्रतप्रमतिर्वसिष्ठः सहस्रम्भरः शुचिजिह्वो अग्निः ||
2.9.e: ACCUSTOMED to the Herald's place, the Herald hath seated him, bright, splendid, passing mighty,  Whose foresight keeps the Law from violation, excellent, pure-tongued, bringing thousands, Agni.

2.9.d: तवं दूतस्त्वमु नः परस्पास्त्वं वस्य आ वर्षभ परणेता | अग्ने तोकस्य नस्तने तनूनामप्रयुछन दीद्यद बोधि गोपाः ||
2.9.e: Envoy art thou, protector from the foeman, strong God, thou leadest us to higher blessings.  Refulgent, be an ever-heedful keeper, Agni, for us and for our seed offspring.

2.9.d: विधेम ते परमे जन्मन्नग्ने विधेम सतोमैरवरे सधस्थे | यस्माद योनेरुदारिथा यजे तं पर तवे हवींषि जुहुरेसमिद्धे ||
2.9.e: May we adore thee in thy loftiest birthplace, and, with our praises, in thy lower station.  The place whence thou issued forth I worship: to thee well kindled have they paid oblations.

2.9.d: अग्ने यजस्व हविषा यजीयाञ्छ्रुष्टी देष्णमभि गर्णीहि राधः | तवं हयसि रयिपती रयीणां तवं शुक्रस्य वचसो मनोता ||
2.9.e: Agni, best Priest, pay worship with oblation; quickly commend the gift to be presented;  For thou art Lord of gathered wealth and treasure. of the bright song of praise thou art inventor.

2.9.d: उभयं ते न कषीयते वसव्यं दिवे-दिवे जायमानस्य दस्म | कर्धि कषुमन्तं जरितारमग्ने कर्धि पतिं सवपत्यस्य रायः ||
2.9.e: The twofold opulence, O Wonder-Worker, of thee new-born each day never decreases.  Enrich with food the man who lauds thee, Agni: make him the lord of wealth with noble offspring.

2.9.d: सैनानीकेन सुविदत्रो अस्मे यष्टा देवानायजिष्ठः सवस्ति | अदब्धो गोपा उत नः परस्पा अग्ने दयुमदुत रेवद दिदीहि ||
2.9.e: May he, benevolent with this fair aspect, best sacrificer, bring the Gods to bless us.  Sure guardian, our protector from the foemen, shine, Agni, with thine affluence and splendour.

2.10.d: जोहूत्रो अग्निः परथमः पितेवेळस पदे मनुषा यत समिद्धः | शरियं वसानो अम्र्तो विचेता मर्म्र्जेन्यः शरवस्यःस वाजी ||
2.10.e: AGNI, first, loudly calling, like a Father, kindled by man upon the seat of worship.  Clothed in his glory, deathless, keen of insight, must be adorned by all, the Strong, the Famous.

2.10.d: शरूया अग्निश्चित्रभानुर्हवं मे विश्वाभिर्गीर्भिरम्र्तो विचेताः | शयावा रथं वहतो रोहिता वोतारुषाह चक्रे विभ्र्त्रः ||
2.10.e: May Agni the resplendent hear my calling through all my songs, Immortal, keen of insight.  Dark steeds or ruddy draw his car, or carried in sundry ways he makes them red of colour.

2.10.d: उत्तानायामजनयन सुषूतं भुवदग्निः पुरुपेशासु गर्भः | शिरिणायां चिदक्तुना महोभिरपरीव्र्तो वसति परचेताः ||
2.10.e: On wood supine they got the well-formed Infant: a germ in various-fashioned plants was Agni;  And in the night, not compassed round by darkness, he dwells exceeding wise, with rays of splendour.

2.10.d: जिघर्म्यग्निं हविषा घर्तेन परतिक्षियन्तं भुवनानि विश्वा | पर्थुं तिरश्चा वयसा बर्हन्तं वयचिष्ठमन्नै रभसं दर्शानम ||
2.10.e: With oil and sacred gifts I sprinkle Agni who makes his home in front of all things living,  Broad, vast, through vital power o’er all expanded, conspicuous, strong with all the food that feeds him.

2.10.d: आ विश्वतः परत्यञ्चं जिघर्म्यरक्षसा मनसा तज्जुषेत | मर्यश्रीः सप्र्हयद्वर्णो अग्निर्नाभिम्र्शे तन्वा जर्भुराणः ||
2.10.e: I pour to him who looks in all directions: may he accept it with a friendly spirit.  Agni with bridegroom's grace and lovely colour may not be touched when all his form is fury.

2.10.d: जञेया भागं सहसानो वरेण तवादूतासो मनुवद वदेम | अनूनमग्निं जुह्वा वचस्या मधुप्र्चं धनसाजोहवीमि ||
2.10.e: By choice victorious, recognize thy portion: with thee for envoy may we speak like Manu.  Obtaining wealth, I call on perfect Agni who with an eloquent tongue dispenses sweetness.

2.11.d: शरुधी हवमिन्द्र मा रिशण्यः सयाम ते दावने वसूनाम | इमा हि तवामूर्जो वर्धयन्ति वसूयवः सिन्धवो न कषरन्तः ||
2.11.e: HEAR thou my call, O Indra; be not heedless: thine may we be for thee to give us treasures;  For these presented viands, seeking riches, increase thy strength like streams of water flowing.

2.11.d: सर्जो महीरिन्द्र या अपिन्वः परिष्ठिता अहिना शूर पूर्वीः | अमर्त्यं चिद दासं मन्यमानमवाभिनदुक्थैर्वाव्र्धानः ||
2.11.e: Floods great and many, compassed by the Dragon, thou badest swell and settest free, O Hero.  Strengthened by songs of praise thou rentest piecemeal the Dāsa, him who deemed himself immortal.

2.11.d: उक्थेष्विन नु शूर येषु चाकन सतोमेष्विन्द्र रुद्रियेषु च | तुभ्येदेता यासु मन्दसानः पर वायवे सिस्रते न शुभ्राः ||
2.11.e: For, Hero, in the lauds wherein thou joyedst, in hymns of praise, O Indra, songs of Rudras,  These streams in which is thy delight approach thee, even as the brilliant ones draw near to Vāyu.

2.11.d: शुभ्रं नु ते शुष्मं वर्धयन्तः शुभ्रं वज्रं बाह्वोर्दधानाः | शुभ्रस्त्वमिन्द्र वाव्र्धानो अस्मे दासीर्विशः सूर्येण सह्याः ||
2.11.e: We who add strength to thine own splendid vigour, laying within thine arms the splendid thunder—  With us mayst thou, O Indra, waxen splendid, with Sūrya overcome the Dāsa races.

2.11.d: गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्हमप्स्वपीव्र्तं मायिनं कषियन्तम | उतो अपो दयां तस्तभ्वांसमहन्नहिं शूर वीर्येण ||
2.11.e: Hero, thou slewest in thy valour Ahi concealed in depths, mysterious, great enchanter,  Dwelling enveloped deep within the waters, him who checked heaven and stayed the floods from flowing.

2.11.d: सतवा नु त इन्द्र पूर्व्या महान्युत सतवाम नूतना कर्तानि | सतवा वज्रं बाह्वोरुशन्तं सतवा हरी सूर्यस्य केतू ||
2.11.e: Indra, we laud thy great deeds wrought aforetime, we laud thine exploits later of achievement;  We laud the bolt that in thine arms lies eager; we laud thy two Bay Steeds, heralds of Sūrya.

2.11.d: हरी नु त इन्द्र वाजयन्ता घर्तश्चुतं सवारमस्वार्ष्टाम | वि समना भूमिरप्रथिष्टारंस्त पर्वतश्चित सरिष्यन ||
2.11.e: Indra, thy Bay Steeds showing forth their vigour have sent a loud cry out that droppeth fatness.  The earth hath spread herself in all her fulness: the cloud that was about to move hath rested.

2.11.d: नि पर्वतः साद्यप्रयुछन सं मात्र्भिर्वावशानो अक्रान | दूरे पारे वाणीं वर्धयन्त इन्द्रेषितां धमनिं पप्रथन नि ||
2.11.e: Down, never ceasing, hath the rain-cloud settled: bellowing, it hath wandered with the Mothers.  Swelling the roar in the far distant limits, they have spread wide the blast sent forth by Indra.

2.11.d: इन्द्रो महां सिन्धुमाशयानं मायाविनं वर्त्रमस्फुरन निः | अरेजेतां रोदसी भियाने कनिक्रदतो वर्ष्णो अस्य वज्रात ||
2.11.e: Indra hath hurled down the magician Vṛtra who lay beleaguering the mighty river.  Then both the heaven and earth trembled in terror at the strong Hero's thunder when he bellowed.

2.11.d: अरोरवीद वर्ष्णो अस्य वज्रो.अमानुषं यन मानुषो निजूर्वात | नि मायिनो दानवस्य माया अपादयत पपिवान सुतस्य ||
2.11.e: Loud roared the mighty Hero's bolt of thunder, when he, the Friend of man, burnt up the monster,  And, having drunk his fill of flowing Soma, baffled the guileful Dānava's devices.

2.11.d: पिबा-पिबेदिन्द्र शूर सोमं मन्दन्तु तवा मन्दिनः सुतासः | पर्णन्तस्ते कुक्षी वर्धयन्त्वित्था सुतः पौर इन्द्रमाव ||
2.11.e: Drink thou, O Hero Indra, drink the Soma; let the joy-giving juices make thee joyful.  They, filling both thy flanks, shall swell thy vigour. The juice that satisfies hath helped Indra.

2.11.d: तवे इन्द्राप्यभूम विप्रा धियं वनेम रतया सपन्तः | अवस्यवो धीमहि परशस्तिं सद्यस्ते रायो दावने सयाम ||
2.11.e: Singers have we become with thee, O Indra: may we serve duly and prepare devotion.  Seeking thy help we meditate thy praises: may we at once enjoy thy gift of riches.

2.11.d: सयाम ते त इन्द्र ये त ऊती अवस्यव ऊर्जं वर्धयन्तः | शुष्मिन्तमं यं चाकनाम देवास्मे रयिं रासि वीरवन्तम ||
2.11.e: May we be thine, such by thy help, O Indra, as swell thy vigour while they seek thy favour.  Give us, thou God, the riches that we long for, most powerful, with stare of noble children.

2.11.d: रासि कषयं रासि मित्रमस्मे रासि शर्ध इन्द्र मारुतंनः | सजोषसो ये च मन्दसानाः पर वायवः पान्त्यग्रणीतिम ||
2.11.e: Give us a friend, give us an habitation; Indra, give us the company of Maruts,  And those whose minds accord with theirs, the Vāyus, who drink the first libation of the Soma.

2.11.d: वयन्त्विन नु येषु मन्दसानस्त्र्पत सोमं पाहि दरह्यदिन्द्र | अस्मान सु पर्त्स्वा तरुत्रावर्धयो दयां बर्हद्भिरर्कैः ||
2.11.e: Let those enjoy in whom thou art delighted. Indra, drink Soma for thy strength and gladness.  Thou hast exalted us to heaven, Preserver, in battles, through the lofty hymns that praise thee.

2.11.d: बर्हन्त इन नु ये ते तरुत्रोक्थेभिर्वा सुम्नमाविवासान | सत्र्णानासो बर्हिः पस्त्यावत तवोता इदिन्द्र वाजमग्मन ||
2.11.e: Great, verily, are they, O thou Protector, who by their songs of praise have won the blessing.  They who strew sacred grass to be thy dwelling, helped by thee have got them strength, O Indra.

2.11.d: उग्रेष्विन नु शूर मन्दसानस्त्रिकद्रुकेषु पाहि सोममिन्द्र | परदोधुवच्छ्मश्रुषु परीणानो याहि हरिभ्यां सुतस्यपीतिम ||
2.11.e: Upon the great Trikadruka days, Hero, rejoicing thee, O Indra, drink the Soma.  Come with Bay Steeds to drink of libation, shaking the drops from out thy beard, contented.

2.11.d: धिष्वा शवः शूर येन वर्त्रमवाभिनद दानुमौर्णवाभम | अपाव्र्णोर्ज्योतिरार्याय नि सव्यतः सादि दस्युरिन्द्र ||
2.11.e: Hero, assume the might wherewith thou clavest Vṛtra piecemeal, the Dānava Aurṇavābha.  Thou hast disclosed the light to light the Ārya: on thy left hand, O Indra, sank the Dasyu.

2.11.d: सनेम ये त ऊतिभिस्तरन्तो विश्वा सप्र्ध आर्येण दस्यून | अस्मभ्यं तत तवाष्ट्रं विश्वरूपमरन्धयः साख्यस्य तरिताय ||
2.11.e: May we gain wealth, subduing with thy succour and with the Ārya, all our foes, the Dasyus.  Our gain was that to Tṛta of our party thou gavest up Tvaṣṭar's son Viśvarūpa.

2.11.d: अस्य सुवानस्य मन्दिनस्त्रितस्य नयर्बुदं वाव्र्धानो अस्तः | अवर्तयत सूर्यो न चक्रं भिनद वलमिन्द्रो अङगिरस्वान ||
2.11.e: He cast down Arbuda what time his vigour was strengthened by libations poured by Tṛta.  Indra sent forth his whirling wheel like Sūrya, and aided by the Aṅgirases rent Vala.

2.11.d: नूनं सा ते परति वरं जरित्रे दुहीयदिन्द्र दक्षिणा मघोनी | शिक्षा सतोत्र्भ्यो माति धग भगो नो बर्हद वदेम व. स. ||
2.11.e: Now let that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, yield in return a boon to him who lauds thee.  Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with brave men, in the assembly.

2.12.d: यो जात एव परथमो मनस्वान देवो देवान करतुना पर्यभूषत | यस्य शुष्माद रोदसी अभ्यसेतां नर्म्णस्य मह्ना स जनास इन्द्रः ||
2.12.e: HE who, just born, chief God of lofty spirit by power and might became the Gods’ protector,  Before whose breath through greatness of his valour the two worlds trembled, He, O men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यः पर्थिवीं वयथमानामद्रंहद यः पर्वतान परकुपितानरम्णात | यो अन्तरिक्षं विममे वरीयो यो दयामस्तभ्नात स जनास इन्द्रः ||
2.12.e: He who fixed fast and firm the earth that staggered, and set at rest the agitated mountains,  Who measured out the air's wide middle region and gave the heaven support, He, men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यो हत्वाहिमरिणात सप्त सिन्धून यो गा उदाजदपधा वलस्य | यो अश्मनोरन्तरग्निं जजान संव्र्क समत्सु स. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: Who slew the Dragon, freed the Seven Rivers, and drove the kine forth from the cave of Vala,  Begat the fire between two stones, the spoiler in warriors’ battle, He, O men, is Indra.

2.12.d: येनेमा विश्वा चयवना कर्तानि यो दासं वर्णमधरंगुहाकः | शवघ्नीव यो जिगीवान लक्षमाददर्यः पुष्टानि स. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: By whom this universe was made to tremble, who chased away the humbled brood of demons,  Who, like a gambler gathering his winnings seized the foe's riches, He, O men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यं समा पर्छन्ति कुह सेति घोरमुतेमाहुर्नैषो अस्तीत्येनम | सो अर्यः पुष्तीर्विज इवा मिनाति शरदस्मै धत्तस. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: Of whom, the Terrible, they ask, Where is He? or verily they say of him, He is not.  He sweeps away, like birds, the foe's possessions. Have faith in him, for He, O men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यो रध्रस्य चोदिता यः कर्शस्य यो बरह्मणो नाधमानस्यकीरेः | युक्तग्राव्णो यो.अविता सुशिप्रः सुतसोमस्य स. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: Stirrer to action of the poor and lowly, of priest, of suppliant who sings his praises;  Who, fair-faced, favours him who presses Soma with stones made ready, He, O men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यस्याश्वासः परदिशि यस्य गावो यस्य गरामा यस्य विश्वे रथासः | यः सूर्यं य उषसं जजान यो अपां नेता स. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: He under whose supreme control are horses, all chariots, and the villages, and cattle;  He who gave being to the Sun and Morning, who leads the waters, He, O men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यं करन्दसी संयती विह्वयेते परे.अवर उभया अमित्राः | समानं चिद रथमातस्थिवांसा नाना हवेते स. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: To whom two armies cry in close encounter, both enemies, the stronger and the weaker;  Whom two invoke upon one chariot mounted, each for himself, He, O ye men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यस्मान न रते विजयन्ते जनासो यं युध्यमाना अवसे हवन्ते | यो विश्वस्य परतिमानं बभूव यो अच्युतच्युत स. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: Without whose help our people never conquer; whom, battling, they invoke to give them succour;  He of whom all this world is but the copy, who shakes things moveless, He, O men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यः शश्वतो मह्येनो दधानानमन्यमानाञ्छर्वा जघान | यः शर्धते नानुददाति शर्ध्यां यो दस्योर्हन्तास. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: He who hath smitten, ere they knew their danger, with his hurled weapon many grievous sinners;  Who pardons not his boldness who provokes him, who slays the Dasyu, He, O men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यः शम्बरं पर्वतेषु कषियन्तं चत्वारिंश्यां शरद्यन्वविन्दत | ओजायमानं यो अहिं जघान दानुं शयानंस. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: He who discovered in the fortieth autumn Śambara as he dwelt among the mountains;  Who slew the Dragon putting forth his vigour, the demon lying there, He, men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यः सप्तरश्मिर्व्र्षभस्तुविष्मानवास्र्जत सर्तवे सप्तसिन्धून | यो रौहिणमस्फुरद वज्रबाहुर्द्यामारोहन्तंस. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: Who with seven guiding reins, the Bull, the Mighty, set free the Seven great Floods to flow at pleasure;  Who, thunder-armed, rent Rauhiṇa in pieces when scaling heaven, He, O ye men, is Indra.

2.12.d: दयावा चिदस्मै पर्थिवी नमेते शुष्माच्चिदस्य पर्वता भयन्ते | यः सोमपा निचितो वज्रबाहुर्यो वज्रहस्तः स. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: Even the Heaven and Earth bow down before him, before his very breath the mountains tremble.  Known as the Soma-drinker, armed with thunder, who wields the bolt, He, O ye men, is Indra.

2.12.d: यः सुन्वन्तमवति यः पचन्तं यः शंसन्तं यः शशमानमूती | यस्य बरह्म वर्धनं यस्य सोमो यस्येदं राधः स. ज. इ. ||
2.12.e: Who aids with favour him who pours the Soma and him who brews it, sacrificer, singer.  Whom prayer exalts, and pouring forth of Soma, and this our gift, He, O ye men, Is Indra.

2.12.d: यः सुन्वते पचते दुध्र आ चिद वाजं दर्दर्षि स किलासि सत्यः | वयं त इन्द्र विश्वह परियासः सुवीरासो विदथमा वदेम ||
2.12.e: Thou verily art fierce and true who sendest strength to the man who brews and pours libation.  So may we evermore, thy friends, O Indra, speak loudly to the synod with our heroes.

2.13.d: रतुर्जनित्री तस्या अपस परि मक्षू जात आविशद यासु वर्धते | तदाहना अभवत पिप्युषी पयो.अंशोः पीयूषं परथमं तदुक्थ्यम ||
2.13.e: THE Season was the parent, and when born therefrom it entered rapidly the floods wherein it grows.  Thence was it full of sap, streaming with milky juice: the milk of the plant's stalk is chief and meet for lauds.

2.13.d: सध्रीमा यन्ति परि बिभ्रतीः पयो विश्वप्स्न्याय पर भरन्त भोजनम | समानो अध्वा परवतामनुष्यदे यस्ताक्र्णोः परथमं सास्युक्थ्यः ||
2.13.e: They come trooping together bearing milk to him, and bring him sustenance who gives support to all.  The way is common for the downward streams to flow. Thou who didst these things first art worthy of our lauds.

2.13.d: अन्वेको वदति यद ददाति तद रूपा मिनन तदपा एक ईयते | विश्वा एकस्य विनुदस्तितिक्षते यस्ताक्र... ||
2.13.e: One priest announces what the institutor gives: one, altering the forms, zealously plies his task,  The third corrects the imperfections left by each. Thou who didst these things first art worthy of our lauds.

2.13.d: परजाभ्यः पुष्टिं विभजन्त आसते रयिमिव पर्ष्ठं परभवन्तमायते | असिन्वन दंष्ट्रैः पितुरत्ति भोजनं यस्ताक्र... ||
2.13.e: Dealing out food unto their people there they sit, like wealth to him who comes, more than the back can bear.  Greedily with his teeth he eats the master's food. Thou who didst these things first art worthy of our lauds.

2.13.d: अधाक्र्णोः पर्थिवीं सन्द्र्शे दिवे यो धौतीनामहिहन्नारिणक पथः | तं तवा सतोमेभिरुदभिर्न वाजिनं देवं देवा अजनन सास्युक्थ्यः ||
2.13.e: Thou hast created earth to look upon the sky: thou, slaying Ahi, settest free the river's paths.  Thee, such, a God, the Gods have quickened with their lauds, even as a steed with waters: meet for praise art thou.

2.13.d: यो भोजनं च दयसे च वर्धनमार्द्रादा शुष्कं मधुमद दुदोहिथ | स शेवधिं नि दधिषे विवस्वति विश्वस्यैक ईशिषे सास्यु. ||
2.13.e: Thou givest increase, thou dealest to us our food: thou milkest from the moist the dry, the rich in sweets.  Thou by the worshipper layest thy precious store: thou art sole Lord of all. Meet for our praise art thou.

2.13.d: यः पुष्पिणीश्च परस्वश्च धर्मणाधि दाने वयवनीरधारयः | यश्चासमा अजनो दिद्युतो दिव उरुरूर्वानभितः स. उ. ||
2.13.e: Thou who hast spread abroad the streams by stablished law, and in the field the plants that blossom and bear seed;  Thou who hast made the matchless lightnings of the sky,—vast, compassing vast realms, meet for our praise art thou.

2.13.d: यो नार्मरं सहवसुं निहन्तवे पर्क्षाय च दासवेशाय चावहः | ऊर्जयन्त्या अपरिविष्टमास्यमुतैवाद्य पुरुक्र्त्स. उ. ||
2.13.e: Who broughtest Nārmara with all his wealth, for sake of food, to slay him that the fiends might be destroyed,  Broughtest the face unclouded of the strengthening one, performing much even now, worthy art thou of praise.

2.13.d: शतं वा यस्य दश साकमाद्य एकस्य शरुष्टौ यद धचोदमाविथ | अरज्जौ दस्यून समुनब दभीतये सुप्राव्योभवः स. उ. ||
2.13.e: Thou boundest up the Dāsa's hundred friends and ten, when, at one's hearing, thou helpest thy worshipper.  Thou for Dabhīti boundest Dasyus not with cords; Thou wast a mighty help. Worthy of lauds art thou.

2.13.d: विश्वेदनु रोधना अस्य पौंस्यं ददुरस्मै दधिरे कर्त्नवे धनम | षळ अस्तभ्ना विष्टिरः पञ्च सन्द्र्शः परिपरो अभवः स. उ. ||
2.13.e: All banks of rivers yielded to his manly might; to him they gave, to him, the Strong, gave up their wealth.  The six directions hast thou fixed, a five-fold view: thy victories reached afar. Worthy of lauds art thou.

2.13.d: सुप्रवाचनं तव वीर वीर्यं यदेकेन करतुना विन्दसे वसु | जातूष्ठिरस्य पर वयः सहस्वतो या चकर्थ सेन्द्र विश्वास्युक्थ्यः ||
2.13.e: Meet for high praise, O Hero, is thy power, that with thy single wisdom thou obtainest wealth,  The life-support of conquering Jātūṣṭhira. Indra, for all thy deeds, worthy of lauds art thou.

2.13.d: अरमयः सरपसस्तराय कं तुर्वीतये च वय्याय च सरुतिम | नीचा सन्तमुदनयः पराव्र्जं परान्धं शरोणं शरवयन स. उ. ||
2.13.e: Thou for Turvīti heldest still the flowing floods, the river-stream for Vayya easily to pass  Didst raise the outcast from the depths, and gavest fame unto the halt and blind. Worthy of lauds art thou.

2.13.d: अस्मभ्यं तद वसो दानाय राधः समर्थयस्व बहु ते वसव्यम | इन्द्र यच्चित्रं शरवस्या अनु दयून बर्हद वदेम व. स. ||
2.13.e: Prepare thyself to grant us that great bounty, O Vasu, for abundant is thy treasure.  Snatch up the wonderful, O Indra, daily. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो भरतेन्द्राय सोममामत्रेभिः सिञ्चता मद्यमन्धः | कामी हि वीरः सदमस्य पीतिं जुहोत वर्ष्णे तदिदेश वष्टि ||
2.14.e: MINISTERS, bring the Soma juice for Indra, pour forth the gladdening liquor with the beakers.  To drink of this the Hero longeth ever; offer it to the Bull, for this he willeth.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो यो अपो वव्रिवांसं वर्त्रं जघानाशन्येव वर्क्षम | तस्मा एतं भरत तद्वशायनेष इन्द्रो अर्हति पीतिमस्य ||
2.14.e: Ye ministers, to him who with the lightning smote, like a tree, the rain-withholding Vṛtra—  Bring it to him, him who is fain to taste it, a draught of this which Indra here deserveth.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो यो दर्भीकं जघान यो गा उदाजदप हि वलं वः | तस्मा एतमन्तरिक्षे न वातमिन्द्रं सोमैरोर्णुत जूर्न वस्त्रैः ||
2.14.e: Ye ministers, to him who smote Dṛbhīka, who drove the kine forth, and discovered Vala,  Offer this draught, like Vita in the region: clothe him with Soma even as steeds with trappings.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो य उरणं जघान नव चख्वांसं नवतिं चबाहून | यो अर्बुदमव नीचा बबाधे तमिन्द्रं सोमस्यभ्र्थे हिनोत ||
2.14.e: Him who did Uraṇa to death, Adhvaryus! though showing arms ninety-and-nine in number;  Who cast down headlong Arbuda and slew him,—speed ye that Indra to our offered Soma.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो यः सवश्नं जघान यः शुष्णमशुषं यो वयंसम | यः पिप्रुं नमुचिं यो रुधिक्रां तस्मा इन्द्रायान्धसो जुहोत ||
2.14.e: Ye ministers, to him who struck down Svaśna, and did to death Vyaṁsa and greedy Śuṣṇa,  And Rudhikrās and Namuci and Pipru,—to him, to Indra, pour ye forth libation.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो यः शतं शम्बरस्य पुरो बिभेदाश्मनेव पूर्वीः | यो वर्चिनः शतमिन्द्रः सहस्रमपावपद भरतासोममस्मै ||
2.14.e: Ye ministers, to him who as with thunder demolished Śambara's hundred ancient castles;  Who cast down Varcin's sons, a hundred thousand,—to him, to Indra, offer ye the Soma.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो यः शतमा सहस्रं भूम्या उपस्थे.अवपज्जघन्वान | कुत्सस्यायोरतिथिग्वस्य वीरान नयाव्र्णग भरता सोममस्मै ||
2.14.e: Ye ministers, to him who slew a hundred thousand, and cast them down upon earth's bosom;  Who quelled the valiant men of Atithigva, Kutsa, and Āyu,—bring to him the Soma.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो यन नरः कामयाध्वे शरुष्टी वहन्तो नशथा तदिन्द्रे | गभस्तिपूतं भरत शरुतायेन्द्राय सोमं यज्यवो जुहोत ||
2.14.e: Ministers, men, whatever thing ye long for obtain ye quickly bringing gifts to Indra.  Bring to the Glorious One what bands have cleansed; to Indra bring, ye pious ones, the Soma.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवः कर्तना शरुष्टिमस्मै वने निपूतं वन उन नयध्वम | जुषाणो हस्त्यमभि वावशे व इन्द्राय सोमं मदिरं जुहोत ||
2.14.e: Do ye, O ministers, obey his order: that purified in wood, in wood uplift ye.  Well pleased he longs for what your hands have tended: offer the gladdening Soma juice to Indra.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवः पयसोधर्यथा गोः सोमेभिरीं पर्णता भोजमिन्द्रम | वेदाहमस्य निभ्र्तं म एतद दित्सन्तं भूयो यजतश्चिकेत ||
2.14.e: As the cow's udder teems with milk, Adhvaryus, so fill with Soma Indra, liberal giver.  I know him: I am sure of this, the Holy knows that I fain would give to him more largely.

2.14.d: अध्वर्यवो यो दिव्यस्य वस्वो यः पार्थिवस्य कषम्यस्य राजा | तमूर्दरं न परिणता यवेनेन्द्रं सोमेभिस्तदपोवो अस्तु ||
2.14.e: Him, ministers, the Lord of heavenly treasure and all terrestrial wealth that earth possesses,  Him, Indra, fill with Soma as a garner is filled with barley full: be this your labour.
Prepare thyself to grant us that great booty, O Vasu, for abundant is thy treasure.  Gather up wondrous wealth, O Indra, daily. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.15.d: पर घा नवस्य महतो महानि सत्या सत्यस्य करणानि वोचम | तरिकद्रुकेश्वपिबत सुतस्यास्य मदे अहिमिन्द्रो जघान ||
2.15.e: Now, verily, will I declare the exploits, mighty and true, of him the True and Mighty.  In the Trikadrukas he drank the Soma: then in its rapture Indra slew the Dragon.

2.15.d: अवंशे दयामस्तभायद बर्हन्तमा रोदसी अप्र्णदन्तरिक्षम | स धारयद पर्थिवीं पप्रथच्च सोमस्य ता मद इन्द्रश्चकार ||
2.15.e: High heaven unsupported in space he stablished: he filled the two worlds and the air's mid-region.  Earth he upheld, and gave it wide expansion. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.

2.15.d: सद्मेव पराचो वि मिमाय मानैर्वज्रेण खान्यत्र्णन नदीनाम | वर्थास्र्जत पथिभिर्दीर्घयाथैः सोमस्य ता ... ||
2.15.e: From front, as ’twere a house, he ruled and measured; pierced with his bolt the fountains of the rivers,  And made them flow at ease by paths far-reaching, These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.

2.15.d: स परवोळ्हॄन परिगत्या दभीतेर्विश्वमधागायुधमिद्धे अग्नौ | सं गोभिरश्वैरस्र्जद रथेभिः सो... ||
2.15.e: Compassing those who bore away Dabhīti, in kindled fire he burnt up all their weapons.  And made him rich with kine and cars and horses. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.

2.15.d: स ईं महीं धुनिमेतोररम्णात सो अस्नातॄनपारयत सवस्ति | त उत्स्नाय रयिमभि पर तस्थुः सो... ||
2.15.e: The mighty roaring flood he stayed from flowing, and carried those who swam not safely over.  They having crossed the stream attained to riches. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.

2.15.d: सोदञ्चं सिन्धुमरिणान महित्वा वज्रेणान उषसः सं पिपेष | अजवसो जविनीभिर्विव्र्श्चन सो... ||
2.15.e: With mighty power he made the stream flow upward, crushed with his thunderbolt the car of Uṣas,  Rending her slow steeds with his rapid coursers. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.

2.15.d: स विद्वानपगोहं कनीनामाविर्भवन्नुदतिष्ठत पराव्र्क | परति शरोण सथाद वयनगचष्ट सो... ||
2.15.e: Knowing the place wherein the maids were hiding, the outcast showed himself and stood before them.  The cripple stood erect, the blind beheld them. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.

2.15.d: भिनद वलमङगिरोभिर्ग्र्णानो वि पर्वतस्य दरंहितान्यैरत | रिणग रोधांसि कर्त्रिमाण्येषां सो... ||
2.15.e: Praised by the Aṅgirases he slaughtered Vala, and burst apart the bulwarks of the mountain.  He tore away their deftly-built defences. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.

2.15.d: सवप्नेनाभ्युप्या चुमुरिं धुनिं च जघन्थ दस्यं पर दभीतिमावः | रम्भी चिदत्र विविदे हिरण्यं सो... ||
2.15.e: Thou, with sleep whelming Cumuri and Dhuni, slewest the Dasyu, keptest safe Dabhīti.  There the staff-bearer found the golden treasure. These things did Indra in the Soma's rapture.
Now let that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra , yield in return a boon to him who lauds thee.  Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with brave men, in assembly.

2.16.d: पर वः सतां जयेष्ठतमाय सुष्टुतिमग्नाविव समिधाने हविर्भरे | इन्द्रमजुर्यं जरयन्तमुक्षितं सनाद युवानमवसे हवामहे ||
2.16.e: To him, your own, the best among the good, I bring eulogy, like oblation in the kindled fire.  We invocate for help Indra untouched by eld, who maketh all decay, strengthened, for ever young.

2.16.d: यस्मादिन्द्राद बर्हतः किं चनें रते विश्वान्यस्मिन सम्भ्र्ताधि वीर्या | जठरे सोमं तन्वी सहो महो हस्ते वज्रं भरति शीर्षणि करतुम ||
2.16.e: Without whom naught exists, Indra the Lofty One; in whom alone all powers heroic are combined.  The Soma is within him, in his frame vast strength, the thunder in his hand and wisdom in his head.

2.16.d: न कषोणीभ्यां परिभ्वे त इन्द्रियं न समुद्रैः पर्वतैरिन्द्र ते रथः | न ते वज्रमन्वश्नोति कश्चन यदाशुभिः पतसि योजना पुरु ||
2.16.e: Not by both worlds is thine own power to be surpassed, nor may thy car be stayed by mountains or by seas.  None cometh near, O Indra, to thy thunderbolt, when with swift steeds thou fliest over many a league.

2.16.d: विश्वे हयस्मै यजताय धर्ष्णवे करतुं भरन्ति वर्षभाय सश्चते | वर्षा यजस्व हविषा विदुष्टरः पिबेन्द्र सोमं वर्षभेण भानुना ||
2.16.e: For all men bring their will to him the Resolute, to him the Holy One, to him the Strong they cleave.  Pay worship with oblation, strong and passing wise. Drink thou the Soma, Indra, through the mighty blaze.

2.16.d: वर्ष्णः कोशः पवते मध्व ऊर्मिर्व्र्षभान्नाय वर्षभाय पातवे | वर्षणाध्वर्यू वर्षभासो अद्रयो वर्षणं सोमं वर्षभाय सुष्वति ||
2.16.e: The vessel of the strong flows forth, the flood of meath, unto the Strong who feeds upon the strong, for drink,  Strong are the two Adhvaryus, strong are both the stones. They press the Soma that is strong for him the Strong.

2.16.d: वर्षा ते वज्र उत ते वर्षा रथो वर्षणा हरी वर्षभाण्यायुधा | वर्ष्णो मदस्य वर्षभ तवमीशिष इन्द्र सोमस्य वर्षभस्य तर्प्णुहि ||
2.16.e: Strong is thy thunderbolt, yea, and thy car is strong; strong are thy Bay Steeds and thy weapons powerful.  Thou, Indra, Bull, art Lord of the strong gladdening drink. with the strong Soma, Indra, satisfy thyself.

2.16.d: पर ते नावं न समने वचस्युवं बरह्मणा यामि सवनेषुदाध्र्षिः | कुविन नो अस्य वचसो निबोधिषदिन्द्रमुत्सं न वसुनः सिचामहे ||
2.16.e: I, bold by prayer, come near thee in thy sacred rites, thee like a saving ship, thee shouting in the war.  Verily he will hear and mark this word of ours: we will pour Indra forth as ’twere a spring of wealth.

2.16.d: पुरा सम्बाधादभ्या वव्र्त्स्व नो धेनुर्न वत्सं यवसस्य पिप्युषी | सक्र्त सु ते सुमतिभिः शतक्रतो सं पत्नीभिर्न वर्षणो नसीमहि ||
2.16.e: Turn thee unto us ere calamity come nigh, as a cow full of pasture turns her to her calf.  Lord of a Hundred Powers, may we once firmly cling to thy fair favours even as husbands to their wives.
Now let that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, yield in return a boon to him who lauds thee.  Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.17.d: तदस्मै नव्यमङगिरस्वदर्चत शुष्मा यदस्य परत्नथोदीरते | विश्वा यद गोत्रा सहसा परीव्र्ता मदे सोमस्य दरंहितान्यैरयत ||
2.17.e: LIKE the Aṅgirases, sing this new song forth to him, for, as in ancient days, his mighty powers are shown,  When in the rapture of the Soma he unclosed with strength the solid firm-shut stables of the kine.

2.17.d: स भुतु यो ह परथमाय धायस ओजो मिमानो महिमानमातिरत | शूरो यो युत्सु तन्वं परिव्यत शीर्षणि दयां महिना परत्यमुञ्चत ||
2.17.e: Let him be even that God who, for the earliest draught measuring out his power, increased his majesty;  Hero who fortified his body in the wars, and through his greatness set the heaven upon his head.

2.17.d: अधाक्र्णोः परथमं वीर्यं महद यदस्याग्रे बरह्मणा शुष्ममैरयः | रथेष्ठेन हर्यश्वेन विच्युताः पर जीरयः सिस्रते सध्र्यक पर्थक ||
2.17.e: Thou didst perform thy first great deed of hero might what time thou showedst power, through prayer, before this folk.  Hurled down by thee the car-borne Lord of Tawny Steeds, the congregated swift ones fled in sundry ways.

2.17.d: अधा यो विश्वा भुवनाभि मज्मनेशानक्र्त परवया अभ्यवर्धत | आद रोदसी जयोतिषा वह्निरातनोत सीव्यन तमांसि दुधिता समव्ययत ||
2.17.e: He made himself by might Lord of all living things, and strong in vital power waxed great above them all.  He, borne on high, o’erspread with light the heaven and earth, and, sewing up the turbid darkness, closed it in.

2.17.d: स पराचीनान पर्वतान दरंहदोजसाधराचीनमक्र्णोदपामपः | अधारयत पर्थिवीं विश्वधायसमस्तभ्नान मायया दयामवस्रसः ||
2.17.e: He with his might made firm the forward-bending hills, the downward rushing of the waters he ordained.  Fast he upheld the earth that nourisheth all life, and stayed the heaven from falling by his wondrous skill.

2.17.d: सास्मा अरं बाहुभ्यां यं पिताक्र्णोद विश्वस्मादा जनुषो वेदसस परि | येना पर्थिव्यां नि करिविं शयध्यै वज्रेण हत्व्यव्र्णक तुविष्वणिः ||
2.17.e: Fit for the grasping of his arms is what the Sire hath fabricated from all kind of precious wealth.  The thunderbolt, wherewith, loud-roaring, he smote down, and striking him to death laid Krivi on the earth.

2.17.d: अमाजूरिव पित्रोः सचा सती समानादा सदसस्त्वामिये भगम | कर्धि परकेतमुप मास्या भर दद्धि भागं तन्वो येन मामहः ||
2.17.e: As she who in her parents' house is growing old, I pray to thee as Bhaga from the seat of all.  Grant knowledge, mete it out and bring it to us here: give us the share wherewith thou makest people glad.

2.17.d: भोजं तवामिन्द्र वयं हुवेम ददिष टवमिन्द्रापांसि वाजान | अविड्ढीन्द्र चित्रया न ऊति कर्धि वर्शन्निन्द्र वस्यसो नः ||
2.17.e: May we invoke thee as a liberal giver thou givest us, O Indra, strength and labours.  Help us with manifold assistance, Indra:  Mighty  One, Indra, make us yet more wealthy.
Now may that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, give in return a boon to him who lauds thee.  Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.18.d: पराता रथो नवो योजि सस्निश्चतुर्युगस्त्रिकशः सप्तरश्मिः | दशारित्रो मनुष्यः सवर्षाः स इष्टिभिर्मतिभीरंह्यो भूत ||
2.18.e: THE rich new car hath been equipped at morning; four yokes it hath, three whips, seven reins to guide it:  Ten-sided, friendly to mankind, light-winner, that must be urged to speed with prayers and wishes.

2.18.d: सास्मा अरं परथमं स दवितीयमुतो तर्तीयं मनुषः स होता | अन्यस्या गर्भमन्य ऊ जनन्त सो अन्येभिः सचते जेन्यो वर्षा ||
2.18.e: This is prepared for him the first, the second, and the third time: he is man's Priest and Herald.  Others get offspring of another parent he goeth, as a noble Bull, with others.

2.18.d: हरी नु कं रथ इन्द्रस्य योजमायै सूक्तेन वचसा नवेन | मो षु तवामत्र बहवो हि विप्रा नि रीरमन यजमानासो अन्ये ||
2.18.e: To Indra's car the Bay Steeds have I harnessed, that new well-spoken words may bring him hither.  Here let not other worshippers detain thee, for among us are many holy singers.

2.18.d: आ दवाभ्यां हरिभ्यामिन्द्र याह्या चतुर्भिरा षड्भिर्हूयमानः | आष्टाभिर्दशभिः सोमपेयमयं सुतःसुमख मा मर्धस कः ||
2.18.e: Indra, come hitherward with two Bay Coursers, come thou with four, with six when invocated.  Come thou with eight, with ten, to drink the Soma. Here is the juice, brave Warrior: do not scorn it.

2.18.d: आ विंशत्या तरिंशता याह्यर्वां आ चत्वारिंशता हरिभिर्यजानः | आ पञ्चाशता सुरथेभिरिन्द्रा षष्ट्या सप्तत्या सोमपेयम ||
2.18.e: O Indra, come thou hither having harnessed thy car with twenty, thirty, forty horses.  Come thou with fifty well trained coursers, Indra, sixty or seventy, to drink the Soma.

2.18.d: आशीत्या नवत्या याह्यर्वां आ शतेन हरिभिरुह्यमानः | अयं हि ते शुनहोत्रेषु सोम इन्द्र तवाया परिषिक्तो मदाय ||
2.18.e: Come to us hitherward, O Indra, carried by eighty, ninety, or an hundred horses.  This Soma juice among the Śunahotras hath been poured out, in love, to glad thee, Indra.

2.18.d: मम बरह्मेन्द्र याह्यछा विश्वा हरी धुरि धिष्वा रथस्य | पुरुत्रा हि विहव्यो बभूथास्मिञ्छूर सवने मादयस्व ||
2.18.e: To this my prayer, O Indra, come thou hither: bind to thy car's pole all thy two Bay Coursers.  Thou art to be invoked in many places Hero, rejoice thyself in this libation.

2.18.d: न म इन्द्रेण सख्यं वि योषदस्मभ्यमस्य दक्षिणा दुहीत | उप जयेष्ठे वरूथे गभस्तौ पराये-पराये जिगीवांसः सयाम ||
2.18.e: Ne’er be my love from Indra disunited still may his liberal Milch-cow yield us treasure.  So may we under his supreme protection, safe in his arms, succeed in each forth-going.
Now may that wealthy Cow Of thine, O Indra, give in return a boon to him who lauds thee.  Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.19.d: अपाय्यस्यान्धसो मदाय मनीषिणः सुवानस्य परयसः | यस्मिन्निन्द्रः परदिवि वाव्र्धान ओको दधे बरह्मण्यन्तश्च नरः ||
2.19.e: DRAUGHTS of this sweet juice have been drunk for rapture, of the wise Soma-presser's offered dainty,  Wherein, grown mighty in the days aforetime, Indra hath found delight, and men who worship.

2.19.d: अस्य मन्दानो मध्वो वज्रहस्तो.अहिमिन्द्रो अर्णोव्र्तं वि वर्श्चत | पर यद वयो स सवसराण्यछा परयांसि च नदीनां चक्रमन्त ||
2.19.e: Cheered by this meath Indra, whose hand wields thunder, rent piecemeal Ahi who barred up the waters,  So that the quickening currents of the rivers flowed forth like birds unto their resting-places.

2.19.d: स माहिन इन्द्रो अर्णो अपां परैरयदहिहाछा समुद्रम | अजनयत सूर्यं विदद गा अक्तुनाह्नां वयुनानि साधत ||
2.19.e: Indra, this Mighty One, the Dragon's slayer, sent forth the flood of waters to the ocean.  He gave the Sun his life, he found the cattle, and with the night the works of days completed.

2.19.d: सो अप्रतीनि मनवे पुरूणीन्द्रो दाशद दाशुषे हन्ति वर्त्रम | सद्यो यो नर्भ्यो अतसाय्यो भूत पस्प्र्धानेभ्यः सूर्यस्य सातौ ||
2.19.e: To him who worshippeth hath Indra given many and matchless gifts. He slayeth Vṛtra.  Straight was he to be sought with supplications by men who struggled to obtain the sunlight.

2.19.d: स सुन्वत इन्द्रः सूर्यमा देवो रिणं मर्त्याय सतवान | आ यद रयिं गुहदवद्यमस्मै भरदंशं नैतशो दशस्यन ||
2.19.e: To him who poured him gifts he gave up Sūrya,—Indra, the God, the Mighty, to the mortal;  For Etaśa with worship brought him riches that keep distress afar, as ’twere his portion.

2.19.d: स रन्धयत सदिवः सारथये शुष्णमशुषं कुयवं कुत्साय | दिवोदासाय नवतिं च नवेन्द्रः पुरो वयैरच्छम्बरस्य ||
2.19.e: Once to the driver of his chariot, Kutsa, he gave up greedy Sūrya, plague of harvest;  And Indra, for the sake of Divodāsa demolished Śambara's nine-and-ninety castles.

2.19.d: एवा त इन्द्रोचथमहेम शरवस्या न तमना वाजयन्तः | अश्याम तत साप्तमाशुषाणा ननमो वधरदेवस्य पीयोः ||
2.19.e: So have we brought our hymn to thee, O Indra, strengthening thee and fain ourselves for glory.  May we with best endeavours gain this friendship, and mayst thou bend the godless scorner's weapons.

2.19.d: एवा ते गर्त्समदाः शूर मम्नावस्यवो न वयुनानि तक्षुः | बरह्मण्यन्त इन्द्र ते नवीय इषमूर्जं सुक्षितिं सुम्नमश्युः ||
2.19.e: Thus the Gṛtsamadas for thee, O Hero, have wrought their hymn and task as seeking favour.  May they who worship thee afresh, O Indra, gain food and strength, bliss, and a happy dwelling.
Now may that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, give in return a boon to him who lauds thee,  Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.20.d: वयं ते वय इन्द्र विद्धि षु णः पर भरामहे वाजयुर्न रथम | विपन्यवो दीध्यतो मनीषा सुम्नमियक्षन्तस्त्वावतो नॄन ||
2.20.e: As one brings forth his car when fain for combat, so bring we power to thee—regard us, Indra—  Well skilled in song, thoughtful in spirit, seeking great bliss from one like thee amid the Heroes.

2.20.d: तवं न इन्द्र तवाभिरूती तवायतो अभिष्टिपासि जनान | तवमिनो दाशुषो वरूतेत्थाधीरभि यो नक्षति तवा ||
2.20.e: Indra, thou art our own with thy protection, a guardian near to men who love thee truly,  Active art thou, the liberal man's defender, his who draws near to thee with right devotion.

2.20.d: स नो युवेन्द्रो जोहूत्रः सखा शिवो नरामस्तु पाता | यः शंसन्तं यः शशमानमूती पचन्तं च सतुवन्तंच परणेषत ||
2.20.e: May Indra, called with solemn invocations. the young, the Friend, be men's auspicious keeper,  One who will further with his aid the singer, the toiler, praiser, dresser of oblations.

2.20.d: तमु सतुष इन्द्रं तं गर्णीषे यस्मिन पुरा वाव्र्धुः शाशदुश्च | स वस्वः कामं पीपरदियानो बरह्मण्यतो नूतनस्यायोः ||
2.20.e: With laud and song let me extol that Indra in whom of old men prospered and were mighty.  May he, implored, fulfil the prayer for plenty of him who worships, of the living mortal.

2.20.d: सो अङगिरसामुचथा जुजुष्वान बरह्मा तूतोदिन्द्रो गातुमिष्णन | मुष्णन्नुषसः सूर्येण सतवानश्नस्य चिच्छिश्नथत पूर्व्याणि ||
2.20.e: He, Indra whom the Aṅgirases' praise delighted, strengthened their prayer and made their goings prosper.  Stealing away the mornings with the sunlight, he, lauded, crushed even Aśna's ancient powers.

2.20.d: स ह शरुत इन्द्रो नाम देव ऊर्ध्वो भुवन मनुषे दस्मतमः | अव परियमर्शसानस्य साह्वाञ्छिरो भरद दासस्य सवधावान ||
2.20.e: He verily, the God, the glorious Indra, hath raised him up for man, best Wonder-Worker.  He, self-reliant, mighty and triumphant, brought low the dear head of the wicked Dāsa.

2.20.d: स वर्त्रहेन्द्रः कर्ष्णयोनीः पुरन्दरो दासीरैरयद वि | अजनयन मनवे कषामपश्च सत्रा शंसं यजमानस्य तूतोत ||
2.20.e: Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, Fort-destroyer, scattered the Dāsa hosts who dwelt in darkness.  For men hath he created earth and waters, and ever helped the prayer of him who worships.

2.20.d: तस्मै तवस्यमनु दायि सत्रेन्द्राय देवेभिरर्णसातौ | परति यदस्य वज्रं बाह्वोर्धुर्हत्वी दस्यून पुर आयसीर्नि तारीत ||
2.20.e: To him in might the Gods have ever yielded, to Indra in the tumult of the battle.  When in his arms they laid the bolt, he slaughtered the Dasyus and cast down their forts of iron.
Now may that wealthy Cow of thine, O Indra, give in return a boon to him who lauds thee.  Give to thy praisers: let not fortune fail us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.21.d: विश्वजिते धनजिते सवर्जिते सत्राजिते नर्जित उर्वराजिते | अश्वजिते गोजिते अब्जिते भरेन्द्राय सोमं यजताय हर्यतम ||
2.21.e: To him the Lord of all, the Lord of wealth, of light; him who is Lord for ever, Lord of men and tilth,  Him who is Lord of horses, Lord of kine, of floods, to Indra, to the Holy bring sweet Soma juice.

2.21.d: अभिभुवे.अभिभङगाय वन्वते.अषाळ्हाय सहमानाय वेधसे | तुविग्रये वह्नये दुष्टरीतवे सत्रासाहे नम इन्द्राय वोचत ||
2.21.e: To him the potent One, who conquers and breaks down, the Victor never vanquished who disposes all,  The mighty-voiced, the rider, unassailable, to Indra everconquering speak your reverent prayer.

2.21.d: सत्रासाहो जनभक्षो जनंसहश्च्यवनो युध्मो अनु जोषमुक्षितः | वर्तंचयः सहुरिर्विक्ष्वारित इन्द्रस्य वोचं पर कर्तानि वीर्या ||
2.21.e: Still Victor, loved by mortals, ruler over men, o’erthrower, warrior, he hath waxen as he would;  Host-gatherer, triumphant, honoured mid the folk. Indra's heroic deeds will I tell forth to all.

2.21.d: अनानुदो वर्षभो दोधतो वधो गम्भीर रष्वो असमष्टकाव्यः | रध्रचोदः शनथनो वीळितस पर्थुरिन्द्रः सुयज्ञ उषसः सवर्जनत ||
2.21.e: The strong who never yields, who slew the furious fiend, the deep, the vast, of wisdom unattainable;  Who speeds the good, the breaker-down, the firm, the vast,—Indra whose rites bring joy hath made the light of Dawn.

2.21.d: यज्णेन गातुमप्तुरो विविद्रिरे धियो हिन्वाना उशिजो मनीषिणः | अभिस्वरा निषदा गा अवस्यव इन्द्रे हिन्वाना दरविणान्याशत ||
2.21.e: By sacrifice the yearning sages sending forth their songs found furtherance from him who speeds the flood.  In Indra seeking help with worship and with hymn, they drew him to themselves and won them kine and wealth.

2.21.d: इन्द्र शरेष्ठानि दरविणानि धेहि चित्तिं दक्षस्य सुभगत्वं अस्मे | पोषं रयीणामरिष्टिं तनूनां सवाद्मानं वाचः सुदिनत्वमह्नाम ||
2.21.e: Indra, bestow on us the best of treasures, the spirit of ability and fortune;  Increase of riches, safety of our bodies, charm of sweet speech, and days of pleasant weather.

2.22.d: तरिकद्रुकेषु महिषो यवाशिरं तुविशुष्मस्त्र्पत सोममपिबद विष्णुना सुतं यथावशत | स ईं ममाद महि कर्म कर्तवे महामुरुं सैनं सश्चद देवो देवं सत्यमिन्द्रंसत्य इन्दुः ||
2.22.e: At the Trikadrukas the Great and Strong hath drunk drink blent with meal. With Viṣṇu hath he quaffed the poured out Soma juice, all that he would.  That hath so heightened him the Great, the Wide, to do his mighty work.  So may the God attain the God, true Indu Indra who is true.

2.22.d: अध तविषीमानभ्योजसा करिविं युधाभवदा रोदसी अप्र्णदस्य मज्मना पर वाव्र्धे | अधत्तान्यं जठरे परेमरिच्यत सैनं ... ||
2.22.e: So he resplendent in the battle overcame Krivi by might. He with his majesty hath filled the earth and heaven, and waxen strong.  One share of the libation hath he swallowed down: one share he left.  So may the God attend the God, true Indu Indra who is true.

2.22.d: साकं जातः करतुना साकमोजसा ववक्षिथ साकं वर्द्धो वीर्यैः सासहिर्म्र्धो विचर्षणिः | दाता राधः सतुवते काम्यं वसु सैनं ... ||
2.22.e: Brought forth together with wisdom and mighty power thou grewest great; with hero deeds subduing the malevolent, most swift in act;  Giving prosperity, and lovely wealth to him who praiseth thee. So may the God attend the God, true Indu Indra who is true.

2.22.d: तव तयन नर्यं नर्तो.अप इन्द्र परथमं पूर्व्यं दिवि परवाच्यं कर्तम | यद देवस्य शवसा परारिणा असुं रिणन्नपः | भुवद विश्वमभ्यादेवमोजसा विदादूर्जं शतक्रतुर्विदादिषम ||
2.22.e: This, Indra, was thy hero deed, Dancer, thy first and ancient work, worthy to be told forth in heaven,  What time thou sentest down life with a God's own power, freeing the floods.  All that is godless may he conquer with his might, and, Lord of Hundred Powers, find for us strength and food.

2.23.d: गणानां तवा गणपतिं हवामहे कविं कवीनामुपमश्रवस्तमम | जयेष्ठराजं बरह्मणां बरह्मणस पत आ नः षर्ण्वन्नूतिभिः सीद सादनम ||
2.23.e: WE call thee, Lord and Leader of the heavenly hosts, the wise among the wise, the famousest of all,  The King supreme of prayers, O Brahmaṇaspati: hear us with help; sit down in place of sacrifice.

2.23.d: देवाश्चित ते असुर्य परचेतसो बर्हस्पते यज्ञियं भागमानशुः | उस्रा इव सूर्यो जयोतिषा महो विश्वेषामिज्जनिता बरह्मणामसि ||
2.23.e: Bṛhaspati, God immortal! verily the Gods have gained from thee, the wise, a share in holy rites.  As with great light the Sun brings forth the rays of morn, so thou alone art Father of all sacred prayer.

2.23.d: आ विबाध्या परिरापस्तमांसि च जयोतिष्मन्तं रथं रतस्य तिष्ठसि | बर्हस्पते भीमममित्रदम्भनं रक्षोहणंगोत्रभिदं सवर्विदम ||
2.23.e: When thou hast chased away revilers and the gloom, thou mountest the refulgent car of sacrifice;  The awful car, Bṛhaspati, that quells the foe, slays demons, cleaves the stall of kine, and finds the light.

2.23.d: सुनीतिभिर्नयसि तरायसे जनं यस्तुभ्यं दाशान न तमंहो अश्नवत | बरह्मद्विषस्तपनो मन्युमीरसि बर्हस्पते महि तत ते महित्वनम ||
2.23.e: Thou leadest with good guidance and preservest men; distress o’ertakes not him who offers gifts to thee.  Him who hates prayer thou punishest, Bṛhaspati, quelling his wrath: herein is thy great mightiness.

2.23.d: न तमंहो न दुरितं कुतश्चन नारातयस्तितिरुर्न दवयाविनः | विश्वा इदस्माद धवरसो वि बाधसे यं सुगोपा रक्षसि बरह्मणस पते ||
2.23.e: No sorrow, no distress from any side, no foes, no creatures double-tongued have overcome the man,—  Thou drivest all seductive fiends away from him whom, careful guard, thou keepest Brahmaṇaspati.

2.23.d: तवं नो गोपाः पथिक्र्द विचक्षणस्तव वरताय मतिभिर्जरामहे | बर्हस्पते यो नो अभि हवरो दधे सवा तं मर्मर्तु दुछुना हरस्वती ||
2.23.e: Thou art our keeper, wise, preparer of our paths: we, for thy service, sing to thee with hymns of praise.  Bṛhaspati, whoever lays a snare for us, him may his evil fate, precipitate, destroy.

2.23.d: उत वा यो नो मर्चयादनागसो.अरातीवा मर्तः सानुको वर्कः | बर्हस्पते अप तं वर्तया पथः सुगं नो अस्यै देववीतये कर्धि ||
2.23.e: Him, too, who threatens us without offence of ours, the evilminded, arrogant, rapacious man,—  Him turn thou from our path away, Bṛhaspati: give us fair access to this banquet of the Gods.

2.23.d: तरातारं तवा तनूनां हवामहे.अवस्पर्तरधिवक्तारमस्मयुम | बर्हस्पते देवनिदो नि बर्हय मा दुरेवा उत्तरं सुम्नमुन नशन ||
2.23.e: Thee as protector of our bodies we invoke, thee, saviour, as the comforter who loveth us.  Strike, O Bṛhaspati, the Gods’ revilers down, and let not the unrighteous come to highest bliss.

2.23.d: तवया वयं सुव्र्धा बरह्मणस पते सपार्हा वसु मनुष्या ददीमहि | या नो दूरे तळितो या अरातयो.अभि सन्ति जम्भया ता अनप्नसः ||
2.23.e: Through thee, kind prosperer, O Brahmaṇaspati, may we obtain the wealth of Men which all desire:  And all our enemies, who near or far away prevail against us, crush, and leave them destitute.

2.23.d: तवया वयमुत्तमं धीमहे वयो बर्हस्पते पप्रिणा सस्निना युजा | मा नो दुःशंसो अभिदिप्सुरीशत पर सुशंसा मतिभिस्तारिषीमहि ||
2.23.e: With thee as our own rich and liberal ally may we, Bṛhaspati, gain highest power of life.  Let not the guileful wicked man be lord of us:—still may we prosper, singing goodly hymns of praise.

2.23.d: अनानुदो वर्षभो जग्मिराहवं निष्टप्ता शत्रुं पर्तनासुसासहिः | असि सत्य रणया बरह्मणस पत उग्रस्य चिद दमिता वीळुहर्षिणः ||
2.23.e: Strong, never yielding, hastening to the battle-cry, consumer of the foe, victorious in the strife,  Thou art sin's true avenger, Brahmaṇaspati, who tamest e’en the fierce, the wildly passionate.

2.23.d: अदेवेन मनसा यो रिशण्यति शासामुग्रो मन्यमानो जिघांसति | बर्हस्पते म परणक तस्य नो वधो नि कर्म मन्युं दुरेवस्य शर्धतः ||
2.23.e: Whoso with mind ungodly seeks to do us harm, who, deeming him a man of might mid lords, would slay,—  Let not his deadly blow reach us, Bṛhaspati; may we humiliate the strong ill-doer's wrath.

2.23.d: भरेषु हव्यो नमसोपसद्यो गन्ता वाजेषु सनिता धनं धनम | विश्वा इदर्यो अभिदिप्स्वो मर्धो बर्हस्पतिर्वि ववर्हा रथां इव ||
2.23.e: The mover mid the spoil, the winner of all wealth, to be invoked in fight and reverently adored,  Bṛhaspati hath overthrown like cars of war all wicked enemies who fain would injure us.

2.23.d: तेजिष्थया तपनि रक्षसस्तप ये तवा निदे दधिरे दर्ष्टवीर्यम | आविस्तत कर्ष्व यदसत त उक्थ्यं बर्हस्पते वि परिरापो अर्दय ||
2.23.e: Burn up the demons with thy fiercest flaming brand, those who have scorned thee in thy manifested might.  Show forth that power that shall deserve the hymn of praise: destroy the evil speakers, O Bṛhaspati.

2.23.d: बर्हस्पते अति यदर्यो अर्हाद दयुमद विभाति करतुमज्जनेषु | यद दीदयच्छवस रतप्रजात तदस्मसु दरविणं धेहिचित्रम ||
2.23.e: Bṛhaspati, that which the foe deserves not which shines among the folk effectual, splendid,  That, Son of Law I which is with might refulgent-that treasure wonderful bestow thou on us.

2.23.d: मा न सतेनेभ्यो ये अभि दरुहस पदे निरामिणो रिपवो.अन्नेषु जाग्र्धुः | आ देवानामोहते वि वरयो हर्दि बर्हस्पते नपरः साम्नो विदुः ||
2.23.e: Give us not up to those who, foes in ambuscade, are greedy for the wealth of him who sits at ease,  Who cherish in their heart abandonment of Gods. Bṛhaspati, no further rest shall they obtain.

2.23.d: विश्वेभ्यो हि तवा भुवनेभ्यस परि तवष्टाजनत साम्नः साम्नः कविः | स रणचिद रणया बरह्मणस पतिर्द्रुहो हन्ता मह रतस्य धर्तरि ||
2.23.e: For Tvaṣṭar, he who knows each sacred song, brought thee to life, preeminent o’er all the things that be.  Guilt-scourger, guilt-avenger is Bṛhaspati, who slays the spoiler and upholds the mighty Law.

2.23.d: तव शरिये वयजिहीत पर्वतो गवां गोत्रमुदस्र्जो यदङगिरः | इन्द्रेण युजा तमसा परीव्र्तं बर्हस्पते निरपामौब्जो अर्णवम ||
2.23.e: The mountain, for thy glory, cleft itself apart when, Aṅgiras! thou openedst the stall of kine.  Thou, O Bṛhaspati, with Indra for ally didst hurl down water-floods which gloom had compassed round.

2.23.d: बरह्मणस पते तवमस्य यन्ता सूक्तस्य बोधि तनयं च जिन्व | विश्वं तद भद्रं यदवन्ति देवा बर्हद वदेम ... ||
2.23.e: O Brahmaṇaspati, be thou controller of this our hymn and prosper thou our children.  All that the Gods regard with love is blessed. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.24.d: सेमामविड्ढि परभ्र्तिं य ईशिषे.अया विधेम नवया महा गिरा | यथा नो मीढ्वान सतवते सखा तव बर्हस्पतेसीषधः सोत नो मतिम ||
2.24.e: BE pleased with this our offering, thou who art the Lord; we will adore thee with this new and mighty song.  As this thy friend, our liberal patron, praises thee, do thou, Bṛhaspati, fulfil our hearts' desire.

2.24.d: यो नन्त्वान्यनमन नयोजसोतादर्दर्मन्युना शम्बराणि वि | पराच्यावयदच्युता बरह्मणस पतिरा चाविशद वसुमन्तं वि पर्वतम ||
2.24.e: He who with might bowed down the things that should be bowed, and in his fury rent the holds of Śambara:  Who overthrew what shook not, Brahmaṇaspati,—he made his way within the mountain stored with wealth.

2.24.d: तद देवानां देवतमाय कर्त्वमश्रथ्नन दर्ळ्हाव्रदन्त वीळिता | उद गा आजदभिनद बरह्मणा वलमगूहत तमो वयचक्षयत सवः ||
2.24.e: That was a great deed for the Godliest of the Gods: strong things were loosened and the firmly fixed gave way.  He drave the kine forth and cleft Vala through by prayer, dispelled the darkness and displayed the light of heaven.

2.24.d: अश्मास्यमवतं बरह्मणस पतिर्मधुधारमभि यमोजसात्र्णत | तमेव विश्वे पपिरे सवर्द्र्शो बहु साकं सिसिचुरुत्समुद्रिणम ||
2.24.e: The well with mouth of stone that poured a flood of meath, which Brahmaṇaspati hath opened with his might—  All they who see the light have drunk their fill thereat: together they have made the watery fount flow forth.

2.24.d: सना ता का चिद भुवना भवीत्वा माद्भिः शरद्भिर्दुरो वरन्त वः | अयतन्ता चरतो अन्यद-अन्यदिद य चकार वयुना बरह्मणस पतिः ||
2.24.e: Ancient will be those creatures, whatsoe’er they be; with moons, with autumns, doors unclose themselves to you.  Effortless they pass on to perfect this and that, appointed works which Brahmaṇaspati ordained.

2.24.d: अभिनक्षन्तो अभि ये तमानशुर्निधिं पणीनां परमंगुहा हितम | ते विद्वांसः परतिचक्ष्यान्र्ता पुनर्यत उायन तदुदीयुराविशम ||
2.24.e: They who with much endeavour searching round obtained the Paṇis’ noblest treasure hidden in the cave,—  Those sages, having marked the falsehoods, turned them back whence they had come, and sought again to enter in.

2.24.d: रतावानः परतिचक्ष्यान्र्ता पुनरात आ तस्थुः कवयो महस पथः | ते बाहुभ्यां धमितमग्निमश्मनि नकिः षो अस्त्यरणो जहुर्हि तम ||
2.24.e: The pious ones when they had seen the falsehoods turned them back, the sages stood again upon the lofty ways.  Cast down with both their arms upon the rock they left the kindled fire, and said, No enemy is he.

2.24.d: रतज्येन कषिप्रेण बरह्मणस पतिर्यत्र वष्टि पर तदश्नोति धन्वना | तस्य साध्वीरिषवो याभिरस्यति नर्चक्षसो दर्शये कर्णयोनयः ||
2.24.e: With his swift bow, strung truly, Brahmaṇaspati reaches the mark whate’er it be that he desires.  Excellent are the arrows wherewithal he shoots, keen-eyed to look on men and springing from his ear.

2.24.d: स संनयः स विनयः पुरोहितः स सुष्टुतः स युधिब्रह्मणस पतिः | चाक्ष्मो यद वाजं भरते मती धनादित सूर्यस्तपति तप्यतुर्व्र्था ||
2.24.e: He brings together and he parts, the great High Priest; extolled is he, in battle Brahmaṇaspati.  When, gracious, for the hymn he brings forth food and wealth, the glowing Sun untroubled sends forth fervent heat.

2.24.d: विभु परभु परथमं मेहनावतो बर्हस्पतेः सुविदत्राणि राध्या | इमा सातानि वेन्यस्य वाजिनो येन जना उभये भुञ्जते विशः ||
2.24.e: First and preeminent, excelling all besides are the kind gifts of liberal Bṛhaspati.  These are the boons of him the Strong who should be loved, whereby both classes and the people have delight.

2.24.d: यो.अवरे वर्जने विश्वथा विभुर्महामु रण्वः शवसा ववक्षिथ | स देवो देवान परति पप्रथे पर्थु विश्वेदु तापरिभूर्ब्रह्मणस पतिः ||
2.24.e: Thou who in every way supreme in earthly power, rejoicing, by thy mighty strength hast waxen great,—  He is the God spread forth in breadth against the Gods: he, Brahmaṇaspati, encompasseth this All.

2.24.d: विश्वं सत्यं मघवाना युवोरिदापश्चन पर मिनन्ति वरतं वाम | अछेन्द्राब्रह्मणस्पती हविर्नो.अन्नं युजेव वाजिना जिगातम ||
2.24.e: From you, twain Maghavans, all truth proceedeth: even the waters break not your commandment.  Come to us, Brahmaṇaspati and Indra, to our oblation like yoked steeds to fodder.

2.24.d: उताशिष्ठा अनु शर्ण्वन्ति वह्नयः सभेयो विप्रो भरते मती धना | वीळुद्वेषा अनु वश रणमाददिः स ह वाजी समिथे बरह्मणस पतिः ||
2.24.e: The sacrificial flames most swiftly hear the call: the priest of the assembly gaineth wealth for hymns.  Hating the stern, remitting at his will the debt, strong in the shock of fight is Brahmaṇaspati.

2.24.d: बरह्मणस पतेरभवद यथावशं सत्यो मन्युर्महि कर्माकरिष्यतः | यो गा उदाजत स दिवे वि चाभजन महीव रीतिः शवसासरत पर्थक ||
2.24.e: The wrath of Brahmaṇaspati according to his will had full effect when he would do a mighty deed.  The kine he drave forth and distributed to heaven, even as a copious flood with strength flows sundry ways.

2.24.d: बरह्मणस पते सुयमस्य विश्वहा रायः सयाम रथ्यो वयस्वतः | वीरेषु वीरानुप परंधि नस्त्वं यदीशानो बरह्मणा वेषि मे हवम ||
2.24.e: O Brahmaṇaspati, may we be evermore masters of wealth well-guided, full of vital strength.  Heroes on heroes send abundantly to us, when thou omnipotent through prayer seekest my call.
O Brahmaṇaspati, be thou controller of this our hymn, and prosper thou our children.  All that the Gods regard with love is blessed. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.25.d: इन्धानो अग्निं वनवद वनुष्यतः कर्तब्रह्मा शूशुवद रातहव्य इत ||
2.25.e: HE lighting up the flame shall conquer enemies: strong shall he be who offers prayer and brings his gift.  He with his seed spreads forth beyond another's seed, whomever Brahmaṇaspati takes for his friend.

2.25.d: जातेन जातमति स पर सर्स्र्ते यं-यं युजंक्र्णुते बरह्मणस पतिः ||
2.25.e: With heroes he shall overcome his hero foes, and spread his wealth by kine wise by himself is be.  His children and his children's children grow in strength, whomever Brahmaṇaspati takes for his friend.

2.25.d: वीरेभिर्वीरान वनवद वनुष्यतो गोभी रयिं पप्रथद बोधति तमना | तोकं च तस्य तनयं च वर्धते यं-यं ... ||
2.25.e: He, mighty like a raving river's billowy flood, as a bull conquers oxen, overcomes with strength.  Like Agni's blazing rush he may not be restrained, whomever Brahmaṇaspati takes for his friend.

2.25.d: सिन्धुर्न कषोदः शिमीवान रघायतो वर्षेव वध्रीन्रभि वष्ट्योजसा | अग्नेरिव परसितिर्नाह वर्तवे यं-यं .. ||
2.25.e: For him the floods of heaven flow never failing down: first with the heroes he goes forth to war for kine.  He slays in unabated vigour with great might, whomever Brahmaṇaspati takes for his friend.

2.25.d: तस्मा अर्षन्ति दिव्या असश्चतः स सत्वभिः परथमो गोषुगछति | अनिभ्र्ष्टतविषिर्हन्त्योजसा यं-यं ... ||
2.25.e: All roaring rivers pour their waters down for him, and many a flawless shelter hath been granted him.  Blest with the happiness of Gods he prospers well, whomever Brahmaṇaspati takes for his friend.

2.25.d: तस्मा इद विश्वे धुनयन्त सिन्धवो.अछिद्रा शर्म दधिरे पुरूणि | देवानां सुम्ने सुभगः स एधते यं-यं ... ||

2.26.d: रजुरिच्छंसो वनवद वनुष्यतो देवयन्निददेवयन्तमभ्यसत | सुप्रावीरिद वनवत पर्त्सु दुष्टरं यज्वेदयज्योर्वि भजाति भोजनम ||
2.26.e: THE righteous singer shall o’ercome his enemies, and he who serves the Gods subdue the godless man.  The zealous man shall vanquish the invincible, the worshipper share the food of him who worships not.

2.26.d: यजस्व वीर पर विहि मनायतो भद्रं मनः कर्णुष्व वर्त्रतूर्ये | हविष कर्णुष्व सुभगो यथाससि बरह्मणस पतेरव आ वर्णीमहे ||
2.26.e: Worship, thou hero, chase the arrogant afar: put on auspicious courage for the fight with foes.  Prepare oblation so that thou mayst have success. we crave the favouring help of Brahmaṇaspati.

2.26.d: स इज्जनेन स विशा स जन्मना स पुत्रैर्वाजं भरतेधना नर्भिः | देवानां यः पितरमाविवासति शरद्धामना हविषा बरह्मणस पतिम ||
2.26.e: He with his folk, his house, his family, his sons, gains booty for himself, and, with the heroes, wealth,  Who with oblation and a true believing heart serves Brahmaṇaspati the Father of the Gods.

2.26.d: यो अस्मै हव्यैर्घ्र्तवद्भिरविधत पर तं पराचा नयति बरह्मणस पतिः | उरुष्यतीमंहसो रक्षती रिषो.अंहोश्चिदस्मा उरुचक्रिरद्भुतः ||
2.26.e: Whoso hath honoured him with offerings rich in oil, him Brahmaṇaspati leads forward on his way,  Saves him from sorrow, frees him from his enemy, and is his wonderful deliverer from woe.

2.27.d: इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो घर्तस्नूः सनाद राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि | शर्णोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ||
2.27.e: THESE hymns that drop down fatness, with the ladle I ever offer to the Kings Ādityas.  May Mitra, Aryaman, and Bhaga hear us, the mighty Varuṇa Dakṣa, and Aṁśa.

2.27.d: इमं सतोमं सक्रतवो मे अद्य मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणो जुषन्त | आदित्यासः शुचयो धारपूता अव्र्जिना अनवद्या अरिष्टाः ||
2.27.e: With one accord may Aryaman and Mitra and Varuṇa this day accept this praise-song—  Ādityas bright and pure as streams of water, free from all guile and falsehood, blameless, perfect.

2.27.d: त आदित्यास उरवो गभीरा अदब्धासो दिप्सन्तो भूर्यक्षाः | अन्तः पश्यन्ति वर्जिनोत साधु सर्वं राजभ्यः परमा चिदन्ति ||
2.27.e: These Gods, Ādityas, vast, profound, and faithful, with many eyes, fain to deceive the wicked,  Looking within behold the good and evil near to the Kings is even the thing most distant.

2.27.d: धारयन्त आदित्यासो जगत सथा देवा विश्वस्य भुवनस्य गोपाः | दीर्घाधियो रक्षमाणा असुर्यं रतावानश्चयमाना रणानि ||
2.27.e: Upholding that which moves and that which moves not, Ādityas, Gods, protectors of all being,  Provident, guarding well the world of spirits, true to eternal Law, the debt-exactors.

2.27.d: विद्यामादित्या अवसो वो अस्य यदर्यमन भय आ चिन मयोभु | युष्माकं मित्रावरुणा परणीतौ परि शवभ्रेव दुरितानिव्र्ज्याम ||
2.27.e: May I, Ādityas, share m this your favour which, Aryaman, brings profit e’en in danger.  Under your guidance, Varuṇa and Mitra, round troubles may I pass, like rugged places.

2.27.d: सुगो हि वो अर्यमन मित्र पन्था अन्र्क्षरो वरुण साधुरस्ति | तेनादित्या अधि वोचता नो यछता नो दुष्परिहन्तु शर्म ||
2.27.e: Smooth is your path, O Aryaman and Mitra; excellent is it, Varuṇa, and thornless.  Thereon, Ādityas, send us down your blessing: grant us a shelter hard to be demolished.

2.27.d: पिपर्तु नो अदिती राजपुत्राति दवेषांस्यर्यमा सुगेभिः | बर्हन मित्रस्य वरुणस्य शर्मोप सयाम पुरुवीरा अरिष्टाः ||
2.27.e: Mother of Kings, may Aditi transport us, by fair paths Aryaman, beyond all hatred.  May we uninjured, girt by many heroes, win Varuṇa's and Mitra's high protection.

2.27.d: तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन तरीन्रुत दयून तरीणि वरता विदथे अन्तरेषाम | रतेनादित्या महि वो महित्वं तदर्यमन वरुण मित्र चारु ||
2.27.e: With their support they stay three earths, three heavens; three are their functions in the Gods’ assembly.  Mighty through Law, Ādityas, is your greatness; fair is it, Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Mitra.

2.27.d: तरी रोचना दिव्या धारयन्त हिरण्ययाः शुचयो धारपूताः | अस्वप्नजो अनिमिषा अदब्धा उरुशंसा रजवे मर्त्याय ||
2.27.e: Golden and splendid, pure like streams of water, they hold aloft the three bright heavenly regions.  Ne’er do they slumber, never close their eyelids, faithful, far-ruling for the righteous mortal.

2.27.d: तवं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ये च देवा असुर ये च मर्ताः | शतं नो रास्व शरदो विचक्षे.अच्यामायूंषि सुधितानि पूर्वा ||
2.27.e: Thou over all, O Varuṇa, art Sovran, be they Gods, Asura! or be they mortals.  Grant unto us to see a hundred autumns ours be the blest long lives of our forefathers.

2.27.d: न दक्षिणा वि चिकिते न सव्या न पराचीनमादित्या नोतपश्चा | पाक्या चिद वसवो धीर्या चिद युष्मानीतो अभयंज्योतिरश्याम ||
2.27.e: Neither the right nor left do I distinguish, neither the cast nor yet the west, Ādityas.  Simple and guided by your wisdom, Vasus! may I attain the light that brings no danger.

2.27.d: यो राजभ्य रतनिभ्यो ददाश यं वर्धयन्ति पुष्टयश्चनित्याः | स रेवान याति परथमो रथेन वसुदावा विदथेषु परशस्तः ||
2.27.e: He who bears gifts unto the Kings, true Leaders, he whom their everlasting blessings prosper,  Moves with his chariot first in rank and wealthy, munificent and lauded in assemblies.

2.27.d: शुचिरपः सूयवसा अदब्ध उप कषेति वर्द्धवयाः सुवीरः | नकिष टं घनन्त्यन्तितो न दूराद य आदित्यानां भवति परणीतौ ||
2.27.e: Pure, faithful, very strong, with heroes round him, he dwells beside the waters rich with pasture.  None slays, from near at hand or from a distance, him who is under the Ādityas’ guidance.

2.27.d: अदिते मित्र वरुणोत मर्ळ यद वो वयं चक्र्मा कच्चिदागः | उर्वश्यामभयं जयोतिरिन्द्र मा नो दीर्घा अभि नशन तमिस्राः ||
2.27.e: Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa, forgive us however we have erred and sinned against you.  May I obtain the broad light free from peril: O Indra, let not during darkness seize us.

2.27.d: उभे अस्मै पीपयतः समीची दिवो वर्ष्टिं सुभगो नाम पुष्यन | उभा कषयावाजयन याति पर्त्सूभावर्धौ भवतः साधू अस्मै ||
2.27.e: For him the Twain united pour their fulness, the rain from heaven: he thrives most highly favoured.  He goes to war mastering both the mansions: to him both portions of the world are gracious.

2.27.d: या वो माया अभिद्रुहे यजत्राः पाशा आदित्या रिपवे विच्र्त्ताः | अश्वीव तानति येषं रथेनारिष्टा उरावा शर्मन सयाम ||
2.27.e: Your guiles, ye Holy Ones, to quell oppressors, your snares spread out against the foe, Ādityas,  May I car-borne pass like a skilful horseman: uninjured may we dwell in spacious shelter.

2.27.d: माहं मघोनो वरुण परियस्य भूरिदाव्न आ विदं शूनमापेः | मा रायो राजन सुयमादव सथां बर्हद वदेम ... ||
2.27.e: May I not live, O Varuṇa, to witness my wealthy, liberal, dear friend's destitution.  King, may O never lack well-ordered riches. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.28.d: इदं कवेरादित्यस्य सवराजो विश्वानि सान्त्यभ्यस्तु मह्ना | अति यो मन्द्रो यजथाय देवः सुकीर्तिं भिक्षे वरुणस्य भूरेः ||
2.28.e: THIS laud of the self-radiant wise Āditya shall be supreme o’er all that is in greatness.

2.28.d: तव वरते सुभगासः सयाम सवाध्यो वरुण तुष्टुवांसः | उपायन उषसां गोमतीनामग्नयो न जरमाणा अनु दयून ||
2.28.e: beg renown of Varuṇa the Mighty, the God exceeding kind to him who worships.

2.28.d: तव सयाम पुरुवीरस्य शर्मन्नुरुशंसस्य वरुण परणेतः | यूयं नः पुत्रा अदितेरदब्धा अभि कषमध्वं युज्याय देवाः ||
2.28.e: Having extolled thee. Varuṇa, with thoughtful care may we have high fortune in thy service,  Singing thy praises like the fires at coming, day after day, of mornings rich in cattle.

2.28.d: पर सीमादित्यो अस्र्जद विधर्तान रतं सिन्धवो वरुणस्य यन्ति | न शराम्यन्ति न वि मुचन्त्येते वयो न पप्तू रघुयापरिज्मन ||
2.28.e: May we be in thy keeping, O thou Leader wide-ruling Varuṇa, Lord of many heroes.  O sons of Aditi, for ever faithful, pardon us, Gods, admit us to your friendship.

2.28.d: वि मच्छ्रथाय रशनामिवाग रध्याम ते वरुण खां रतस्य | मा तन्तुश्छेदि वयतो धियं मे मा मात्रा शार्यपसः पुर रतोः ||
2.28.e: He made them flow, the Āditya, the Sustainer: the rivers run by Varuṇa's commandment.  These feel no weariness, nor cease from flowing: swift have they flown like birds in air around us.

2.28.d: अपो सु मयक्ष वरुण भियसं मत सम्राळ रतावो.अनु मा गर्भाय | दामेव वत्साद वि मुमुग्ध्यंहो नहि तवदारे निमिषश्चनेशे ||
2.28.e: Loose me from sin as from a bond that binds me: may we swell, Varuṇa, thy spring of Order.  Let not my thread, while I weave song, be severed, nor my work's sum, before the time, be shattered.

2.28.d: मा नो वधैर्वरुण ये त इष्टावेनः कर्ण्वन्तमसुर भरीणन्ति | मा जयोतिषः परवसथानि गन्म वि षू मर्धः शिश्रथो जीवसे नः ||
2.28.e: Far from me, Varuṇa, remove all danger accept me graciously, thou Holy Sovran.  Cast off, like cords that hold a calf, my troubles: I am not even mine eyelid's lord without thee.

2.28.d: नमः पुरा ते वरुणोत नूनमुतापरं तुविजात बरवाम | तवे हि कं पर्वते न शरितान्यप्रच्युतानि दूळभ वरतानि ||
2.28.e: Strike us not, Varuṇa, with those dread weapons which, Asura, at thy bidding wound the sinner.  Let us not pass away from light to exile. Scatter, that we may live, the men who hate us

2.28.d: पर रणा सावीरध मत्क्र्तानि माहं राजन्नन्यक्र्तेन भोजम | अव्युष्टा इन नु भूयसीरुषास आ नो जीवान वरुण तासु शाधि ||
2.28.e: O mighty Varuṇa, now and hereafter, even as of old, will we speak forth our worship.  For in thyself, invincible God, thy statutes ne’er to be moved are fixed as on a mountain.

2.28.d: यो मे राजन युज्यो वा सखा वा सवप्ने भयं भीरवे मह्यमाह | सतेनो वा यो दिप्सति नो वर्को वा तवं तस्माद वरुणपाह्यस्मान ||
2.28.e: Move far from me what sins I have committed: let me not suffer, King, for guilt of others.  Full many a morn remains to dawn upon us: in these, O Varuṇa, while we live direct us.
O King, whoever, be he friend or kinsman, hath threatened me affrighted in my slumber-  If any wolf or robber fain would harm us, therefrom, O Varuṇa, give thou us protection.

2.29.d: धर्तव्रता आदित्या इषिरा आरे मत कर्त रहसूरिवागः | शर्ण्वतो वो वरुण मित्र देवा भद्रस्य विद्वानवसे हुवेवः ||
2.29.e: UPHOLDERS of the Law, ye strong Ādityas, remove my sin like her who bears in secret.  You, Varuṇa, Mitra and all Gods who listen, I call to help me, I who know your goodness.

2.29.d: यूयं देवाः परमतिर्यूयमोजो यूयं दवेषांसि सनुतर्युयोत | अभिक्षत्तारो अभि च कषमध्वमद्या च नो मर्ळयतापरं च ||
2.29.e: Ye, Gods, are providence and ye are power: remove ye utterly all those who hate us.  As givers of good things deal with us kindly: this day be gracious to us and hereafter.

2.29.d: किमू नु वः कर्णवामापरेण किं सनेन वसव आप्येन | यूयं नो मित्रावरुणादिते च सवस्तिमिन्द्रामरुतो दधात ||
2.29.e: What service may we do you with our future, what service, Vasus, with our ancient friendship?  O Aditi, and Varuṇa and Mitra, Indra and Maruts, make us well and happy.

2.29.d: हये देवा यूयमिदापय सथ ते मर्ळत नाधमानाय मह्यम | मा वो रथो मध्यमवाळ रते भून मा युष्मावस्त्वापिषु शरमिष्म ||
2.29.e: Ye, O ye Gods, are verily our kinsmen as such be kind to me who now implore you.  Let not your car come slowly to our worship: of kinsmen such as you ne’er let us weary.

2.29.d: पर व एको मिमय भूर्यागो यन मा पितेव कितवं शशास | आरे पाषा आरे अघानि देवा मा माधि पुत्रे विमिव गरभीष्ट ||
2.29.e: I singly have sinned many a sin against you, and ye chastised me as a sire the gambler.  Far be your nets, far, Gods, be mine offences: seize me not like a bird upon her offspring.

2.29.d: अर्वाञ्चो अद्या भवता यजत्रा आ वो हार्दि भयमानो वययेयम | तराध्वं नो देवा निजुरो वर्कस्य तराध्वं कर्तादवपदो यजत्राः ||
2.29.e: Turn yourselves hitherward this day, ye Holy, that fearing in my heart I may approach you.  Protect us, God; let not the wolf destroy us. Save us, ye Holy, from the pit and falling.
May I not live, O Varuṇa, to witness my wealthy, liberal, dear friend's destitution.  King, may I never lack well-ordered riches. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.30.d: रतं देवाय कर्ण्वते सवित्र इन्द्रायाहिघ्ने न रमन्त आपः | अहर-अहर्यात्यक्तुरपां कियात्या परथमः सर्ग आसाम ||
2.30.e: THE streams unceasing flow to Indra, slayer of Ahi, Savitar, God, Law's fulfiller,  Day after day goes on the sheen of waters. What time hath past since they were first set flowing?

2.30.d: यो वर्त्राय सिनमत्राभरिष्यत पर तं जनित्री विदुष उवाच | पथो रदन्तीरनु जोषमस्मै दिवे-दिवे धुनयो यन्त्यर्थम ||
2.30.e: His Mother—for she knew—spake and proclaimed him who was about to cast his bolt at Vṛtra.  Cutting their paths according to his pleasure day after day flow to their goal the rivers.

2.30.d: ऊर्ध्वो हयस्थादध्यन्तरिक्षे.अधा वर्त्राय पर वधंजभार | मिहं वसान उप हीमदुद्रोत तिग्मायुधो अजयच्छत्रुमिन्द्रः ||
2.30.e: Aloft he stood above the airy region, and against Vṛtra shot his deadly missile.  Enveloped in a cloud he rushed upon him. Indra subdued the foe with sharpened weapons.
