2.30.d: बर्हस्पते तपुषाश्नेव विध्य वर्कद्वरसो असुरस्य वीरान | यथा जघन्थ धर्षता पुरा चिदेवा जहि शत्रुमस्माकमिन्द्र ||
2.30.e: As with a bolt, Bṛhaspati, fiercely flaming, pierce thou Vṛkadvaras’, the Asura's, heroes.  Even as in time of old with might thou slewest, so slay even now our enemy, O Indra.

2.30.d: अव कषिप दिवो अश्मानमुच्चा येन शत्रुं मन्दसानो निजूर्वाः | तोकस्य सातौ तनयस्य भूरेरस्मानर्धं कर्णुतादिन्द्र गोनाम ||
2.30.e: Cast down from heaven on high thy bolt of thunder wherewith in joy thou smitest dead the foeman.  For gain of children make us thine, O Indra, of many children's children and of cattle.

2.30.d: पर हि करतुं वर्हथो यं वनुथो रध्रस्य सथो यजमानस्य चोदौ | इन्द्रासोमा युवमस्मानविष्टमस्मिन भयस्थे कर्णुतमु लोकम ||
2.30.e: Whomso ye love, his power ye aid and strengthen; ye Twain are the rich worshipper's advancers.  Graciously favour us, Indra and Soma; give us firm standing in this time of danger.

2.30.d: न मा तमन न शरमन नोत तन्द्रन न वोचाम मा सुनोतेति सोमम | यो मे पर्णाद यो ददद यो निबोधाद यो मा सुन्वन्तमुप गोभिरायत ||
2.30.e: Let it not vex me, tire me, make me slothful, and never let us say, Press not the Soma;  For him who cares for me, gives gifts, supports me, who comes with kine to me who pour libations.

2.30.d: सरस्वति तवमस्मानविड्ढि मरुत्वती धर्षती जेषि शत्रून | तयं चिच्छर्धन्तं तविषीयमाणमिन्द्रो हन्ति वर्षभं शण्डिकानाम ||
2.30.e: Sarasvatī, protect us: with the Maruts allied thou boldly conquerest our foemen,  While Indra does to death the daring chieftain of Śaṇḍikas exulting in his prowess.

2.30.d: यो नः सनुत्य उत वा जिघत्नुरभिख्याय तं तिगितेन विध्य | बर्हस्पत आयुधैर्जेषि शत्रून दरुहे रीषन्तं परि धेहि राजन ||
2.30.e: Him who waylays, yea, him who would destroy us,—aim at him, pierce him with thy sharpened weapon.  Bṛhaspati, with arms thou slayest foemen O King, give up the spoiler to destruction.

2.30.d: अस्माकेभिः सत्वभिः शूर शूरैर्वीर्य कर्धि यानि ते कर्त्वानि | जयोगभूवन्ननुधूपितासो हत्वी तेशामा भरानो वसूनि ||
2.30.e: Perform, O Hero, with our valiant heroes the deeds heroic which thou hast to finish.  Long have they been inflated with presumption: slay them, and bring us hither their possessions.

2.30.d: तं वः शर्धं मारुतं सुम्नयुर्गिरोप बरुवे नमसा दैव्यं जनम | यथा रयिं सर्ववीरं नशामहा अपत्यसाचं शरुत्यं दिवे-दिवे ||
2.30.e: I craving joy address with hymn and homage your heavenly host, the company of Maruts,  That we may gain wealth with full store of heroes, each day more famous, and with troops of children.

2.31.d: अस्माकं मित्रावरुणावतं रथमादित्यै रुद्रैर्वसुभिः सचाभुवा | पर यद वयो न पप्तन वस्मनस परि शरवस्यवोह्र्षीवन्तो वनर्षदः ||
2.31.e: HELP, Varuṇa and Mitra, O ye Twain allied with Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, help our car,  That, as the wild birds of the forest from their home, our horses may fly forth, glad, eager for renown.

2.31.d: अध समा न उदवता सजोषसो रथं देवासो अभि विक्षु वाजयुम | यदाशवः पद्याभिस्तित्रतो रजः पर्थिव्याः सानौ जङघनन्त पाणिभिः ||
2.31.e: Yea, now ye Gods of one accord speed on our car what time among the folk it seeks an act of might;  When, hasting through the region with the stamp of hoofs, our swift steeds trample on the ridges of the earth.

2.31.d: उत सय न इन्द्रो विश्वचर्षणिर्दिवः शर्धेन मारुतेन सुक्रतुः | अनु नु सथात्यव्र्काभिरूतिभी रथं महे सनये वाजसातये ||
2.31.e: Or may our Indra here, the Friend of all mankind, coming from heaven, most wise, girt by the Marut host,  Accompany, with aid untroubled by a foe, our car to mighty gain, to win the meed of strength.

2.31.d: उत सय देवो भुवनस्य सक्षणिस्त्वष्टा गनाभिः सजोषा जूजुवद रथम | इळा भगो बर्हद्दिवोत रोदसी पूषा पुरन्धिरश्विनावधा पती ||
2.31.e: Or may this Tvaṣṭar, God who rules the world with power, one-minded with the Goddesses speed forth our car;  Iḷā and Bhaga the celestial, Earth and Heaven, Pūṣan, Purandhi, and the Aśvins, ruling Lords.

2.31.d: उत तये देवी सुभगे मिथूद्र्शोषासानक्ता जगतामपीजुवा | सतुषे यद वां पर्थिवि नव्यसा वच सथातुश्च वयस्त्रिवया उपस्तिरे ||
2.31.e: Or, seen alternate, those two blessed Goddesses, Morning and Night who stir all living things to act:  While with my newest song I praise you both, O Earth, that from what moves not ye may spread forth threefold food.

2.31.d: उत वः शंसमुशिजामिव शमस्यहिर्बुध्न्यो.अज एकपादुत | तरित रभुक्षाः सविता चनो दधे.अपां नपादाशुहेमा धिया शमि ||
2.31.e: Your blessing as a boon for suppliants we desire: the Dragon of the Deep, and Aja-Ekapād,  Trita, Ṛbhukṣan, Savitar shall joy in us, and the Floods’ swift Child in our worship and our prayer.

2.31.d: एता वो वश्म्युद्यता यजत्रा अतक्षन्नायवो नव्यसे सम | शरवस्यवो वाजं चकानाः सप्तिर्न रथ्यो अह धीतिमश्याः ||
2.31.e: These earnest prayers I pray to you, ye Holy: to pay you honour, living men have formed them,  Men fain to win the prize and glory. May they win, as a car-horse might the goal, your notice.

2.32.d: अस्य मे दयावाप्र्थिवी रतायतो भूतमवित्री वचसः सिषासतः | ययोरायः परतरं ते इदं पुर उपस्तुते वसूयुर्वां महो दधे ||
2.32.e: GRACIOUSLY further, O ye Heaven and Earth, this speech striving to win reward, of me your worshipper.  First rank I give to you, Immortal, high extolled! I, fain to win me wealth, to you the mighty Pair.

2.32.d: मा नो गुह्या रिप आयोरहन दभन मा न आभ्यो रीरधो दुछुनाभ्यः | मा नो वि यौः सख्या विद्धि तस्य नः सुम्नायता मनसा तत तवेमहे ||
2.32.e: Let not man's guile annoy us, secret or by day: give not us up a prey to these calamities.  Sever not thou our friendship: think thereon for us. This, with a heart that longs for bliss, we seek from thee.

2.32.d: अहेळता मनसा शरुष्टिमा वह दुहानां धेनुं पिप्युषीमसश्चतम | पद्याभिराशुं वचसा च वाजिनं तवां हिनोमि पुरुहूत विश्वहा ||
2.32.e: Bring hither with benignant mind the willing Cow teeming with plenteous milk, full, inexhaustible.  O thou invoked by many, day by day I urge thee with my word, a charger rapid in his tread.

2.32.d: राकामहं सुहवां सुष्टुती हुवे शर्णोतु नः सुभगा बोधतु तमना | सीव्यत्वपः सूच्याछिद्यमानया ददातु वीरं सतदायमुक्थ्यम ||
2.32.e: With eulogy I call on Rākā swift to hear may she, auspicious, hear us, and herself observe.  With never-breaking needle may she sew her work, and give a hero son most wealthy, meet for praise.

2.32.d: यास्ते राके सुमतयः सुपेशसो याभिर्ददासि दाशुषे वसूनि | ताभिर्नो अद्य सुमना उपागहि सहस्रपोषं सुभगे रराणा ||
2.32.e: All thy kind thoughts, O Rākā, lovely in their form, wherewith thou grantest wealth to him who offers gifts—  With these come thou to us this day benevolent, O Blessed One, bestowing food of thousand sorts.

2.32.d: सिनीवालि पर्थुष्टुके या देवानामसि सवसा | जुषस्व हव्यमाहुतं परजां देवि दिदिड्ढि नः ||
2.32.e: O broad-tressed Sinīvālī, thou who art the Sister of the Gods,  Accept the offered sacrifice, and, Goddess, grant us progeny.

2.32.d: या सुबाहुः सवङगुरिः सुषूमा बहुसूवरी | तस्यै विश्पत्न्यै हविः सिनीवाल्यै जुहोतन ||
2.32.e: With lovely fingers, lovely arms, prolific Mother of many sons—  Present the sacred gifts to her, to Sinīvālī Queen of men.

2.32.d: या गुङगूर्या सिनीवाली या राका या सरस्वती | इन्द्राणीमह्व ऊतये वरुणानीं सवस्तये ||
2.32.e: Her, Sinīvālī, her, Gungū, her, Rākā, her, Sarasvatī, Indrāṇī to mine aid I call, and Varuṇānī for my weal.

2.33.d: आ ते पितर्मरुतां सुम्नमेतु मा नः सूर्यस्य सन्द्र्षो युयोथाः | अभि नो वीरो अर्वति कषमेत पर जायेमहि रुद्र परजाभिः ||
2.33.e: FATHER of Maruts, let thy bliss approach us: exclude us not from looking on the sunlight.  Gracious to our fleet courser be the Hero may we transplant us, Rudra, in our children.

2.33.d: तवादत्तेभी रुद्र शन्तमेभिः शतं हिमा अशीय भेषजेभिः | वयस्मद दवेषो वितरं वयंहो वयमीवाश्चातयस्वा विषूचीः ||
2.33.e: With the most saving medicines which thou givest, Rudra, may I attain a hundred winters.  Far from us banish enmity and hatred, and to all quarters maladies and trouble.

2.33.d: शरेष्ठो जातस्य रुद्र शरियासि तवस्तमस्तवसां वज्रबाहो | पर्षि णः पारमंहसः सवस्ति विश्वा अभीती रपसो युयोधि ||
2.33.e: Chief of all born art thou in glory, Rudra, armed with the thunder, mightiest of the mighty.  Transport us over trouble to well-being repel thou from us all assaults of mischief.

2.33.d: मा तवा रुद्र चुक्रुधामा नमोभिर्मा दुष्टुती वर्षभ मासहूती | उन नो वीरानर्पय भेषजेभिर्भिषक्तमं तवा भिषजां शर्णोमि ||
2.33.e: Let us not anger thee with worship, Rudra, ill praise, Strong God! or mingled invocation.  Do thou with strengthening balms incite our heroes: I hear thee famed as best of all physicians.

2.33.d: हवीमभिर्हवते यो हविर्भिरव सतोमेभी रुद्रं दिषीय | रदूदरः सुहवो मा नो अस्यै बभ्रुः सुशिप्रो रीरधन मनायै ||
2.33.e: May I with praise-songs win that Rudra's favour who is adored with gifts and invocations.  Ne’er may the tawny God, fair-checked, and gracious, swifthearing, yield us to this evil purpose.

2.33.d: उन मा ममन्द वर्षभो मरुत्वान तवक्षीयसा वयसा नाधमानम | घर्णीव छायामरपा अशीया विवासेयं रुद्रस्य सुम्नम ||
2.33.e: The Strong, begirt by Maruts, hath refreshed me, with most invigorating food, imploring.  As he who finds a shade in fervent sunlight may I, uninjured, win the bliss of Rudra.

2.33.d: कव सय ते रुद्र मर्ळयाकुर्हस्तो यो अस्ति भेषजो जलाषः | अपभर्ता रपसो दैव्यस्याभी नु मा वर्षभ चक्षमीथाः ||
2.33.e: Where is that gracious hand of thine, O Rudra, the hand that giveth health and bringeth comfort,  Remover of the woe that Gods have sent us? O Strong One, look thou on me with compassion.

2.33.d: पर बभ्रवे वर्षभाय शवितीचे महो महीं सुष्टुतिमीरयामि | नमस्या कल्मलीकिनं नमोभिर्ग्र्णीमसि तवेषं रुद्रस्य नाम ||
2.33.e: To him the strong, great, tawny, fair-complexioned, I utter forth a mighty hymn of praises.  We serve the brilliant God with adorations, we glorify, the splendid name of Rudra.

2.33.d: सथिरेभिरङगैः पुरुरूप उग्रो बभ्रुः शुक्रेभिः पिपिशेहिरण्यैः | ईशानादस्य भुवनस्य भूरेर्न वा उ योषद रुद्रादसुर्यम ||
2.33.e: With firm limbs, multiform, the strong, the tawny adorns himself with bright gold decorations:  The strength of Godhead ne’er departs from Rudra, him who is Sovran of this world, the mighty.

2.33.d: अर्हन बिभर्षि सायकानि धन्वार्हन निष्कं यजतं विश्वरूपम | अर्हन्निदं दयसे विश्वमभ्वं न वा ओजीयो रुद्र तवदस्ति ||
2.33.e: Worthy, thou carriest thy bow and arrows, worthy, thy manyhued and honoured necklace.  Worthy, thou cuttest here each fiend to pieces: a mightier than thou there is not, Rudra.

2.33.d: सतुहि शरुतं गर्तसदं युवानं मर्गं न भीममुपहत्नुमुग्रम | मर्ला जरित्रे रुद्र सतवानो.अन्यं ते अस्मन नि वपन्तु सेनाः ||
2.33.e: Praise him the chariot-borne, the young, the famous, fierce, slaying like a dread beast of the forest.  O Rudra, praised, be gracious to the singer. let thy hosts spare us and smite down another.

2.33.d: कुमारश्चित पितरं वन्दमानं परति नानाम रुद्रोपयन्तम | भूरेर्दातारं सत्पतिं गर्णीषे सतुतस्त्वं भेषजा रास्यस्मे ||
2.33.e: I bend to thee as thou approachest, Rudra, even as a boy before the sire who greets him.  I praise thee Bounteous Giver, Lord of heroes: give medicines to us as thou art lauded.

2.33.d: या वो भेषजा मरुतः शुचीनि या शन्तमा वर्षणो या मयोभु | यानि मनुरव्र्णीता पिता नस्ता शं च योश्चरुद्रस्य वश्मि ||
2.33.e: Of your pure medicines, O potent Maruts, those that are wholesomest and health-bestowing,  Those which our father Manu hath selected, I crave from. Rudra for our gain and welfare.

2.33.d: परि णो हेती रुद्रस्य वर्ज्याः परि तवेषस्य दुर्मतिर्महीगात | अव सथिरा मघवद्भ्यस्तनुष्व मीढ्वस्तोकाय तनयाय मर्ळ ||
2.33.e: May Rudra's missile turn aside and spare us, the great wrath of the impetuous One avoid us.  Turn, Bounteous God, thy strong bow from our princes, and be thou gracious to our seed and offspring.

2.33.d: एवा बभ्रो वर्षभ चेकितान यथा देव न हर्णीषे न हंसि | हवनश्रुन नो रुद्रेह बोधि बर्हद व. व. स. ||
2.33.e: O tawny Bull, thus showing forth thy nature, as neither to be wroth, O God, nor slay us.  Here, Rudra, listen to our invocation. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.34.d: धारावरा मरुतो धर्ष्ण्वोजसो मर्गा न भीमास्तविषीभिरर्चिनः | अग्नयो न शुशुचाना रजीषिणो भर्मिं धमन्तोप गा अव्र्ण्वत ||
2.34.e: THE Maruts of resistless might who love the rain, resplendent, terrible like wild beasts in their strength,  Glowing like flames of fire, impetuous in career, blowing the wandering rain-cloud, have disclosed the kine.

2.34.d: दयावो न सत्र्भिश्चितयन्त खादिनो वयभ्रिया न दयुतयन्तव्र्ष्टयः | रुद्रो यद वो मरुतो रुक्मवक्षसो वर्षाजनि पर्श्न्याः शुक्र ऊधनि ||
2.34.e: They gleam with armlets as the heavens are decked with stars, like cloud-born lightnings shine the torrents of their rain.  Since the strong Rudra, O Maruts with brilliant chests, sprang into life for you in Pṛśni's radiant lap.

2.34.d: उक्षन्ते अश्वानत्यानिवाजिषु नदस्य कर्णैस्तुरयन्त आशुभिः | हिरण्यशिप्रा मरुतो दविध्वतः पर्क्षं याथ पर्षतीभिः समन्यवः ||
2.34.e: They drip like horses in the racings of swift steeds; with the stream's rapid cars they hasten on their way.  Maruts with helms of gold, ye who make all things shake,  come  with your spotted deer, one-minded, to our food.

2.34.d: पर्क्षे ता विश्वा भुवना ववक्षिरे मित्राय वा सदमा जीरदानवः | पर्षदश्वासो अनवभ्रराधस रजिप्यासो न वयुनेषु धूर्षदः ||
2.34.e: They have bestowed of Mitra all that live, to feed, they who for evermore cause their swift drops to flow;  Whose steeds are spotted deer, whose riches never fail, like horses in full speed, bound to the pole in work.

2.34.d: इन्धन्वभिर्धेनुभी रप्शदूधभिरध्वस्मभिः पथिभिर्भ्राजद्र्ष्टयः | आ हंसासो न सवसराणि गन्तन मधोर्मदाय मरुतः समन्यवः ||
2.34.e: With brightly-flaming kine whose udders swell with milk, with glittering lances on your unobstructed paths,  O Maruts, of one mind, like swans who seek their nests, come to the rapturous enjoyment of the meath.

2.34.d: आ नो बरह्माणि मरुतः समन्यवो नरां न शंसः सवनानि गन्तन | अश्वामिव पिप्यत धेनुमूधनि कर्ता धियं जरित्रे वाजपेशसम ||
2.34.e: To these our prayers, O Maruts, come unanimous, come ye to our libations like the praise of men.  Make it swell like a mare, in udder like a cow, and for the singer grace the song with plenteous strength.

2.34.d: तं नो दात मरुतो वाजिनं रथ आपानं बरह्म चितयद दिवे-दिवे | इषं सतोत्र्भ्यो वर्जनेषु कारवे सनिं मेधामरिष्टं दुष्टरं सहः ||
2.34.e: Give us a steed, O Maruts mighty in the car; prevailing prayer that brings remembrance day by day;  Food to your praisers, to your bard in deeds of might give winning wisdom, power uninjured, unsurpassed.

2.34.d: यद युञ्जते मरुतो रुक्मवक्षसो.अश्वान रथेषु भग आ सुदानवः | धेनुर्न शिश्वे सवसरेषु पिन्वते जनाय रातहविषे महीमिषम ||
2.34.e: When the bright-chested Maruts, lavish of their gifts, bind at the time bliss their horses to the cars,  Then, as the milch-cow feeds her calf within the stalls, they pour forth food for all oblation-bringing men.

2.34.d: यो नो मरुतो वर्कताति मर्त्यो रिपुर्दधे वसवो रक्षता रिषः | वर्तयत तपुषा चक्रियाभि तमव रुद्रा अशसो हन्तना वधः ||
2.34.e: Save us, O Maruts, Vasus, from the injurer, the mortal foe who makes us looked upon as wolves.  With chariot all aflame compass him round about: O Rudras, cast away the foeman's deadly bolt.

2.34.d: चित्रं तद वो मरुतो याम चेकिते पर्श्न्या यदूधरप्यापयो दुहुः | यद वा निदे नवमानस्य रुद्रियास्त्रितं जरायजुरतामदाभ्याः ||
2.34.e: Well-known, ye Maruts, is that wondrous course of yours, when they milked Pṛśni's udder, close akin to her.  Or when to shame the bard who lauded, Rudra's Sons, ye O infallible brought Trita to decay.

2.34.d: तान वो महो मरुत एवयाव्नो विष्णोरेषस्य परभ्र्थे हवामहे | हिरण्यवर्णान ककुहान यतस्रुचो बरह्मण्यन्तः शंस्यं राध ईमहे ||
2.34.e: We call you such, great Maruts, following wonted ways, to the oblation paid to Viṣṇu Speeder-on.  With ladles lifted up, with prayer, we seek of them preeminent, golden-hued, the wealth which all extol.

2.34.d: ते दशग्वाः परथमा यज्ञमूहिरे ते नो हिन्वन्तूषसो वयुष्टिषु | उषा न रामीररुणैरपोर्णुते महो जयोतिषाशुचता गोर्णसा ||
2.34.e: They, the Daśagvas, first of all brought sacrifice: they at the break of mornings shall inspirit us.  Dawn with her purple beams uncovereth the nights, with great light glowing like a billowy sea of milk.

2.34.d: ते कषोणीभिररुणेभिर्नाञ्जिभी रुद्रा रतस्य सदनेषुवाव्र्धुः | निमेघमाना अत्येन पाजसा सुश्चन्द्रं वर्णन्दधिरे सुपेशसम ||
2.34.e: The Rudras have rejoiced them in the gathered bands at seats of worship as in purple ornaments.  They with impetuous vigour sending down the rain have taken to themselves a bright and lovely hue.

2.34.d: तानियानो महि वरूथमूतय उप घेदेना नमसा गर्णीमसि | तरितो न यान पञ्च होतॄनभिष्टय आववर्तदवराञ्चक्रियावसे ||
2.34.e: Soliciting their high protection for our help, with this our adoration we sing praise to them,  Whom, for assistance, like the five terrestrial priests. Trita hath brought to aid us hither on his car.

2.34.d: यया रध्रं पारयथात्यंहो यया निदो मुञ्चथ वन्दितारम | अर्वाची सा मरुतो या व ऊतिरो षु वाश्रेव सुमतिर्जिगातु ||
2.34.e: So may your favouring help be turned to us-ward, your kindness like a lowing cow approach us,  Wherewith ye bear your servant over trouble, and free your worshipper from scoff and scorning.

2.35.d: उपेमस्र्क्षि वाजयुर्वचस्यां चनो दधीत नाद्यो गिरो मे | अपां नपादाशुहेमा कुवित स सुपेशसस करति जोषिषद धि ||
2.35.e: EAGER for spoil my flow of speech I utter: may the Floods' Child accept my songs with favour.  Will not the rapid Son of Waters make them lovely, for he it is who shall enjoy them?

2.35.d: इमं सवस्मै हर्द आ सुतष्टं मन्त्रं वोचेम कुविदस्य वेदत | अपां नपादसुर्यस्य मह्ना विश्वान्यर्यो भुवना जजान ||
2.35.e: To him let us address the song well-fashioned, forth from the heart. Shall he not understand it'  The friendly Son of Waters by the greatness of Godhead hath produced all things existing.

2.35.d: समन्या यन्त्युप यन्त्यन्याः समानमूर्वं नद्यः पर्णन्ति | तमू शुचिं शुचयो दीदिवांसमपां नपातं परि तस्थुरापः ||
2.35.e: Some floods unite themselves and others join them: die sounding rivers fill one common storehouse.  On every side the bright Floods have encompassed the bright resplendent Offspring of the Waters.

2.35.d: तमस्मेरा युवतयो युवानं मर्म्र्ज्यमानाः परि यन्त्यापः | स शुक्रेभिः शिक्वभी रेवदस्मे दीदायानिध्मो घर्तनिर्णिगप्सु ||
2.35.e: The never-sullen waters, youthful Maidens, carefully decking, wait on him the youthful.  He with bright rays shines forth in splendid beauty, unfed with wood, in waters, oil-enveloped.

2.35.d: अस्मै तिस्रो अव्यथ्याय नारीर्देवाय देवीर्दिधिषन्त्यन्नम | कर्ता इवोप हि परसर्स्रे अप्सु स पीयूषं धयति पूर्वसूनाम ||
2.35.e: To him three Dames are offering food to feed him, Goddesses to the God whom none may injure.  Within the waters hath he pressed, as hollows, and drinks their milk who now are first made mothers.

2.35.d: अश्वस्यात्र जनिमास्य च सवर्द्रुहो रिषः सम्प्र्चः पाहिसूरीन | आमासु पूर्षु परो अप्रम्र्ष्यं नारातयो वि नशन नान्र्तानि ||
2.35.e: Here was the horse's birth; his was the sunlight. Save thou our princes from the oppressor's onslaught.  Him, indestructible, dwelling at a distance in forts unwrought lies and ill spirits reach not.

2.35.d: सव आ दमे सुदुघा यस्य धेनुः सवधां पीपाय सुभ्वन्नमत्ति | सो अपां नपादूर्जयन्नप्स्वन्तर्वसुदेयाय विधते वि भाति ||
2.35.e: He, in whose mansion is the teeming Milch-cow, swells the Gods’ nectar and cats noble viands.  The Son of Waters, gathering strength in waters, shines for his worshipper to give him treasures.

2.35.d: यो अप्स्वा सुचिना दैव्येन रतावाजस्र उर्विया विभाति | वया इदन्या भुवनान्यस्य पर जायन्ते वीरुधश्च परजाभिः ||
2.35.e: He who in waters with his own pure Godhead shines widely, law-abiding, everlasting—  The other worlds are verily his branches, and plants are born of him with all their offspring.

2.35.d: अपां नपादा हयस्थादुपस्थं जिह्मानामूर्ध्वो विद्युतं वसानः | तस्य जयेष्ठं महिमानं वहन्तीर्हिरण्यवर्णाः परि यन्ति यह्वीः ||
2.35.e: The Waters’ Son hath risen, and clothed in lightning ascended up unto the curled cloud's bosom;  And bearing with them his supremest glory the Youthful Ones, gold-coloured, move around him.

2.35.d: हिरण्यरूपः स हिरण्यसन्द्र्गपां नपात सेदु हिरण्यवर्णः | हिरण्ययात परि योनेर्निषद्या हिरण्यदा ददत्यन्नमस्मै ||
2.35.e: Golden in form is he, like gold to look on, his colour is like gold, the Son of Waters.  When he is seated fresh from golden birthplace those who present their gold give food to feed him.

2.35.d: तदस्यानीकमुत चारु नामापीच्यं वर्धते नप्तुरपाम | यमिन्धते युवतयः समित्था हिरण्यवर्णं घर्तमन्नमस्य ||
2.35.e: This the fair name and this the lovely aspect of him the Waters’ Son increase in secret.  Whom here the youthful Maids together kindle, his food is sacred oil of golden colour.

2.35.d: अस्मै बहूनामवमाय सख्ये यज्ञैर्विधेम नमसा हविर्भिः | सं सानु मार्ज्मि दिधिषामि बिल्मैर्दधाम्यन्नैःपरि वन्द रग्भिः ||
2.35.e: Him, nearest Friend of many, will we worship with sacrifice. and reverence and oblation.  I make his back to shine, with chips provide him; I offer food and with my songs exalt him.

2.35.d: स ईं वर्षाजनयत तासु गर्भं स ईं सिशुर्धयति तं रिहन्ति | सो अपां नपादनभिम्लातवर्णो.अन्यस्येवेह तन्वा विवेष ||
2.35.e: The Bull hath laid his own life-germ Within them. He sucks them as an infant, and they kiss him.  He, Son of Waters, of unfading colour, hath entered here as in another's body.

2.35.d: अस्मिन पदे परमे तस्थिवांसमध्वस्मभिर्विश्वहा दीदिवांसाम | आपो नप्त्रे घर्तमन्नं वहन्तीः सवयमत्कैः परि दीयन्ति यह्वीः ||
2.35.e: While here he dwelleth in sublimest station, resplendent with the rays that never perish,  The Waters, bearing oil to feed their offspring, flow, Youthful Ones, in wanderings about him.

2.35.d: अयांसमग्ने सुक्षितिं जनायायांसमु मघवद्भ्यः सुव्र्क्तिम | विश्वं तद ... ||
2.35.e: Agni, I gave good shelter to the people, and to the princes goodly preparation.  Blessed is all that Gods regard with favour. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.36.d: तुभ्यं हिन्वानो वसिष्ट गा अपो.अधुक्षन सीमविभिरद्रिभिर्नरः | पिबेन्द्र सवाहा परहुतं वषत्क्र्तं होत्रादासोमं परथमो य ईशिषे ||
2.36.e: WATER and milk hath he endued, sent forth to thee: the men have drained him with the filters and the stones.  Drink, Indra, from the Hotar's bowl—first right is thine—Soma hallowed and poured with Vaṣaṭ and Svāhā.

2.36.d: यज्ञैः सम्मिश्लाः पर्षतीभिर्र्ष्टिभिर्यामञ्छुभ्रासो अञ्जिषु परिया उत | आसद्या बर्हिर्भरतस्य सूनवः पोत्रादा सोमं पिबता दिवो नरः ||
2.36.e: Busied with sacrifice, with spotted deer and spears, gleaming upon your way with ornaments, yea, our Friends,  Sitting on sacred grass, ye Sons of Bhārata, drink Soma from the Potar's bowl, O Men of heaven.

2.36.d: अमेव नः सुहवा आ हि गन्तन नि बर्हिषि सदतना रणिष्टन | अथा मन्दस्व जुजुषाणो अन्धसस्त्वष्टर्देवेभिर्जनिभिः सुमद्गणः ||
2.36.e: Come unto us, ye swift to listen: as at home upon the sacred grass sit and enjoy yourselves.  And, Tvaṣṭar, well-content be joyful in the juice with Gods and Goddesses in gladsome company.

2.36.d: आ वक्षि देवानिह विप्र यक्षि चोशन होतर्नि षदा योनिषु तरिषु | परति वीहि परस्थितं सोम्यं मधु पिबाग्नीध्रात्तव भागस्य तर्प्णुहि ||
2.36.e: Bring the Gods hither, Sage, and offer sacrifice: at the three altars seat thee willingly, O Priest.  Accept for thy delight the proffered Soma meath: drink from the Kindler's bowl and fill thee with thy share.

2.36.d: एष सय ते तन्वो नर्म्णवर्धनः सह ओजः परदिवि बाह्वोर्हितः | तुभ्यं सुतो मघवन तुभ्यमाभ्र्तस्त्वमस्य बराह्मनादा तर्पत पिब ||
2.36.e: This is the strengthener of thy body's manly might: strength, victory for all time are placed within thine arms.  Pressed for thee, Maghavan, it is offered unto thee: drink from the chalice of this Brahman, drink thy fill.

2.36.d: जुषेथां यज्ञं बोधतं हवस्य मे सत्तो होता निविदः पूर्व्या अनु | अछा राजाना नम एत्याव्र्तं परशास्त्रादा पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ||
2.36.e: Accept the sacrifice; mark both of you, my call: the Priest hath seated him after the ancient texts.  My prayer that bids them come goes forth to both the Kings: drink ye the Soma meath from the Director's bowl.

2.37.d: मन्दस्व होत्रादनु जोषमन्धसो.अध्वर्यवः स पूर्णांवष्ट्यासिचम | तस्मा एतं भरत तद्वशो ददिर्होत्राद सोमं दरविणोदः पिब रतुभिः ||
2.37.e: Enjoy thy fill of meath out of the Hotar's cup: Adhvaryus he desires a full draught poured for him.  Bring it him: seeking this he gives. Granter of Wealth, drink Soma with the Ṛtus from the Hotar's cup.

2.37.d: यमु पूर्वमहुवे तमिदं हुवे सेदु हव्यो ददिर्यो नाम पत्यते | अध्वर्युभिः परस्थितं सोम्यं मधु पोत्रात सोमं द. प. र. ||
2.37.e: He whom of old I called on, him I call on now. He is to be invoked; his name is He who Gives,  Here brought by priests is Soma meath. Granter of Wealth, drink Soma with the Ṛtus from the Potar's cup.

2.37.d: मेद्यन्तु ते वह्नयो येभिरीयसे.अरिषण्यन वीळयस्वा वनस्पते | आयूया धर्ष्णो अभिगूर्या तवं नेष्ट्रात सोमं ... ||
2.37.e: Fat may the horses be wherewith thou speedest on: Lord of the Wood, unharming, strengthen thou thyself.  Drawing and seizing, Bold One, thou who grantest wealth, drink Soma with the Ṛtus from the Neṣṭar's cup.

2.37.d: अपाद धोत्रादुत पोत्रादमत्तोत नेष्ट्रादजुषत परयो हितम | तुरीयं पात्रमम्र्क्तममर्त्यं दरविणोदाः पिबतु दराविणोदसः ||
2.37.e: From Hotar's cup and Potar's he hath drunk and joyed: the proffered food hath pleased him from the Neṣṭar's bowl.  The fourth cup undisturbed, immortal, let him drink who giveth wealth, the cup of the wealth-giving God.

2.37.d: अर्वाञ्चमद्य यय्यं नर्वाहणं रथं युञ्जाथामिह वां विमोचनम | पर्ङकतं हवींषि मधुना हि कं गतमथा सोमं पिबतं वाजिनीवसू ||
2.37.e: Yoke, O ye Twain, to-day your hero-bearing car, swift-moving hitherward: your loosing-place is here.  Mix the oblations, then come hither with the meath, and drink the Soma, ye rich in abundant strength.

2.37.d: जोष्यग्ने समिधं जोष्याहुतिं जोषि बरह्म जन्यं जोषिसुष्टुतिम | विश्वेभिर्विश्वान रतुना वसो मह उशन देवानुशतः पायया हविः ||
2.37.e: Agni, accept the fuel and our offered gift: accept the prayer of man, accept our eulogy,  Do thou with all, with Ṛtu, O thou Excellent, fain, make the great Gods all fain taste the gift we bring.

2.38.d: उदु षय देवः सविता सवाय शश्वत्तमं तदपा वह्निरस्थात | नूनं देवेभ्यो वि हि धाति रत्नमथाभजद वीतिहोत्रं सवस्तौ ||
2.38.e: UPRISEN is Savitar, this God, to quicken, Priest who neglects not this most constant duty.  To the Gods, verily, he gives rich treasure, and blesses him who calls them to the banquet.

2.38.d: विश्वस्य हि शरुष्टये देव ऊर्ध्वः पर बाहवा पर्थुपाणिः सिसर्ति | आपश्चिदस्य वरत आ निम्र्ग्रा अयं चिद वातो रमते परिज्मन ||
2.38.e: Having gone up on high, the God broad-handed spreads his arms widely forth that all may mark him.  Even the waters bend them to his service: even this wind rests in the circling region.

2.38.d: आशुभिश्चिद यान वि मुचाति नूनमरीरमदतमानं चिदेतोः | अह्यर्षूणां चिन नययानविष्यामनु वरतं सवितुर्मोक्यागात ||
2.38.e: Though borne by swift steeds he will yet unyoke them: e’en the fleet chariot hath he stayed from going.  He hath checked e’en their haste who glide like serpents. Night closely followed Savitar's dominion.

2.38.d: पुनः समव्यद विततं वयन्ती मध्या कर्तोर्न्यधाच्छक्म धीरः | उत संहायास्थाद वय रतूं अदर्धररमतिःसविता देव आगात ||
2.38.e: What was spread out she weaves afresh, re-weaving: the skilful leaves his labour half-completed.  He hath arisen from rest, and parted seasons: Savitar hath approached, God, holy-minded.

2.38.d: नानौकांसि दुर्यो विश्वमायुर्वि तिष्ठते परभवः शोको अग्नेः | जयेष्ठं माता सूनवे भागमाधादन्वस्यकेतमिषितं सवित्रा ||
2.38.e: Through various dwellings, through entire existence, spreads, manifest, the household light of Agni.  The Mother gives her Son the goodliest portion, and Savitar hath sped to meet his summons.

2.38.d: समाववर्ति विष्ठितो जिगीषुर्विश्वेषां कामश्चरताममाभूत | शश्वानपो विक्र्तं हित्व्यागादनु वरतं सवितुर्दैव्यस्य ||
2.38.e: He comes again, unfolded, fain for conquest: at home was he, the love of all things moving.  Each man hath come leaving his evil doings, after the Godlike Savitar's commandment.

2.38.d: तवया हितमप्यमप्सु भागं धन्वान्वा मर्गयसो वि तस्थुः | वनानि विभ्यो नकिरस्य तानि वरता देवस्य सवितुर्मिनन्ति ||
2.38.e: The wild beasts spread through desert places seeking their watery share which thou hast set in waters.  The woods are given to the birds. These statutes of the God Savitar none disobeyeth.

2.38.d: याद्राध्यं वरुणो योनिमप्यमनिशितं निमिषि जर्भुराणः | विश्वो मार्ताण्डो वरजमा पशुर्गात सथशो जन्मानि सविता वयाकः ||
2.38.e: With utmost speed, in restless haste at sunset Varuṇa seeks his watery habitation.  Then seeks each bird his nest, each beast his lodging. In due place Savitar hath set each creature.

2.38.d: न यस्येन्द्रो वरुणो न मित्रो वरतमर्यमा न मिनन्ति रुद्रः | नारातयस्तमिदं सवस्ति हुवे देवं सवितारं नमोभिः ||
2.38.e: Him whose high law not Varuṇa nor Indra, not Mitra, Aryaman, nor Rudra breaketh,  Nor evil-hearted fiends, here for my welfare him I invoke, God Savitar, with worship.

2.38.d: भगं धियं वाजयन्तः पुरन्धिं नराशंसो गनास्पतिर्नो अव्याः | आये वामस्य संगथे रयीणां परिया देवस्य सवितुः सयाम ||
2.38.e: May they who strengthen bliss, and thought and wisdom, and the Dames’ Lord and Narāśaṁsa aid us.  That good may come to us and wealth be gathered, may we be Savitar the God's beloved.

2.38.d: अस्मभ्यं तद दिवो अद्भ्यः पर्थिव्यास्त्वया दत्तं काम्यं राध आ गात | शं यत सतोत्र्भ्य आपये भवात्युरुशंसाय सवितर्जरित्रे ||
2.38.e: So come to us our hearts' desire, the bounty bestowed by thee, from heaven and earth and waters,  That it be well with friends and those who praise thee, and, Savitar, with the loud-lauding singer.

2.39.d: गरावाणेव तदिदथं जरेथे गर्ध्रेव वर्क्षं निधिमन्तमछ | बरह्माणेव विदथ उक्थशासा दूतेव हव्या जन्या पुरुत्रा ||
2.39.e: SING like the two press-stones for this same purpose; come like two misers to the tree of treasure;  Like two laud-singing Brahmans in the assembly, like the folk's envoys called in many places.

2.39.d: परातर्यावाणा रथ्येव वीराजेव यमा वरमा सचेथे | मेने इव तन्वा शुम्भमाने दम्पतीव करतुविदा जनेषु ||
2.39.e: Moving at morning like two car-borne heroes, like to a pair of goats ye come electing;  Like two fair dames embellishing their bodies, like a wise married pair among the people.

2.39.d: शर्ङगेव नः परथमा गन्तमर्वाक छफाविव जर्भुराणातरोभिः | चक्रवाकेव परति वस्तोरुस्रार्वाञ्चा यातं रथ्येव शक्रा ||
2.39.e: Like to a pair of horns come first to us-ward, like to a pair of hoofs with rapid motion;  Come like two Cakavās in the grey of morning, come like two chariot wheels at dawn, ye Mighty.

2.39.d: नावेव नः पारयतं युगेव नभ्येव न उपधीव परधीव | शवानेव नो अरिषण्या तनूनां खर्गलेव विस्रसः पातमस्मान ||
2.39.e: Bear us across the rivers like two vessels, save us as ye were yokes, naves, spokes and fellies.  Be like two dogs that injure not our bodies; preserve us, like two crutches, that we fall not.

2.39.d: वातेवाजुर्या नद्येव रीतिरक्षी इव चक्षुषा यातमर्वाक | हस्ताविव तन्वे शम्भविष्ठा पादेव नो नयतं वस्यो अछ ||
2.39.e: Like two winds ageing not, two confluent rivers, come with quick vision like two eyes before us.  Come like two hands most helpful to the body, and guide us like two feet to what is precious.

2.39.d: ओष्ठाविव मध्वास्ने वदन्ता सतनाविव पिप्यतं जीवसेनः | नासेव नस्तन्वो रक्षितारा कर्णाविव सुश्रुता भूतमस्मे ||
2.39.e: Even as two lips that with the mouth speak honey, even as two breasts that nourish our existence,  Like the two nostrils that protect our being, be to us as our ears that hear distinctly.

2.39.d: हस्तेव शक्तिमभि सन्ददी नः कषामेव नः समजतं रजांसि | इमा गिरो अश्विना युष्मयन्तीः कष्णोत्रेणेव सवधितिं सं शिशीतम ||
2.39.e: Like two hands give ye us increasing vigour; like heaven and earth constrain the airy regions.  Aśvins, these hymns that struggle to approach you, sharpen ye like an axe upon a whetstone.

2.39.d: एतानि वामश्विना वर्धनानि बरह्म सतोमं गर्त्समदासो अक्रन | तानि नरा जुजुषाणोप यातं बर्हद ... ||
2.39.e: These prayers of ours exalting you, O Aśvins, have the Gṛtsamadas, for a laud, made ready.  Welcome them, O ye Heroes, and come hither. Loud may we speak. with brave men, in assembly.

2.40.d: सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणां जनना दिवो जनना पर्थिव्याः | जातौ विश्वस्य भुवनस्य गोपौ देवा अक्र्ण्वन्नम्र्तस्य नाभिम ||
2.40.e: SOMA and Pūṣan, Parents of all riches, Parents of earth and Parents of high heaven,  You Twain, brought forth as the whole world's protectors, the Gods have made centre of life eternal.

2.40.d: इमौ देवौ जायमानौ जुषन्तेमौ तमांसि गूहतामजुष्टा | आभ्यामिन्द्रः पक्वमामास्वन्तः सोमापूषभ्यां जनदुस्रियासु ||
2.40.e: At birth of these two Gods all Gods are joyful: they have caused darkness, which we hate, to vanish.  With these, with Soma and with Pūṣan, India generates ripe warm milk in the raw milch-cows.

2.40.d: सोमापूषणा रजसो विमानं सप्तचक्रं रथमविश्वमिन्वम | विषूव्र्तं मनसा युज्यमानं तं जिन्वथो वर्षणा पञ्चरश्मिम ||
2.40.e: Soma and Pūṣan, urge your chariot hither, the seven-wheeled car that measures out the region,  That stirs not all, that moves to every quarter, five-reined and harnessed by the thought, ye Mighty.

2.40.d: दिव्यन्यः सदनं चक्र उच्चा पर्थिव्यामन्यो अध्यन्तरिक्षे | तावस्मभ्यं पुरुवारं पुरुक्षुं रायस पोषं वि षयतां नाभिमस्मे ||
2.40.e: One in the heaven on high hath made his dwelling, on earth and in the firmament the other.  May they disclose to us great store of treasure, much-longed for, rich in food, source of enjoyment.

2.40.d: विश्वान्यन्यो भुवना जजान विश्वमन्यो अभिचक्षाण एति | सोमापूषणाववतं धियं मे युवाभ्यां विश्वाः पर्तना जयेम ||
2.40.e: One of you Twain is Parent of all creatures, the other journeys onward all-beholding.  Soma and Pūṣan, aid my thought with favour: with you may we o’ercome in all encounters.

2.40.d: धियं पूषा जिन्वतु विश्वमिन्वो रयिं सोमो रयिपतिर्दधातु | अवतु देव्यदितिरनर्वा बर... ||
2.40.e: May Pūṣan stir our thought, the all-impelling, may Soma Lord of riches grant us riches.  May Aditi the perfect Goddess aid us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.41.d: वायो ये ते सहस्रिणो रथासस्तेभिरा गहि | नियुत्वान सोमपीतये ||
2.41.e: O VĀYU, come to us with all the thousand chariots that are thine,  Team-borne, to drink the Soma juice.

2.41.d: नियुत्वान वायवा गह्ययं शुक्रो अयामि ते | गन्तासि सुन्वतो गर्हम ||
2.41.e: Drawn by thy team, O Vāyu, come; to thee is offered this, the pure.  Thou visitest the presser's house.

2.41.d: शुक्रस्याद्य गवाशिर इन्द्रवायू नियुत्वतः | आ यातं पिबतं नरा ||
2.41.e: Indra and Vāyu, drawn by teams, ye Heroes, come today and drink.  Of the bright juice when blent with milk.

2.41.d: अयं वां मित्रावरुणा सुतः सोम रताव्र्धा | ममेदिह शरुतं हवम ||
2.41.e: This Soma hath been shed for you, Law-strengtheners, Mitra-Varuṇa!  Listen ye here to this my call.

2.41.d: राजानावनभिद्रुहा धरुवे सदस्युत्तमे | सहस्रस्थूण आसाते ||
2.41.e: Both Kings who never injure aught seat them in their supremest home,  The thousand-pillared, firmly-based.

2.41.d: ता सम्राजा घर्तासुती आदित्या दानुनस पती | सचेते अनवह्वरम ||
2.41.e: Fed with oblation, Sovran Kings, Ādityas, Lords of liberal gifts.  They wait on him whose life is true.

2.41.d: गोमदू षु नासत्याश्वावद यातमश्विना | वर्ती रुद्रा नर्पाय्यम ||
2.41.e: With kine, Nāsatyas, and with steeds, come, Aśvins, Rudras, to the house  That will protect its heroes well;

2.41.d: न यत परो नान्तर आदधर्षद वर्षण्वसू | दुःशंसो मर्त्यो रिपुः ||
2.41.e: Such, wealthy Gods! as none afar nor standing nigh to us may harm,  Yea, no malicious mortal foe.

2.41.d: ता न आ वोळ्हमश्विना रयिं पिशङगसन्द्र्शम | धिष्न्यावरिवोविदम ||
2.41.e: As such, O longed-far Aśvins, lead us on to wealth of varied sort,  Wealth that shall bring us room and rest.

2.41.d: इन्द्रो अङग महद भयमभी षदप चुच्यवत | स हि सथिरो विचर्षणिः ||
2.41.e: Verily Indra, conquering all, driveth e’en mighty fear away,  For firm is he and swift to act.

2.41.d: इन्द्रश्च मर्ळयाति नो न नः पश्चादघं नशत | भद्रं भवाति नः पुरः ||
2.41.e: Indra be gracious unto us: sin shall not reach us afterward,  And good shall be before us still.

2.41.d: इन्द्र आशाभ्यस परि सर्वाभ्यो अभयं करत | जेता शत्रून विचर्शणिः ||
2.41.e: From all the regions of the world let Indra send security,  The foe-subduer, swift to act.

2.41.d: विश्वे देवास आ गत शर्णुता म इमं हवम | एदं बर्हिर्नि षीदत ||
2.41.e: O all ye Gods, come hitherward: hear this mine invocation, seat  Yourselves upon this sacred grass.

2.41.d: तीव्रो वो मधुमानयं शुनहोत्रेषु मत्सरः | एतं पिबतकाम्यम ||
2.41.e: Among the Śunahotras strong for you is this sweet gladdening draught.  Drink ye of this delightsome juice.

2.41.d: इन्द्रज्येष्ठा ... ||
2.41.e: Ye  Maruts  led by Indra, Gods with Pūṣan for your bounteousest,  Hear all of you this call of mine.

2.41.d: अम्बितमे नदीतमे देवितमे सरस्वति | अप्रशस्ता इव समसि परशस्तिमम्ब नस कर्धि ||
2.41.e: Best Mother, best of Rivers, best of Goddesses, Sarasvatī, We are, as ’twere, of no repute and dear Mother, give thou us renown.

2.41.d: तवे विश्वा सरस्वति शरितायूंषि देव्याम | शुनहोत्रेषु मत्स्व परजां देवि दिदिड्ढि नः ||
2.41.e: In thee, Sarasvatī, divine, all generations have their stay.  Be, glad with Śunahotra's sons: O Goddess grant us progeny.

2.41.d: इमा बरह्म सरस्वति जुषस्व वाजिनीवति | या ते मन्म गर्त्समदा रतावरि परिया देवेषु जुह्वति ||
2.41.e: Enriched with sacrifice, accept Sarasvatī, these prayers of ours,  Thoughts which Gṛtsamadas beloved of Gods bring, Holy One, to thee.

2.41.d: परेतां यज्ञस्य शम्भुवा युवामिदा वर्णीमहे | अग्निंच हव्यवाहनम ||
2.41.e: Ye who bless sacrifice, go forth, for verily we choose you both,  And Agni who conveys our gifts.

2.41.d: दयावा नः पर्थिवी इमं सिध्रमद्य दिविस्प्र्शम | यज्णन्देवेषु यछताम ||
2.41.e: This our effectual sacrifice, reaching the sky, shall Heaven and Earth  Present unto the Gods to-day.

2.41.d: आ वामुपस्थमद्रुहा देवाः सीदन्तु यज्ञियाः | इहाद्यसोमपीतये ||
2.41.e: In both your laps, ye guileless Ones, the Holy Gods shall sit them down  To-day to drink the Soma here.

2.42.d: कनिक्रदज्जनुषं परब्रुवाण इयर्ति वाचमरितेव नावम | सुमङगलश्च शकुने भवासि मा तवा का चिदभिभा विश्व्या विदत ||
2.42.e: TELLING his race aloud with cries repeated, he sends his voice out as his boat a steersman.  O Bird, be ominous of happy fortune from no side may calamity befall thee.

2.42.d: मा तवा शयेन उद वधीन मा सुपर्णो मा तवा विददिषुमान्वीरो अस्ता | पित्र्यामनु परदिशं कनिक्रदत सुमङगलो भद्रवादी वदेह ||
2.42.e: Let not the falcon kill thee, nor the eagle let not the arrow-bearing archer reach thee.  Still crying in the region of the Fathers, speak here auspicious, bearing joyful tidings.

2.42.d: अव करन्द दक्षिणतो गर्हाणां सुमङगलो भद्रवादी शकुन्ते | मा न सतेन ईशत माघशंसो बर्हद ... ||
2.42.e: Bringing good tidings, Bird of happy omen, call thou out loudly southward of our dwellings,  So that no thief, no sinner may oppress us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

2.43.d: परदक्षिनिदभि गर्णन्ति कारवो वयो वदन्त रतुथा शकुन्तयः | उभे वाचौ वदति सामगा इव गायत्रं च तरैष्टुभं चानु राजति ||
2.43.e: HERE on the right sing forth chanters of hymns of praise, even the winged birds that in due season speak.  He, like: a Sāma-chanter utters both the notes, skilled in the mode of Tṛṣṭup and of Gāyatrī.

2.43.d: उद्गातेव शकुने साम गायसि बरह्मपुत्र इव सवनेषु शंससि | वर्षेव वाजी शिशुमतीरपीत्या सर्वतो नः शकुने भद्रमा वद विश्वतो नः शकुने पुण्यमा वद ||
2.43.e: Thou like the chanter-priest chantest the Sāma, Bird; thou singest at libations like a Brahman's son.  Even as a vigorous horse when he comes near the mare, announce to us good fortune, Bird, on every side, proclaim in all directions happy luck, O Bird.

2.43.d: आवदंस्त्वं शकुने भद्रमा वद तूष्णीमासीनः सुमतिं चिकिद्धि नः | यदुत्पतन वदसि कर्करिर्यथा बर्हद . .. ||
2.43.e: When singing here, O Bird. announce good luck to us, and when thou sittest still think on us with kind thoughts.

3.1.d: सोमस्य मा तवसं वक्ष्यग्ने वह्निं चकर्थ विदथे यजध्यै | देवानछा दीद्यद युञ्जे अद्रिं शमाये अग्ने तन्वंजुषस्व ||
3.1.e: THOU, Agni, who wilt have the strong, hast made me the Soma's priest, to worship in assembly.  Thou shinest to the Gods, I set the press-stones. I toil; be joyful in thyself, O Agni.

3.1.d: पराञ्चं यज्ञं चक्र्म वर्धतां गीः समिद्भिरग्निं नमसा दुवस्यन | दिवः शशासुर्विदथा कवीनां गर्त्साय चित तवसे गातुमीषुः ||
3.1.e: East have we turned the rite; may the hymn aid it. With wood and worship shall they honour Agni.  From heaven the synods of the wise have learnt it: e’en for the quick and strong they seek advancement.

3.1.d: मयो दधे मेधिरः पूतदक्षो दिवः सुबन्धुर्जनुषा पर्थिव्याः | अविन्दन्नु दर्शतमप्स्वन्तर्देवासो अग्निमपसि सवसॄणाम ||
3.1.e: The Prudent, he whose will is pure, brought welfare, allied by birth to Heaven and Earth in kinship.  The Gods discovered in the midst of waters beautiful Agni with the Sisters' labour.

3.1.d: अवर्धयन सुभगं सप्त यह्वीः शवेतं जज्ञानमरुषम्महित्वा | शिशुं न जातमभ्यारुरश्वा देवासो अग्निंजनिमन वपुष्यन ||
3.1.e: Him, Blessed One, the Seven strong Floods augmented, him white at birth and red when waxen mighty.  As mother mares run to their new-born you ling, so at his birth the Gods wondered at Agni.

3.1.d: शुक्रेभिरङगै रज आततन्वान करतुं पुनानः कविभिः पवित्रैः | शोचिर्वसानः पर्यायुरपां शरियो मिमीते बर्हतीरनूनाः ||
3.1.e: Spreading with radiant limbs throughout the region, purging his power with wise purifications,  Robing himself in light, the life of waters, he spreads abroad his high and perfect glories.

3.1.d: वव्राजा सीमनदतीरदब्धा दिवो यह्वीरवसाना अनग्नाः | सना अत्र युवतयः सयोनीरेकं गर्भं दधिरे सप्त वाणीः ||
3.1.e: He sought heaven's Mighty Ones, the unconsuming, the unimpaired, not clothed and yet not naked.  Then they, ancient and young, who dwell together, Seven sounding Rivers, as one germ received him.

3.1.d: सतीर्णा अस्य संहतो विश्वरूपा घर्तस्य योनौ सरवथे मधूनाम | अस्थुरत्र धेनवः पिन्वमाना मही दस्मस्य मातरा समीची ||
3.1.e: His piles, assuming every form, are scattered where flow sweet waters, at the spring of fatness;  There stood the milch-kine with full-laden udders, and both paired Mighty Mothers of the Wondrous.

3.1.d: बभ्राणः सूनो सहसो वयद्यौद दाधानः शुक्रा रभसा वपूंषि | शचोतन्ति धारा मधुनो घर्तस्य वर्षा यत्र वाव्र्धे काव्येन ||
3.1.e: Carefully cherished, Son of Strength, thou shoncst assuming lasting and refulgent beauties.  Full streams of fatness and sweet juice descended, there where the Mighty One grew strong by wisdom.

3.1.d: पितुश्चिदूधर्जनुषा विवेद वयस्य धारा अस्र्जद वि धेनाः | गुहा चरन्तं सखिभिः शिवेभिर्दिवो यह्वीभिर्नगुहा बभूव ||
3.1.e: From birth he knew even his Father's bosom, he set his voices and his streams in motion;  Knew him who moved with blessed Friends in secret, with the young Dames of heaven. He stayed not hidden.

3.1.d: पितुश्च गर्भं जनितुश्च बभ्रे पूर्वीरेको अधयत पीप्यानाः | वर्ष्णे सपत्नी शुचये सबन्धू उभे अस्मै मनुष्येनि पाहि ||
3.1.e: He nursed the Infant of the Sire and Maker: alone the Babe sucked many a teeming bosom.  Guard, for the Bright and Strong, the fellow-spouses friendly to men and bound to him in kinship.

3.1.d: उरौ महाननिबाधे ववर्धापो अग्निं यशसः सं हि पूर्वीः | रतस्य योनावशयद दमूना जामीनामग्निरपसिस्वसॄणाम ||
3.1.e: The Mighty One increased in space unbounded; full many a glorious flood gave strength to Agni.  Friend of the house, within the lap of Order lay Agni, in the Sister Rivers' service.

3.1.d: अक्रो न बभ्रिः समिथे महीनां दिद्र्क्षेयः सूनवे भार्जीकः | उदुस्रिया जनिता यो जजानापां गर्भो नर्तमो यह्वो अग्निः ||
3.1.e: As keen supporter where great waters gather, light-shedder whom the brood rejoice to look on;  He who begat, and will beget, the dawnlights, most manly, Child of Floods, is youthful Agni.

3.1.d: अपां गर्भं दर्शतमोषधीनां वना जजान सुभगा विरूपम | देवासश्चिन मनसा सं हि जग्मुः पनिष्ठं जातं तवसं दुवस्यन ||
3.1.e: Him, varied in his form, the lovely Infant of floods and plants the blessed wood hath gendered.  Gods even, moved in spirit, came around him, and served him at his birth, the Strong, the Wondrous.

3.1.d: बर्हन्त इद भानवो भार्जीकमग्निं सचन्त विद्युतो न शुक्राः | गुहेव वर्द्धं सदसि सवे अन्तरपार ऊर्वे अम्र्तन्दुहानाः ||
3.1.e: Like brilliant lightnings, mighty luminaries accompany the light-diffusing Agni,  Waxen, as ’twere in secret, in his dwelling, while in the boundless stall they milk out Amṛta.

3.1.d: ईळे च तवा यजमानो हविर्भिरीळे सखित्वं सुमतिं निकामः | देवैरवो मिमीहि सं जरित्रे रक्षा च नो दम्येभिरनीकैः ||
3.1.e: I sacrificing serve thee with oblations and crave with longing thy good-will and friendship.  Grant, with the Gods, thy grace to him who lauds thee, protect us with thy rays that guard the homestead.

3.1.d: उपक्षेतारस्तव सुप्रणीते.अग्ने विश्वानि धन्या दधानाः | सुरेतसा शरवसा तुञ्जमाना अभि षयाम पर्तनायून्रदेवान ||
3.1.e: May we, O Agni, thou who leadest wisely, thy followers and masters of all treasures,  Strong in the glory of our noble offspring, subdue the godless when they seek the battle.

3.1.d: आ देवानामभवः केतुरग्ने मन्द्रो विश्वानि काव्यानि विद्वान | परति मर्तानवासयो दमूना अनु देवान रथिरो यासिसाधन ||
3.1.e: Ensign of Gods hast thou become, O Agni, joy-giver, knower of all secret wisdom.  Friend of the homestead, thou hast lightened mortals: carborne thou goest to the Gods, fulfilling.

3.1.d: नि दुरोणे अम्र्तो मर्त्यानां राजा ससाद विदथानि साधन | घर्तप्रतीक उर्विया वयद्यौदग्निर्विश्वानि काव्यानि विद्वान ||
3.1.e: Within the house hath sate the King immortal of mortals, filling full their sacred synods.  Bedewed with holy oil he shineth widely, Agni, the knower of all secret wisdom.

3.1.d: आ नो गहि सख्येभिः शिवेभिर्महान महीभिरूतिभिः सरण्यन | अस्मे रयिं बहुलं सन्तरुत्रं सुवाचं भागं यशसं कर्धी नः ||
3.1.e: Come unto us with thine auspicious friendship, come speeding, Mighty, with thy mighty succours.  Grant us abundant wealth that saves from danger, that brings a good repute, a glorious portion.

3.1.d: एता ते अग्ने जनिमा सनानि पर पूर्व्याय नूतनानि वोचम | महान्ति वर्ष्णे सवना कर्तेमा जन्मञ-जन्मन निहितो जातवेदाः ||
3.1.e: To thee who art of old these songs, O Agni, have I declared, the ancient and the later.  These great libations to the Strong are offiered: in every birth is Jātavedas stablished.

3.1.d: जन्मञ-जन्मन निहितो जातवेदा विश्वामित्रेभिरिध्यते अजस्रः | तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे सयाम ||
3.1.e: Stablished in every birth is Jātavedas, kindled perpetual by the Viśvāmitras.  May we rest ever in the loving-kindness, in the auspicious grace of him the Holy.

3.1.d: इमं यज्ञं सहसावन तवं नो देवत्रा धेहि सुक्रतो रराणः | पर यंसि होतर्ब्र्हतीरिषो नो.अग्ने महि दरविनमा यजस्व ||
3.1.e: This sacrifice of ours do thou, O Mighty, O truly Wise, bear to the Gods rejoicing.  Grant us abundant food, thou priestly Herald, vouchsafe to give us ample wealth, O Agni.

3.1.d: इळामग्ने पुरुदंसं सनिं गोः शश्वत्तमं हवमानायसाध | सयान नः सूनुस्तनयो विजावाग्ने सा ते सुमतिर्भुत्वस्मे ||
3.1.e: As holy food, Agni, to thine'invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us he born a son, and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward.

3.2.d: वैश्वानराय धिषणां रताव्र्धे घर्तं न पूतमग्नयेजनामसि | दविता होतारं मनुषश्च वाघतो धिया रथंन कुलिशः सं रण्वति ||
3.2.e: To him, Vaiśvānara, who strengthens Holy Law, to Agni we present our praise like oil made pure.  With thoughtful insight human priests bring him anear, our Herald from of old, as an axe forms a car.

3.2.d: स रोचयज्जनुषा रोदसी उभे स मात्रोरभवत पुत्र ईड्यः | हव्यवाळ अग्निरजरश्चनोहितो दूळभो विशामतिथिर्विभावसुः ||
3.2.e: He made the heaven and earth resplendent by his birth: Child of two Mothers he was meet to be implored,  Agni, oblation-bearer, gracious, ever-young, infallible, rich in radiant light, the guest of men.

3.2.d: करत्वा दक्षस्य तरुषो विधर्मणि देवासो अग्निं जनयन्त चित्तिभिः | रुरुचानं भानुना जयोतिषा महामत्यं न वाजं सनिष्यन्नुप बरुवे ||
3.2.e: Within the range of their surpassinq power, by might, the Gods created Agni with inventive thought.  I, eager to win strength, address him, like a steed, resplendent with his brilliance, with his ample light.

3.2.d: आ मन्द्रस्य सनिष्यन्तो वरेण्यं वर्णीमहे अह्रयं वाजम्र्ग्मियम | रातिं भर्गूणामुशिजं कविक्रतुमग्निं राजन्तं दिव्येन शोचिषा ||
3.2.e: Eager to gain, we crave from him the friendly God strength confident, choiceworthy meet to be extolled:  The Bhṛgus' bounty, willing, strong with sages' lore, even Agni shining forth with light that comes from heaven.

3.2.d: अग्निं सुम्नाय दधिरे पुरो जना वाजश्रवसमिह वर्क्तबर्हिषः | यतस्रुचः सुरुचं विश्वदेव्यं रुद्रं यज्ञानांसाधदिष्टिमपसाम ||
3.2.e: For happiness, men, having trimmed the sacred grass, set Agni glorious for his strength before them here;  Yea, with raised ladles, him bright, dear to all the Gods, perfecting aims of works, Rudra of solemn rites.

3.2.d: पावकशोचे तव हि कषयं परि होतर्यज्ञेषु वर्क्तबर्हिषो नरः | अग्ने दुव इछमानास आप्यमुपासते दरविणं धेहि तेभ्यः ||
3.2.e: Around thy dwelling-place, O brightly-shining Priest, are men at sacrifice, whose sacred grass is trimmed.  Wishing to do thee service, Agni, they are there, desirous of thy friendship grant them store of wealth.

3.2.d: आ रोदसी अप्र्णदा सवर्महज्जातं यदेनमपसो अधारयन | सो अध्वराय परि णीयते कविरत्यो न वाजसातयेचनोहितः ||
3.2.e: He hath filled heaven and earth and the great realm of light, when at his birth the skilful held him in their hold.  He like a horse is led forth to the sacrifice Sage, graciously inclined, that he may win us strength.

3.2.d: नमस्यत हव्यदातिं सवध्वरं दुवस्यत दम्यं जातवेदसम | रथीर्र्तस्य बर्हतो विचर्षणिरग्निर्देवानामभवत पुरोहितः ||
3.2.e: Honour the oblation-bearer, him who knows fair rites, serve ye the Household Friend who knows all things that be.  He drives the chariot of the lofty ordinance: Agni most active, is the great High Priest of Gods.

3.2.d: तिस्रो यह्वस्य समिधः परिज्मनो.अग्नेरपुनन्नुशिजो अम्र्त्यवः | तासामेकामदधुर्मर्त्ये भुजमु लोकमु दवे उप जामिमीयतुः ||
3.2.e: They who are free from death, fain for him, purified three splendours of the mighty Agni, circling all.  To man, for his enjoyment, one of these they gave: the other two have passed into the sister sphere.

3.2.d: विशां कविं विश्पतिं मानुषीरिषः सं सीमक्र्ण्वन सवधितिं न तेजसे | स उद्वतो निवतो याति वेविषत स गर्भमेषु भुवनेषु दीधरत ||
3.2.e: Man's sacrificial food hath sharpened like an axe, for brightness, him the Sage of men, the people's Lord,  Busied with sacred rites he mounts and he descends. He hath laid down his vital germ within these worlds.

3.2.d: स जिन्वते जठरेषु परजज्ञिवान वर्षा चित्रेषु नानदन न सिंहः | वैश्वानरः पर्थुपाजा अमर्त्यो वसु रत्ना दयमानो वि दाशुषे ||
3.2.e: He stirs with life in wombs dissimilar in kind, born as a Lion or a loudly-bellowing Bull:  Vaiśvānara immortal with wide-reaching might, bestowing goods and wealth on him who offiers gifts.

3.2.d: वैश्वानरः परत्नथा नाकमारुहद दिवस पर्ष्ठं भन्दमानः सुमन्मभिः | स पूर्ववज्जनयञ जन्तवे धनं समानमज्मं पर्येति जाग्र्विः ||
3.2.e: Vaiśvānara, as of old, mounted the cope of heaven, heaven's ridge, well greeted, by those skilled in noble songs.  He, as of old, producing riches for the folk, still watchful, traversesthe common way again.

3.2.d: रतावानं यज्ञियं विप्रमुक्थ्यमा यं दधे मातरिश्वा दिवि कषयम | तं चित्रयामं हरिकेशमीमहे सुदीतिमग्निं सुविताय नव्यसे ||
3.2.e: For new prosperity we seek to Agni, him whose course is splendid, gold-haired, excellently bright,  Whom Mātariśvan stablished, dweller in the heaven, meet for high praise and holy, sage and true to Law.

3.2.d: शुचिं न यामन्निषिरं सवर्द्र्शं केतुं दिवो रोचनस्थामुषर्बुधम | अग्निं मूर्धानं दिवो अप्रतिष्कुतं तमीमहे नमसा वाजिनं बर्हत ||
3.2.e: As pure and swift of course, beholder of the light, who stands in heaven's bright sphere a sign, who wakes at dawn,  Agni, the head of heaven, whom none may turn aside-to him the Powerful with mighty prayer we seek.

3.2.d: मन्द्रं होतारं शुचिमद्वयाविनं दमूनसमुक्थ्यं विश्वचर्षणिम | रथं न चित्रं वपुषाय दर्शतं मनुर्हितं सदमिद राय ईमहे ||
3.2.e: The cheerful Priest, the pure, in whom no guile is found, Friend of the House, praise-worthy, dear to all mankind,  Fair to behold for beauty like a splendid car,—Agni the Friend of men we ever seek for wealth.

3.3.d: वैश्वानराय पर्थुपाजसे विपो रत्ना विधन्त धरुणेषु गातवे | अग्निर्हि देवानम्र्तो दुवस्यत्यथा धर्माणि सनता न दूदुषत ||
3.3.e: To him who shines afar, Vaiśvānara, shall bards give precious things that he may go on certain paths:  For Agni the Immortal serves the Deities, and therefore never breaks their everlasting laws.

3.3.d: अन्तर्दूतो रोदसी दस्म ईयते होता निषत्तो मनुषः पुरोहितः | कषयं बर्हन्तं परि भूषति दयुभिर्देवेभिरग्निरिषितो धियावसुः ||
3.3.e: He, wondrous envoy, goes between the earth and heaven, firm seated as the Herald, great High Priest of men.  He compassethwith rays the lofty dwelling-place, Agni, sent forward by the Gods, enriched with piayer.

3.3.d: केतुं यज्ञानां विदथस्य सा धनं विप्रासो अग्निं महयन्त चित्तिभिः | अपांसि यस्मिन्नधि सन्दधुर्गिरस्तस्मिन सुम्नानि यजमान आ चके ||
3.3.e: Sages shall glorify Agni with earnest thoughts, ensign of sacrifice, who fills the synod full:  In whom the singers have stored up their holy acts to him the worshipper looks for joy and happiness.

3.3.d: पिता यज्ञानामसुरो विपश्चितां विमानमग्निर्वयुनं च वाघताम | आ विवेश रोदसी भूरिवर्पसा पुरुप्रियो भन्दते धामभिः कविः ||
3.3.e: The Sire of sacrifice, great God of holy bards, Agni, the measure and the symbol of the priests,  Hath entered heaven and earth that show in varied form: the Sage whom many love rejoiceth in his might.

3.3.d: चन्द्रमग्निं चन्द्ररथं हरिव्रतं वैश्वानरमप्सुषदं सवर्विदम | विगाहं तूर्णिं तविषीभिराव्र्तं भूर्णिं देवास इह सुश्रियं दधुः ||
3.3.e: Bright Agni with the bright car, Lord of green domains, Vaiśvānara dweller in the floods, who finds the light,  Pervading, swift and wild, encompassed round with powers, him very glorious have the Gods established here.

3.3.d: अग्निर्देवेभिर्मनुषश्च जन्तुभिस्तन्वानो यज्ञं पुरुपेशसं धिया | रथीरन्तरीयते साधदिष्टिभिर्जीरो दमूना अभिशस्तिचातनः ||
3.3.e: Agni, together with the Gods and Manu's folk by thought extending sacrifice in varied form,  Goes, car-borne, to and fro with those who crown each rite, the fleet, the Household Friend, who turns the curse aside.

3.3.d: अग्ने जरस्व सवपत्य आयुन्यूर्जा पिन्वस्व समिषो दिदीहि नः | वयांसि जिन्व बर्हतश्च जाग्र्व उशिग देवानामसि सुक्रतुर्विपाम ||
3.3.e: Sing, Agni, for long life to us and noble sons: teem thou with plenty, shine upon us store of food.  Increase the great man's strength, thou ever-vigilant: thou, longing for the Gods, knowest their hymns full well.

3.3.d: विश्पतिं यह्वमतिथिं नरः सदा यन्तारं धीनामुशिजं च वाघताम | अध्वराणां चेतनं जातवेदसं पर शंसन्ति नमसा जूतिभिर्व्र्धे ||
3.3.e: The Mighty One, Lord of the people and their guest, the leader of their thoughts, devoted Friend of priests,  Our solemn rites' announcer, Jātavedas, men with worship ever praise, with urgings for their weal.

3.3.d: विभावा देवः सुरणः परि कषितीरग्निर्बभूव शवसासुमद्रथः | तस्य वरतानि भूरिपोषिणो वयमुप भूषेमदम आ सुव्र्क्तिभिः ||
3.3.e: Agni the God resplendent, giver of great joy, hath on his lovely car compassed the lands with, might.  Let us with pure laudations in his house approach the high laws of the nourisher of multitudes.

3.3.d: वैश्वानर तव धामान्या चके येभिः सवर्विदभवो विचक्षण | जात आप्र्णो भुवनानि रोदसी अग्ने ता विस्वा परिभूरसि तमना ||
3.3.e: I celebrate thy glories, O Vaiśvānara, wherewith thou, O farsighted God, has found the light.  Thou filledst at thy birth both worlds, the earth and heaven: all this, O Agni, hast thou compassed of thyself.

3.3.d: वैश्वानरस्य दंसनाभ्यो बर्हदरिणादेकः सवपस्यया कविः | उभा पितरा महयन्नजायताग्निर्द्यावाप्र्थिवी भूरिरेतसा ||
3.3.e: By his great skill the Sage alone hath brought to pass a great deed, mightier than Vaiśvānara's wondrous acts.  Agni sprang into being, magnifying both his Parents, Heaven and Earth, rich in prolific seed.

3.4.d: समित-समित सुमना बोध्यस्मे शुचा-शुचा सुमतिं रासि वस्वः | आ देव देवान यजथाय वक्षि सखा सखीन सुमना यक्ष्यग्ने ||
3.4.e: BE friendly with each kindled log of fuel, with every flash bestow the boon of riches.  Bring thou the Gods, O God, unto our worship: serve, well-inclined, as Friend thy friends, O Agni.

3.4.d: यं देवासस्त्रिरहन्नायजन्ते दिवे-दिवे वरुणो मित्रो अग्निः | सेमं यज्ञं मधुमन्तं कर्धी नस्तनूनपाद घर्तयोनिं विधन्तम ||
3.4.e: Agni whom daily Varuṇa and Mitra the Gods bring thrice a day to this our worship,  Tanūnapāt, enrich with meath our service that dwells with holy oil, that offers honour.

3.4.d: पर दीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः परथमं यजध्यै | अछा नमोभिर्व्र्षभं वन्दध्यै स देवान यक्षदिषितो यजीयान ||
3.4.e: The thought that bringeth every boon proceedeth to worship first the Priest of the libation,  That we may greet the Strong One with our homage. Urged, may he bring the Gods, best Sacrificer.

3.4.d: ऊर्ध्वो वां गातुरध्वरे अकार्यूर्ध्वा शोचींषि परस्थिता रजांसि | दिवो वा नाभा नयसादि होता सत्र्णीमहि देवव्यचा वि बर्हिः ||
3.4.e: On high your way to sacrifice was made ready; the radiant flames went upward to the regions.  Full in the midst of heaven the Priest is seated: sirew we the sacred grass where Gods may rest them.

3.4.d: सप्त होत्राणि मनसा वर्णाना इन्वन्तो विश्वं परति यन्न्र्तेन | नर्पेशसो विदथेषु पर जाता अभीमं यज्ञं वि चरन्त पूर्वीः ||
3.4.e: Claiming in mind the seven priests' burntoblations, inciting all, they came in settled order.  To this our sacrifice approach the many who show in hero beauty at assemblies.

3.4.d: आ भन्दमाने उषसा उपाके उत समयेते तन्वा विरूपे | यथा नो मित्रो वरुणो जुजोषदिन्द्रो मरुत्वानुत वा महोभिः ||
3.4.e: Night and Dawn, lauded, hither come together, both smiling, different are their forms in colour,  That Varuṇa and Mitra may accept us, and Indra, girt by Maruts, with his glories.

3.4.d: दैव्या होतारा परथमा नय रञ्जे सप्त पर्क्षासः सवधयामदन्ति | रतं शंसन्त रतमित त आहुरनु वरतं वरतपा दीध्यानाः ||
3.4.e: I crave the grace of heaven's two chief Invokers: the seven swift steeds joy in their wonted manner.  These speak of truth, praising the truth eternal, thinking on Order as the guards of Order.

3.4.d: आ भारती भारतीभिः सजोषा इळा देवैर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः | सरस्वती सारस्वतेभिरर्वाक तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं सदन्तु ||
3.4.e: May Bhāratī with all her Sisters, Iḷā accordant with the Gods, with mortalls Agni,  Sarasvatī with all her kindred Rivers, come to this grass, Three Goddesses, and seat them.

3.4.d: तन नस्तुरीपमध पोषयित्नु देव तवष्टर्वि रराणः सयस्व | यतो वीरः कर्मण्यः सुदक्षो युक्तग्रावा जायते देवकामः ||
3.4.e: Well pleased with us do thou O God, O Tvaṣṭar, give ready issue to our procreant vigour,  Whence springs the hero, powerful, skilled in action, lover of Gods, adjuster of the press-stones.

3.4.d: वनस्पते.अव सर्जोप देवानग्निर्हविः शमिता सूदयाति | सेदु होता सत्यतरो यजाति यथा देवानां जनिमानि वेद ||
3.4.e: Send to the Gods the oblation, Lord of Forests; and let the Immolator, Agni, dress it.  He as the truer Priest shall offer worship, for the Gods’ generations well he knoweth.

3.4.d: आ याह्यग्ने समिधानो अर्वां इन्द्रेण देवैः सरथं तुरेभिः | बर्हिर्न आस्तामदितिः सुपुत्रा सवाहा देवा अम्र्तामादयन्ताम ||
3.4.e: Come thou to us, O Agni, duly kindled, together with the potent Gods and Indra.  On this our grass sit Aditi, happy Mother, and let our Hail delight the Gods Immortal.

3.5.d: परत्यग्निरुषसश्चेकितानो.अबोधि विप्रः पदवीः कवीनाम | पर्थुपाजा देवयद्भिः समिद्धो.अप दवारा तमसो वह्निरावः ||
3.5.e: AGNI who shines against the Dawns is wakened. The holy Singer who precedes the sages.  With far-spread lustre, kindled by the pious, the Priest hath thrown both gates of darkness open.

3.5.d: परेद वग्निर्वाव्र्धे सतोमेभिर्गीर्भि सतोतॄणां नमस्य उक्थैः | पूर्वीर्र्तस्य सन्द्र्शश्चकानः सं दूतो अद्यौदुषसो विरोके ||
3.5.e: Agni hath waxen mighty by laudations, to be adored with hymns of those who praise him.  Loving the varied shows of holy Order at the first flush of dawn he shines as envoy.

3.5.d: अधाय्यग्निर्मानुषीषु विक्ष्वपां गर्भो मित्र रतेन साधन | आ हर्यतो यजतः सान्वस्थादभूदु विप्रो हव्योमतीनाम ||
3.5.e: Amid men's homes hath Agni been established, fulfilling with the Law, Friend, germ of waters.  Loved and adored, the height he hath ascended, the Singer, object of our invocations.

3.5.d: मित्रो अग्निर्भवति यत समिद्धो मित्रो होता वरुणो जातवेदाः | मित्रो अध्वर्युरिषिरो दमूना मित्रः सिन्धूनामुत पर्वतानाम ||
3.5.e: Agni is Mitra when enkindled duly, Mitra as Priest, Varuṇa, Jātavedas;  Mitra as active minister, and House-Friend, Mitra of flowing rivers and of mountains.

3.5.d: पाति परियं रिपो अग्रं पदं वेः पाति यज्वश्चरञंसूर्यस्य | पाति नाभा सप्तशीर्षाणमग्निः पाति देवानामुपमादं रष्वः ||
3.5.e: The Earth's, the Bird's dear lofty place he guardeth, he guardeth in his might the course of Sūrya,  Guardeth the Seven-headed in the centre, guardeth sublime the Deities enjoyment.

3.5.d: रभुश्चक्र ईड्यं चारु नाम विश्वानि देवो वयुनानि विद्वान | ससस्य चर्म घर्तवत पदं वेस्तदिदग्नी रक्षत्यप्रयुछन ||
3.5.e: The skilful God who knows all forms of knowledge made for himself a fair form, meet for worship.  This Agni guards with care that never ceases the Soma's skin, the Bird's place rich in fatness.

3.5.d: आ योनिमग्निर्घ्र्तवन्तमस्थात पर्थुप्रगाणमुशन्तमुशानः | दीद्यानः शुचिर्र्ष्वः पावकः पुनः-पुनर्मातरा नव्यसी कः ||
3.5.e: Agni hath entered longingly the longing shrine rich with fatness, giving easy access.  Resplendent, pure, sublime and purifying, again, again he renovates his Mothers.

3.5.d: सद्यो जात ओषधीभिर्ववक्षे यदी वर्धन्ति परस्वो घर्तेन | आप इव परवता शुम्भमाना उरुश्यदग्निः पित्रोरुपस्थे ||
3.5.e: Born suddenly, by plants he grew to greatness, when tender shoots with holy oil increased him,  Like waters lovely when they hasten downward may Agni in his Parents' lap protect us.

3.5.d: उदु षटुतः समिधा यह्वो अद्यौद वर्ष्मन दिवो अधि नाभा पर्थिव्याः | मित्रो अग्निरीड्यो मातरिश्वा दूतो वक्षद यजथाय देवान ||
3.5.e: Extolled, the Strong shone forth with kindled fuel to the earth's centre, to the height of heaven.  May Agni, Friend, adorable Mātariśvan, as envoy bring the Gods unto our worship.

3.5.d: उदस्तम्भीत समिधा नाकं रष्वो.अग्निर्भवन्नुत्तमो रोचनानाम | यदी भर्गुभ्यः परि मातरिश्वा गुहा सन्तं हव्यवाहं समीधे ||
3.5.e: Best of all luminaries lofty Agni supported with his flame the height of heaven,  When, far from Bhṛgus, Mātariśvan kindled the oblation-bearer where he lay in secret.
As holy food, Agni to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-word.

3.6.d: पर कारवो मनना वच्यमाना देवद्रीचीं नयत देवयन्तः | दक्षिणावाड वाजिनी पराच्येति हविर्भरन्त्यग्नये घर्ताची ||
3.6.e: URGED on by deep devotion, O ye singers, bring, pious ones, the God-approaching ladle.  Borne onward to the right it travels eastward, and, filled with oil, to Agni bears oblation.

3.6.d: आ रोदसी अप्र्णा जायमान उत पर रिक्था अध नु परयज्यो | दिवश्चिदग्ने महिना पर्थिव्या वच्यन्तां ते वह्नयः सप्तजिह्वाः ||
3.6.e: Thou at thy birth didst fill both earth and heaven, yea, Most Adorable, thou didst exceed them.  Even through the heaven's and through the earth's expanses let thy swift seventongued flames roll on, O Agni.

3.6.d: दयौश्च तवा पर्थिवी यज्ञियासो नि होतारं सादयन्ते दमाय | यदी विशो मानुषीर्देवयन्तीः परयस्वतीरीळते शुक्रमर्चिः ||
3.6.e: Both Heaven and Earth and Gods who should be worshipped establish thee as Priest for every dwelling,  Whenever human families, God-devoted, bringing oblations; laud thy splendid lustre.

3.6.d: महान सधस्थे धरुव आ निषत्तो.अन्तर्द्यावा माहिने हर्यमाणः | आस्क्रे सपत्नी अजरे अम्र्क्ते सबर्दुघे उरुगायस्यधेनू ||
3.6.e: Firm in the Gods’ home is the Mighty seated, between vast Heaven and Earth the well-beloved-  Those Cows who yield, unharmed, their nectar, Spouses of the Far-Strider, everyoung, united.

3.6.d: वरता ते अग्ने महतो महानि तव करत्वा रोदसी आ ततन्थ | तवं दूतो अभवो जायमानस्त्वं नेता वर्षभ चर्षणीनाम ||
3.6.e: Great are the deeds of thee, the Great, O Agni: thou by thy power hast spread out earth and heaven.  As soon as thou wast born thou wast an envoy, thou, Mighty One, was Leader of the people.

3.6.d: रतस्य वा केशिना योग्याभिर्घ्र्तस्नुवा रोहिता धुरि धिष्व | अथा वह देवान देव विश्वान सवध्वरा कर्णुहि जातवेदः ||
3.6.e: Bind to the pole with cords of holy Order the long-maned ruddy steeds who sprinkle fatness.  Bring hithier, O thou God, all Gods together: provide them noble worship, Jātavedas.

3.6.d: दिवश्चिदा ते रुचयन्ते रोका उषो विभातीरनु भासि पूर्वीः | अपो यदग्न उशधग वनेषु होतुर्मन्द्रस्य पनयन्त देवाः ||
3.6.e: Even from the sky thy brilliant lights shone hither: still hast thou beamed through many a radiant morning,  That the Gods praised their joyous Herald's labour eagerly burning, Agni, in the forests.

3.6.d: उरौ वा ये अन्तरिक्षे मदन्ति दिवो वा ये रोचने सन्ति देवाः | ऊमा वा ये सुहवासो यजत्रा आयेमिरे रथ्यो अग्ने अश्वाः ||
3.6.e: The Gods who take delight in air's wide region, or those the dwellers in heaven's realm of brightness,  Or those, the Holy, prompt to hear, our helpers, who, carborne, turn their horses hither, Agni—-

3.6.d: ऐभिरग्ने सरथं याह्यर्वां नानारथं वा विभवो हयश्वाः | पत्नीवतस्त्रिंशतं तरींश्च देवाननुष्वधमा वह मादयस्व ||
3.6.e: With these, borne on one ear, Agni, approach us, or borne on many, for thy steeds are able.  Bring, witb their Dames, the Gods, the Three and-Thirty, after thy Godlike nature, and be joyful.

3.6.d: स होता यस्य रोदसी चिदुर्वी यज्ञं-यज्ञमभि वर्धे गर्णीतः | पराची अध्वरेव तस्थतुः सुमेके रतावरी रतजातस्य सत्ये ||
3.6.e: He is the Priest at whose repeated worship even wide Heaven and Earth sing out for increase.  They fair and true and holy coming forward stand at his sacrifice who springs from Order.
As holy food, Agni, to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to usward.

3.7.d: पर य आरुः शितिप्र्ष्ठस्य धासेरा मातरा विविशुः सप्त वाणीः | परिक्षिता पितरा सं चरेते पर सर्स्राते दीर्घमायुः परयक्षे ||
3.7.e: THE seven tones risen from the whitebacked viand have made their way between the pair of Mothers.  Both circumjacent Parents come together to yield us length of days they hasten forward.

3.7.d: दिवक्षसो धेनवो वर्ष्णो अश्वा देवीरा तस्थौ मधुमद वहन्तीः | रतस्य तवा सदसि कषेमयन्तं पर्येका चरति वर्तनिं गौः ||
3.7.e: The Male who dwells in heaven hath Mares and Milchkine: he came to Goddesses who bring sweet treasure.  To thee safe resting in the seat of Order the Cow alone upon her way proceedeth.

3.7.d: आ सीमरोहत सुयमा भवन्तीः पतिश्चिकित्वान रयिविद रयीणाम | पर नीलप्र्ष्ठो अतसस्य धासेस्ता अवासयत पुरुधप्रतीकः ||
3.7.e: Wise Master, wealthy finder-out of riches, he mounted those who may with case be guided.  He, dark-backed, manifold with varied aspect, hath made them burst forth from their food the brush-wood.

3.7.d: महि तवाष्ट्रमूर्जयन्तीरजुर्यं सतभूयमानं वहतो वहन्ति | वयङगेभिर्दिद्युतानः सधस्थ एकामिव रोदसी आ विवेश ||
3.7.e: Strength-giving streams bear hither him eternal, fain to support the mighty work. of Tvaṣṭar.  He, flashing in his home with all his members, hath entered both the worlds as they were single.

3.7.d: जानन्ति वर्ष्णो अरुषस्य शेवमुत बरध्नस्य शासने रणन्ति | दिवोरुचः सुरुचो रोचमाना इळा येषां गण्या माहिना गीः ||
3.7.e: They know the red Bull's blessing, and are joyful under the flaming-coloured Lord's dominion:  They who give shine from heavenwith fair effulgence, whose lofty song like Iḷā must be honoured.

3.7.d: उतो पित्र्भ्यां परविदानु घोषं महो महद्भ्यामनयन्त शूषम | उक्षा ह यत्र परि धानमक्तोरनु सवं धाम जरितुर्ववक्ष ||
3.7.e: Yea, by tradition from the ancient sages they brought great strength from the two mighty Parents,  To where the singer's Bull, the night's dispeller, after his proper law hath waxen stronger.

3.7.d: अध्वर्युभिः पञ्चभिः सप्त विप्राः परियं रक्षन्ते निहितं पदं वेः | पराञ्चो मदन्त्युक्षणो अजुर्या देवा देवानामनु हि वरता गुः ||
3.7.e: Seven holy singers guard with five Adhvaryus the Bird's beloved firmly-settled station.  The willing Bulls, untouched by old, rejoice them: as Gods themselves the ways of Gods they follow.
I crave the grace of heaven's two chief Invokers: the seven swift steeds joy in their wonted manner.  These speak of truth, praising the Truth Eternal, thinking on Order as the guards of Order.

3.7.d: वर्षायन्ते महे अत्याय पूर्वीर्व्र्ष्णे चित्राय रश्मयः सुयामाः | देव होतर्मन्द्रतरश्चिकित्वान महो देवान रोदसी एह वक्षि ||
3.7.e: The many seek the great Steed as a stallion: the reins obey the Lord of varied colour.  O heavenly Priest, most pleasant, full of wisdom, bring the great Gods to us, and Earth and Heaven.

3.7.d: पर्क्षप्रयजो दरविणः सुवाचः सुकेतव उषसो रेवदूषुः | उतो चिदग्ने महिना पर्थिव्याः कर्तं चिदेनः सं महे दशस्य ||
3.7.e: Rich Lord, the Mornings have gleamed forth in splendour, fair-rayed, fair-speaking, worshipped with all viands,  Yea, with the glory of the earth, O Agni. Forgive us, for our weal, e’en sin cornmitted.
As holy food, Agni, to thine invoker, give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son, and spreading offspring Agni, be this thy gracious will to usward.

3.8.d: अञ्जन्ति तवामध्वरे देवयन्तो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन | यदूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा दरविणेह धत्ताद यद वा कषयो मातुरस्या उपस्थे ||
3.8.e: GOD-SERVING men, O Sovran of the Forest, with heavenly meath at sacrifice anoint thee.  Grant wealth to us when thou art standing upright as when reposing on this Mother's bosom.

3.8.d: समिद्धस्य शरयमाणः पुरस्ताद बरह्म वन्वानो अजरं सुवीरम | आरे अस्मदमतिं बाधमान उच्छ्रयस्व महते सौभगाय ||
3.8.e: Set up to eastward of the fire enkindled, accepting prayer that wastes not, rich in hero.  Driving far from us poverty and famine, lift thyself up to bring us great good fortune.

3.8.d: उच्छ्रयस्व वनस्पते वर्ष्मन पर्थिव्या अधि | सुमिती मीयमानो वर्चो धा यज्ञवाहसे ||
3.8.e: Lord of the Forest, raise. thyself up on the loftiest spot of earth.  Give splendour, fixt and measured well, to him who brings the sacrifice.

3.8.d: युवा सुवासाः परिवीत आगात स उ शरेयान भवति जायमानः | तं धीरासः कवय उन नयन्ति सवाध्यो मनसा देवयन्तः ||
3.8.e: Well-robed, enveloped he is come, the youthful: springing to life his glory waxeth greater.  Contemplative in mind and God-adoring, sages of high intelligence upraise him.

3.8.d: जातो जायते सुदिनत्वे अह्नां समर्य आ विदथे वर्धमानः | पुनन्ति धीरा अपसो मनीषा देवया विप्र उदियर्ति वाचम ||
3.8.e: Sprung up he rises in the days' fair weather, increasing in the men-frequented synod.  With song the wise and skilful consecrate him: his voice the God-adoring singer utters.  6, Ye whom religious men have firmly planted; thou Forest Sovran whom the axe hath fashioned,—  Let those the Stakes divine which here are standing be fain to grant us wealth with store of children.

3.8.d: यान वो नरो देवयन्तो निमिम्युर्वनस्पते सवधितिर्वा ततक्ष | ते देवासः सवरवस्तस्थिवांसः परजावदस्मे दिधिषन्तु रत्नम ||
3.8.e: O men who lift the ladles up, these hewn and planted in the ground,  Bringing a blessing to the field, shall bear our precious gift to Gods.

3.8.d: ये वर्क्णासो अधि कषमि निमितासो यतस्रुचः | ते नो वयन्तु वार्यं देवत्रा कषेत्रसाधसः ||
3.8.e: Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, careful leaders, Earth, Heaven, and Prthivi and Air's mid-region,  Accordant Deities shall bless our worship and make our sacrifice's ensign lofty.

3.8.d: आदित्या रुद्रा वसवः सुनीथा दयावाक्षामा पर्थिवी अन्तरिक्षम | सजोषसो यज्ञमवन्तु देवा ऊर्ध्वं कर्ण्वन्त्वध्वरस्य केतुम ||
3.8.e: Like swan's that flee in lengthened line, the Pillars have come to us arrayed in brilliant coIour.  They, lifted up on high, by sages, eastward, go forth as Gods to the God's dwelling-places.

3.8.d: हंसा इव शरेणिशो यतानाः शुक्रा वसानाः सवरवो नागुः | उन्नीयमानाः कविभिः पुरस्ताद देवा देवानामपि यन्ति पाथः ||
3.8.e: Those Stakes upon the earth with rings that deck them seem to the eye like horns of horned creatures;  Or, as upraised by priests in invocation, let them assist us in the rush to battle.

3.8.d: शर्ङगाणीवेच्छ्र्ङगिणां सं दद्र्श्रे चषालवन्तः सवरवः पर्थिव्याम | वाघद्भिर्वा विहवे शरोषमाणा अस्मानवन्तु पर्तनाज्येषु ||
3.8.e: Lord of the Wood, rise with a hundred branches. with thousand branches may we rise to greatness,  Tlou whom this hatchct, with an edge well whetted for great felicity, hath brought before us.

3.8.d: वनस्पते शतवल्शो वि रोह सहस्रवल्शा वि वयं रुहेम | यं तवामयं सवधितिस्तेजमानः परणिनाय महते सौभगाय ||

3.9.d: सखायस्त्वा वव्र्महे देवं मर्तास ऊतये | अपां नपातंसुभगं सुदीदितिं सुप्रतूर्तिमनेहसम ||
3.9.e: WE as thy friends have chosen thee, mortals a God, to be our help,  The Waters’ Child, the blessed, the resplendent One, victorious and beyond compare.

3.9.d: कायमानो वना तवं यन मातॄरजगन्नपः | न तत तेग्ने परम्र्षे निवर्तनं यद दूरे सन्निहाभवः ||
3.9.e: Since thou delighting in the woods hast gone unto thy mother streams,  Not to be scorned, Agni, is that return of thine when from afar thou now art here.

3.9.d: अति तर्ष्टं ववक्षिथाथैव सुमना असि | पर-परान्ये यन्ति पर्यन्य आसते येषां सख्ये असि शरितः ||
3.9.e: O'er pungent smoke host thou prevailed, and thus art thou benevolent.  Some go before, and others round about thee sit, they in whose friendship thou hast place.

3.9.d: ईयिवांसमति सरिधः शश्वतीरति सश्चतः | अन्वीमविन्दन निचिरासो अद्रुहो.अप्सु सिंहमिव शरितम ||
3.9.e: Him who had passed beyond his foes, beyond continual pursuits, Him the unerring Ones, observant, found in floods, couched like a lion in his lair.

3.9.d: सस्र्वांसमिव तमनाग्निमित्था तिरोहितम | ऐनं नयन मातरिश्वा परावतो देवेभ्यो मथितं परि ||
3.9.e: Him wandering at his own free will, Agni here hidden from our view,  Him Mātariśvan brought to us from far away produced by friction, from the Gods.

3.9.d: तं तवा मर्ता अग्र्भ्णत देवेभ्यो हव्यवाहन | विश्वान यद्यज्ञानभिपासि मानुष तव करत्वा यविष्ठ्य ||
3.9.e: O Bearer of Oblations, thus mortals received thee from the Gods,  Whilst thou, the Friend of man, guardest each sacrifice with thine own power, Most Youthful One.

3.9.d: तद भद्रं तव दंसना पाकाय चिच्छदयति | तवां यदग्ने पशवः समासते समिद्धमपिशर्वरे ||
3.9.e: Amid thy wonders this is good, yea, to the simple is it clear,  When gathered round about thee, Agni, lie the herds where thou art kindled in the morn.

3.9.d: आ जुहोता सवध्वरं शीरं पावकशोचिषम | आशुं दूतमजिरं परत्नमीड्यं शरुष्टी देवं सपर्यत ||
3.9.e: Offer to him who knows fair rites, who burns with purifying glow,  Swift envoy, active, ancient, and adorable: serve ye the God attentively.

3.9.d: तरीणि शता तरी सहस्राण्यग्निं तरिंशच्च देवा नवचासपर्यन | औक्षन घर्तैरस्त्र्णन बर्हिरस्मा आदिद धोतारं नयसादयन्त ||
3.9.e: Three times a hundred Gods and thrice a thousand, and three times ten and nine have worshipped Agni,  For him spread sacred grass, with oil bedewed him, and stablished him as Priest and Sacrificer.

3.10.d: तवामग्ने मनीषिणः सम्राजं चर्षणीनाम | देवं मर्तास इन्धते समध्वरे ||
3.10.e: THEE Agni, God, Imperial Lord of all mankind, do mortal men  With understanding kindle at the sacrifice.

3.10.d: तवां यज्ञेष्व रत्विजमग्ने होतारमीळते | गोपा रतस्य दीदिहि सवे दमे ||
3.10.e: They laud thee in their solemn rites, Agni, as Minister and Priest,  Shine forth in thine own home as guardian of the Law.

3.10.d: स घा यस्ते ददाशति समिधा जातवेदसे | सो अग्ने धत्तेसुवीर्यं स पुष्यति ||
3.10.e: He, verily, who honours thee with fuel, Knower of all life,  He, Agni! wins heroic might, he prospers well.

3.10.d: स केतुरध्वराणामग्निर्देवेभिरा गमत | अञ्जानः सप्त होत्र्भिर्हविष्मते ||
3.10.e: Ensign of sacrifices, he, Agni, with Gods is come to us,  Decked by the seven priests, to him who bringeth gifts.

3.10.d: पर होत्रे पूर्व्यं वचो.अग्नये भरता बर्हत | विपां जयोतींषि बिभ्रते न वेधसे ||
3.10.e: To Agni, the Invoking Priest, offer your best, your lofty speech,  To him Ordainer-like who brings the light of songs.

3.10.d: अग्निं वर्धन्तु नो गिरो यतो जायत उक्थ्यः | महे वाजायद्रविणाय दर्शतः ||
3.10.e: Let these our hymns make Agni grow, whence, meet for laud, he springs to life,  To mighty strength and great possession, fair to see.

3.10.d: अग्ने यजिष्ठो अध्वरे देवान देवयते यज | होता मन्द्रो विराजस्यति सरिधः ||
3.10.e: Best Sacrificer, bring the Gods, O Agni, to the pious man:  A joyful Priest, thy splendour drive our foes afar

3.10.d: स नः पावक दीदिहि दयुमदस्मे सुवीर्यम | भवा सतोत्र्भ्योन्तमः सवस्तये ||
3.10.e: As such, O Purifier, shine on us heroic glorious might:  Be nearest Friend to those who laud thee, for their weal.

3.10.d: तं तवा विप्रा विपन्यवो जाग्र्वांसः समिन्धते | हव्यवाहममर्त्यं सहोव्र्धम ||
3.10.e: So, wakeful, versed in sacred hymns, the holy singers kindly thee.  Oblation-bearer, deathless, cherisher of strength.

3.11.d: अग्निर्होता पुरोहितो.अध्वरस्य विचर्षणिः | स वेद यज्ञमानुषक ||
3.11.e: AGNI is Priest, the great High Priest of sacrifice, most swift in act:  He knows the rite in constant course.

3.11.d: स हव्यवाळ अमर्त्य उशिग दूतस चनोहितः | अग्निर्धिया सं रण्वति ||
3.11.e: Oblation-bearer, deathless, well inclined, an eager messenger,  Agni comes nigh us with the thought.

3.11.d: अग्निर्धिया स चेतति केतुर्यज्ञस्य पूर्व्यः | अर्थं हयस्य तरणि ||
3.11.e: Ensign of sacrifice from of old, Agni well knoweth with his thought  To prosper this man's aim and hope.

3.11.d: अग्निं सूनुं सनश्रुतं सहसो जातवेदसम | वह्निं देवाक्र्ण्वत ||
3.11.e: Agni, illustrious from old time, the Son of Strength who knows all life,  The Gods have made to their Priest.

3.11.d: अदाभ्यः पुरेता विशामग्निर्मानुषीणाम | तूर्णी रथः सदा नवः ||
3.11.e: Infallible is Agni, he who goes before the tribes of men,  A chariot swift and ever new.
Strength of the Gods which none may harm, subduing all his enemies,  Agni is mightiest in fame.

3.11.d: अभि परयांसि वाहसा दाश्वानश्नोति मर्त्यः | कषयं पावकशोचिषः ||
3.11.e: By offering sacred food to him the mortal worshipper obtains.  A home from him whose light makes pure.

3.11.d: परि विश्वानि सुधिताग्नेरश्याम मन्मभिः | विप्रासो जातवेदसः ||
3.11.e: From Agni, by our hymns, may we gain all things that bring happiness,  Singers of him who knows all life.

3.11.d: अग्ने विश्वानि वार्या वाजेषु सनिषामहे | तवे देवास एरिरे ||
3.11.e: O Agni, in our deeds of might may we obtain all precious things:  Tle Gods are centred all in thee.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी आ गतं सुतं गीर्भिर्नभो वरेण्यम | अस्य पातं धियेषिता ||
3.12.e: MOVED, Indra-Agni, by our hymn, come to the juice, the precious dew:  Drink ye thereof, impelled by song.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी जरितुः सचा यज्ञो जिगाति चेतनः | अया पातमिमं सुतम ||
3.12.e: O Indra-Agni, with the man who lauds you comes the wakening rite:  So drink ye both this juice assured.

3.12.d: इन्द्रमग्निं कविछदा यज्ञस्य जूत्या वर्णे | ता सोमस्येह तर्म्पताम ||
3.12.e: Through force of sacrifice I choose Indra-Agni who love the wise:  With Soma let these sate them here.

3.12.d: तोशा वर्त्रहणा हुवे सजित्वानापराजिता | इन्द्राग्नी वाजसातमा ||
3.12.e: Indra and Agni I invoke, joint-victors, bounteous, unsubdued,  Foe-slayers, best to win the spoil.

3.12.d: पर वामर्चन्त्युक्थिनो नीथाविदो जरितारः | इन्द्राग्नी इष आ वर्णे ||
3.12.e: Indra and Agni, singers skilled in melody hymn you, bringing lauds:  I choose you for the sacred food.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी नवतिं पुरो दासपत्नीरधूनुतम | साकमेकेन कर्मणा ||
3.12.e: Indra and Agni, ye cast down the ninety forts which Dāsas held,  Together, with one mighty deed.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी अपसस पर्युप पर यन्ति धीतयः | रतस्य पथ्या अनु ||
3.12.e: To Indra-Agni reverent thoughts go forward from the holy task  Along the path of sacred Law.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी तविषाणि वां सधस्थानि परयांसि च | युवोरप्तूर्यं हितम ||
3.12.e: O Indra-Agni, powers are yours, and dwellings and delightful food  Good is your readiness to act.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी रोचना दिवः परि वाजेषु भूषथः | तद वांचेति पर वीर्यम ||
3.12.e: Indra and Agni, in your deeds of might ye deck heaven's lucid realms:  Famed is that hero strength of yours.

3.13.d: पर वो देवायाग्नये बर्हिष्ठमर्चास्मै | गमद देवेभिरास नो यजिष्ठो बर्हिरा सदत ||
3.13.e: To Agni, to this God of yours I sing aloud with utmost power.  May he come to us with the Gods, and sit, best Offerer, on the grass.

3.13.d: रतावा यस्य रोदसी दक्षं सचन्त ऊतयः | हविष्मन्तस्तमीळते तं सनिष्यन्तो.अवसे ||
3.13.e: The Holy, whose are earth and heaven, and succour waits upon his strength;  Him men who bring oblations laud, and they who wish to gain, for grace.

3.13.d: स यन्ता विप्र एषां स यज्ञानामथा हि षः | अग्निं तं वो दुवस्यत दाता यो वनिता मघम ||
3.13.e: He is the Sage who guides these men, Leader of sacred rites is he.  Him your own Agni, serve ye well, who winneth and bestoweth wealth.

3.13.d: स नः शर्माणि वीतये.अग्निर्यछतु शन्तमा | यतो नःप्रुष्णवद वसु दिवि कषितिभ्यो अप्स्वा ||
3.13.e: So may the gracious Agni grant most goodly shelter for our use;  Whence in the heavens or in the floods he shall pour wealth upon our lands.
